events.title: Analyzing the Issues That Motivate Voters | Communities United
events.description:
Many factors can __motivate people to participate in elections.__ Some of the most common reasons include a desire to have their voices heard, a belief that their vote can make a difference, a sense of civic duty, a disposition about political issues (personal values), or a desire to support a particular candidate or party.

With the __midterm and national elections__ happening every year, and __state primary and special elections__ happening nearly every month, we will analyze-discuss not only _how_ will Americans vote, but also _why_ they are planning to vote that way.

The new national polls that examine the electorate in an effort to understand what exactly is motivating voters to vote will be reviewed. The studies of both Democratic likely voters and Republican likely voters reveal that voters are animated by either party values or economic issues.  The question is whether state and national elections are determined by either of the major parties or by a larger majority of Independent voters.

Those are the broad overviews, but the devil in the details is always the voter turnout. At the end of the day, in this case, Election Day, the key is __motivating voters to cast their ballots.__  Voter turnout is essential, if not the most important, key to winning an election. 

The __"Analyze the Issues that Motivate Voters"__ event program _requires_ advance preparation-knowledge and is intended for voters with voter registration knowlege-experiences.  This event program is not a basic voter registration presentation.

*** NEW ***

Q: Are you prepared to Motivate Registered Voters? ... (review upon registration confirmation)

Review "National Voter Education-Registration-Empowerment Year of Action" [(mobilization)](www.mobilize.us/2020victorious/event/580830/) and _all referenced links._

The 2024 Election season will include innovative community-based organizing with a national program platform to engage networks in local-regional-state-national communities to educate-register-mobilize voters for state-by-state 'down-ballot' and primary-presidential elections, and to reclaim the U.S. House of Representatives, expand the U.S. Senate, and secure the White House for the democracy we deserve.

This program is a practical-functional skills training in community outreach and having persuasive conversations with colleagues-neighbors, family-friends and community networks, using relational organizing and community outreach to motivate all voters (frequent-infrequent) — we are excited to start organizing together!

- - - - -

- - - - -

160 million Americans cast their ballots in 2020 – shattering voter turnout records and making history.  And we can’t stop now.  There is still work to be done before we are #VoteReady!

ELECTION PROTECTION HOTLINE: Call or Text 866-OUR-VOTE * Tweet @866OURVOTE

events.description:
**HELLO VOLUNTEERS!**

At Feed Louisville, we often say that volunteers are the backbone of our organization. With help from people like you, we sent out 142,979 meals in 2024 to the houseless and food-insecure community. Join us in the kitchen to help our team turn donated food into nutritious meals! From prepping vegetables, making sandwiches, packaging meals, and much more, there is plenty to help with!

### SHIFTS: 
There are two volunteer time slots to choose from Monday-Friday: 

**9 am to 12 pm and/or 1 pm to 3:30 pm.**
If you need to come a little late or leave a little early, no problem at all. _Sign up for the shift your schedule best aligns with._
**Each volunteer must register for their own shift.**

### DRESS GUIDELINES:
When volunteering in our kitchen, we ask you to dress comfortably and appropriately! Here are a few key points to remember:

- Volunteers must wear a **hair covering** such as a hat, hair net, or bandana. 

- Long hair must be tied up and covered. We provide hair nets.

- Volunteers must wear closed-toe shoes.

- Volunteers must have their shoulders, abdomen, and armpits covered.   

- Short-sleeve or long-sleeve shirts only, no crop-tops permitted.

- Volunteers with artificial nails and/or nail polish must wear gloves (will be provided) when handling any Ready-To-Eat or raw food.

### SAFETY AND AGE REQUIREMENTS:
For safety reasons, we **do not allow persons under 10 years of age** to volunteer in our kitchen. 

- Volunteers between 10 to 14 years old must be accompanied by an adult and will be assigned to non-kitchen tasks. 

- Those 14 to 18 years old may be allowed to use knives or work around industrial kitchen equipment, depending on their experience level. 

- Anyone 18 years and older can work in our production kitchen.

**GROUPS:** If you want to bring a group of 10 or more, please email volunteer@feedlouisville.org so we can work with you to schedule a date that works best!

### LOCATION:
Our kitchen is at 1334 Story Avenue Louisville, KY. Please read these directions before coming to volunteer!

[How to get to our kitchen](https://youtu.be/35OON5TVOY0)

If driving on Story Ave, the entrance to our parking lot is directly across from the Whirling Tiger, at the corner of Webster and Story. Enter through the open black gates on your left, drive until you come to the T in the road, then turn right. Drive towards the yellow dumpster at the end and enter our parking lot surrounded by a chain link fence. 

If driving on North Spring Street, take a left at the Louisville Division Fire Station 3 and keep driving straight to the yellow dumpster and chain link fenced area. 

After parking, walk towards the building and up the wooden stairs. Continue until you see a door that says "Social Events and Feed Louisville". Once inside, walk towards the double doors and turn right. Go through the white doors and around the bend to the volunteer station!

If you have trouble finding us, please call or text us at 502-418-7443 and we will gladly guide you in the right direction!

### THANK YOU!
We are grateful for your willingness to help us in our mission to rescue more food and put it into the hands of the houseless and food-insecure in Louisville. If you cannot make it to our kitchen, consider sharing our story and the work of our community partners on social media, or consider donating to increase the number of people we can feed!

Looking forward to meeting you,
Caitlyn Morgan
Expo and Volunteer Coordinator

Reach out to volunteer@feedlouisville.org with any questions!

events.title: Hennepin County Court Watch
events.description:
Court watching is a tactic to raise public awareness about our legal system and to hold the system accountable through witnessing, documenting, and sharing experiences at bail hearings. This is a powerful and critical tool for organizing because so much harm is never witnessed and goes unchecked. Court watching is a tool of PEOPLE POWER against those in power. 

MN Freedom Funds court watching is a volunteer-based program aimed at shining a light on Ramsey County and Hennepin County Arraignment hearings. This is where money bail decisions are made and ultimately, people's access to pretrial freedom is determined.​

Hennepin County Court Watch Shifts are every 1st Thursday and every 2nd Monday of the month at 1:30 pm. 

Ramsey County Court Watch Shifts every 4th Monday of the month at 9:00am

*These dates are subject to change*

events.title: Day of Action: Lehigh Acres
events.description:
### Are you passionate about democracy and making a change in your community?
Join us for a Day of Action in Lehigh Acres! We will be hitting the streets to connect with voters who are at risk of being dropped from the voter rolls and to encourage vote-by-mail enrollment. Our newly developed Deep Canvassing technique is a powerful way to impact our community and ensure every voice is heard directly. Whether you're a seasoned canvasser or new to the process, we will provide you with on the spot training to ensure you're equipped for the task. Let's work together to build a
better future for Lee County and beyond. Join us, and let's make a difference!

*What to bring: Charged cell phone, bottled water, comfortable shoes, a hat, and sunscreen.*

**Event details: **
1. Meet in the parking lot of the East Branch of Lee County Public Library, 881 Gunnery Road,
Lehigh Acres.
2. Become part of a Deep Canvassing team, working with an experienced Deep Canvasser.
3. Upload your assigned MiniVAN turf (approx 20 doors). Grab your Deep Canvass clipboard, pens,
and door hanger letters.
4. Hit the road with your canvassing team.
5. Return to the library, return unused materials, and wrap up findings.

events.description:
# Seattle Indivisible's Bimonthly Call with Rep. Adam Smith's Staff

Join us for **Seattle Indivisible's bimonthly call** with Rep. Adam Smith's staff! This is your opportunity to engage directly with congressional staff on the most pressing issues facing our nation today.

## Key Issues in 2025

We are navigating a complex political landscape marked by significant challenges, including:

- **Constitutional Concerns**  
  Recent actions by the administration, such as the dismantling of longstanding government programs and the centralization of power, have raised serious questions about the erosion of democratic principles.

- **Economic Uncertainty**  
  The imposition of a federal spending freeze has led to confusion and legal challenges, impacting various programs and contributing to fiscal instability.

- **Social Equity**  
  Proposed policies affecting marginalized communities, including restrictions on transgender rights and potential cuts to social safety nets, underscore the ongoing struggle for social justice.

## 📢 Submit Your Question

Have a question or concern? **Submit your question** for the call through the link below:

➡️ [**Submit Your Question Here**](https://forms.gle/7TyAiLi5mnwznthH8)

We look forward to your participation in this vital discussion!

events.title: PA: Attend Allegheny County Board of Health Meetings!

location.venue: Allegheny County Courthouse Gold Room, Room 410 (4th floor)

events.description:
**Join us at the next Allegheny County Board of Health (BOH) meeting to demand that all new fracking be prohibited in Allegheny County.** 

It can no longer be denied: Fracking can't be done without threatening human health and climate stability. Just as recently as 2023, a state-funded health study in southwest PA found that fracking correlates with increased rates of asthma and low birth weight, as well as sharply elevated risk of childhood lymphoma _(5-7 times the national average)_.

Per the Pennsylvania Disease and Prevention Control Act of 1955, "Local boards and departments of health shall be primarily responsible for the prevention and control of communicable and non-communicable disease... in accordance with the regulations of the board and subject to the supervision and guidance of the department." *This means that the Allegheny County BOH is responsible for and has the power to enact policy to prevent the incredibly harmful effects of fracking!*

**RSVP to receive details and reminders, as well as talking points for submitting in-person and written comments.** See you there!

**_The BOH requires speakers to sign up at least 24 hours prior to the meeting. Please make sure to sign up by 12:00pm ET the day before the scheduled meeting_**

events.title: PPT & T4APA! Communications Committee
events.description:
## Join PPT for our Art Build on 10/17! We'll be making signs and beautiful art for the PRESS CONFERENCE PARADE we're holding on 10/20 [RSVP FOR THE PRESS CONFERENCE HERE](https://www.mobilize.us/ppt/event/855939/)

Building the narrative of Transit Justice in our community is a critical part of our work. The Communications Committee hosts monthly virtual working meetings to tell the story of PPT’s campaigns, successes, and struggles. During these meetings, attendees help produce content that communicates our work to the public— including writing blogs, editing videos, creating content for our social media channels, curating photography, and doing graphic design.

Since 2025, the Communications Committee has been a joint space for members of Pittsburghers for Public Transit and supporters of [Transit for All PA!](https://www.transitforallpa.org/), the statewide transit campaign that we lead. Supporters of both organizations are welcome at these meetings, and we may work on projects relevant to Allegheny County or elsewhere in Pennsylvania.

### You might be a good fit for the Communications Committee if...
- You love writing and/or social media content creation
- You have experience with photography, graphic design, or web design

**Note:** Communications Committee meetings often involve working closely with documents on Google Docs or sourced from the internet, looking at photographs or video online, or creating content using the online image creation tool Canva. Please keep this in mind if that might pose an accessibility challenge for you.
events.accessibility_notes: ASL and Spanish interpretation is available on request, butmust be booked in advance. events.title: PPT & T4APA! Research Committee
events.description:
The Research Committee is the brain of PPT’s policy work, hosting weekly working meetings to conduct data and policy research in support of our campaigns. During these meetings, attendees analyze data, investigate policies active in other cities, and assemble reports that recommend action that can improve our transit system. [Check out the Research Committee’s past work](https://www.pittsburghforpublictransit.org/research-and-resources/) to see the types of projects you might collaborate on as part of the Research Committee.

Since 2025, the Research Committee has been a joint space for members of Pittsburghers for Public Transit and supporters of [Transit for All PA!](https://www.transitforallpa.org/), the statewide transit campaign that we lead. Supporters of both organizations are welcome at these meetings, and we may work on projects relevant to Allegheny County or elsewhere in Pennsylvania.

### You might be a good fit for the Research Committee if...
- You have a knack for crunching numbers
- You consider yourself a policy wonk
- You love chasing research topics down a rabbit hole
- You have an academic or professional background in data, research or planning (although none is required to join the committee!)

**Note:** Research committee meetings often involve working closely with documents, on Google Docs or sourced from the internet. Please keep this in mind if that might pose an accessibility challenge for you.

events.title: Court Watch PGH for Youth Justice: Decertifications

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Decertification Hearings in Allegheny County

A decertification hearing is a legal proceeding that allows the court to determine whether a young person charged as an adult should instead have their case transferred to juvenile court. In Pennsylvania, youth ages 14 and older charged with certain serious offenses are automatically charged as adults, but they may request a decertification hearing to challenge that status.

The court considers several factors during a decertification hearing, including: the youth’s age and maturity, prior juvenile record, amenability to rehabilitation within the juvenile system, and the nature and circumstances of the offense. 

If the court grants decertification, the case is reassigned to juvenile court, where the focus shifts from punishment to rehabilitation and age-appropriate accountability. Unlike IOJ hearings, which assess the conditions and location of detention, decertification hearings are about jurisdiction—deciding whether the case belongs in adult or juvenile court.

These hearings are crucial opportunities to protect youth from the lifelong consequences of adult prosecution and incarceration.

Court Watch with us!

events.title: VA Youth Gun Violence Prevention Advocacy Training Info Session (For Young People Under 26)
events.description:
The only national, youth-led initiative training young people to meet with lawmakers and advocate for urgently needed gun reform.
The Team ENOUGH Youth Advocacy Training Program, formerly known as the Team ENOUGH Lobbying Collective, educates and mobilizes young people, ages 13-26, to be advocates for gun violence prevention legislation in their own communities.

Led by National Coordinators Elizabeth Paul and Felix Hedberg, we are recruiting young people in Virginia to join our Youth Advocacy Training Program. Program members will attend a series of webinars and trainings where they meet with policy experts to hear more about the bills being considered in their community and become equipped with the skills they need to have impactful conversations with lawmakers. 

After attending training, program members will be accompanied by experienced advocates as they meet directly with lawmakers to advance priorities in the movement to end gun violence. With gun violence being the leading cause of death for young people in America, it’s imperative that our leaders hear directly from us on this issue. 

Each week throughout our application period we are hosting these informational calls so you can learn more about the Youth Advocacy Training Program, ask questions about the program and see if you would like to apply. 

You can learn more about the program and apply at https://www.bradyunited.org/take-action/join-movement/team-enough/youth-advocacy-training-program

location.venue: Raymond O. Shelton School Administrative Center

events.description:
You're Invited! Join Families for Strong Public Schools in Advocating for Students!

Local school boards play a critical role in shaping the future of our schools, making key decisions on funding, curriculum, and other policies that directly impact our children’s education.

As activism for diverse, historically accurate education grows, Families for Strong Public Schools is expanding its School Board Monitoring Program across the state. This initiative empowers volunteers to attend school board meetings, monitor decisions, and submit monthly reports on critical issues, including:

Budget allocation and funding priorities
Curriculum and educational policies
Community engagement and transparency

We need passionate advocates like you to ensure that decisions are being made in the best interest of students, families, and public education.

Why Get Involved?

By attending meetings, you can:

Speak up on behalf of students and families.
Monitor discussions to ensure funding and curriculum decisions align with the needs of all students.
Advocate for transparency, equity, and strong public schools.

Your voice matters. Together, we can ensure that every decision made at the board level reflects the values and priorities of our community. 

Let’s build a brighter future for our students—one meeting at a time!

—--------------**Español abajo** —--------------

We’re organizing to build a better future. Will you join us? 

**On the 4th Thursday of every month,** Moms, parents, caregivers, and families from across the nation are gathering virtually for our MomsRising Monthly Community Meetings. Each month, we’ll dive into a different topic, hear from special guest experts, leaders, and advocates, celebrate victories and hope, get informed, get organized, and take action.

This moment is all-hands-on-deck. We need everyone to come together, get informed, and take meaningful steps to protect our communities, our institutions, and our economy. These gatherings are about more than just updates—they’re about building power, community, and hope. Because when we come together, we are powerful.

**Let’s rise together—RSVP now to join us! You can even sign up for multiple months at a time by checking multiple dates.**

Please share this with everyone you know who is ready to take action and build power for the times ahead and ask them to join the meeting too!

Together, we can create a brighter, more hopeful future. 

**This event will be conducted in English, with simultaneous translation available in Spanish.**

—--------------**Español** —--------------

Estamos organizándonos para construir un futuro mejor. ¿Puedes ayudarnos? 

**El cuarto jueves de cada mes,** mamás, padres de familia, proveedores de cuidados y familias de toda la nación se reunirán virtualmente en las reuniones comunitarias mensuales de MomsRising/MamásConPoder. Cada mes exploraremos un tema distinto; escucharemos a invitados especiales expertos, a líderes y a defensores; celebraremos las victorias y la esperanza, nos informaremos, organizaremos y entraremos en acción.

Es hora de que todos nos pongamos manos a la obra. Necesitamos que todos se unan, informen y den pasos significativos para proteger a nuestras comunidades, a nuestras instituciones y a nuestra economía. Estas reuniones son para más que compartir información, son para fortalecer el poder, la comunidad y la esperanza. Porque cuando nos unimos somos poderosos.

**Levantémonos juntos. ¡Confirma tu asistencia ahora para acompañarnos! Incluso te puedes inscribir para participar varios meses seleccionando varias fechas.**

¡Por favor comparte esto con todas las personas que conozcas que estén listas para entrar en acción y para fortalecer el poder para los tiempos difíciles que tenemos por delante y pídeles que también asistan a la reunión!

Juntos podemos crear un futuro más brillante y optimista. 

**Este evento se realizará en inglés y tendremos disponible interpretación simultánea en español.**

events.title: RuCo Action Monthly Meetings 2025
events.description:
Join us for our monthly meetings where we plan ways to engage with our community to fight for reproductive justice! We have a lot of work to do in 2025 and we want you to join us in the fight! Come out and learn how you can help.

RuCo Action is a Planned Parenthood Action Council that works to build power in our local community by advocating for reproductive justice, sexual healthcare access, and bodily autonomy. We aim to mobilize Rutherford County residents by organizing educational opportunities, training programs, advocacy initiatives, and community building opportunities.

Together, we can activate supporters of social justice in Rutherford County and beyond to build real change. United, we can break the decade-old Tennessee Supermajority and show Tennesseans that we are not a red state, but a gerrymandered state with low voter turnout and civic engagement. By engaging the Rising American Electorate - youth, women, POC, and LGBTQ individuals - we can unlock the power we need to end this gridlock and vote in bold unapologetic leaders who will fight for the rights of all Tennesseans and future generations.

All are welcome at RuCo Action events. If you have any questions, please reach out to us on Instagram or Facebook - @ruco_action or facebook.com/RuCoActionCouncil

events.title: ICM Advocacy Committee Meeting
events.description:
**Join ICM’s Advocacy Committee – Where Your Voice Shapes a Better Future for Children!**

Are you passionate about creating real change for children in Georgia? Do you believe in the power of advocacy to drive policies that protect and uplift young lives? Then the **Interfaith Children’s Movement Advocacy Committee** is where you belong!

**What We Do:**  
Our Advocacy Committee is a dynamic, solutions-driven group of members, lay leaders, and leaders of different faith communities and congregations, advocates, and changemakers dedicated to prioritizing the well-being of children and families in Georgia. Each month, we strategize, collaborate, and take action to ensure every child has the opportunity to thrive.

**When We Meet:**  
Join us every 4th Thursday of the month from 6:30-7:30 p.m. (usually on Zoom, with a few exceptions throughout the year) to brainstorm, plan, and execute advocacy efforts that make a tangible difference. These meetings are lively, inspiring, and full of opportunities to make an impact.

**Why You Should Join:**  
- Be at the forefront of meaningful advocacy efforts.  
- Connect with a diverse, passionate community committed to justice and equity for children.  
- Turn your ideas into action, from crafting advocacy campaigns to engaging directly with policymakers.  
- Be a voice for children who need champions like you.

**Get Involved Today!**  
Your ideas and energy are the missing piece to our movement. Together, we’ll build a brighter future for Georgia’s children. Sign up now to attend our next meeting and be part of the change!

**Make your voice heard – because children can’t wait!**  

Ready to take action? Join the Advocacy Committee today!

events.title: ICM Grow the Movement (GTM) Committee Meeting
events.description:
### Join the Grow the Movement (GTM) Committee  

Are you ready to make a tangible impact on the lives of children in Georgia? The Interfaith Children’s Movement’s *Grow the Movement (GTM) Committee* is seeking passionate individuals to help connect faith communities across the state and advocate for children’s well-being.  

**What We Do:**  
The GTM Committee works to build county-based interfaith coalitions, uniting people of faith to champion the needs of children in their local communities. Our ultimate goal is to have coalitions in all 159 counties, creating a statewide network of advocates ensuring every child has someone fighting for their future.  

**Why Join?**  
- Be part of a team committed to meaningful, community-driven change.  
- Collaborate with others to expand our reach and influence.  
- Help create a sustainable framework for advocacy at the local level.  

The committee meets monthly to strategize, share ideas, and mobilize action. Together, we can amplify the voice of faith communities and ensure that no child in Georgia is left without a dedicated advocate.  

*Sign up for the next meeting and join the movement to make every child a priority.*

events.title: Team ENOUGH Welcome Session (For Young People Under 26)
events.description:
Are you a young person between 13 and 25 years old who is interested in taking action around preventing gun violence? Join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session to learn more about the different ways you can engage.

Team ENOUGH is a youth-led program whose mission is to educate young voices about gun violence and mobilize them to take meaningful action against it. Supported by Brady United, we harness the expertise and experience of today’s youth to advance our intersectional work across the country.

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

For us, preventing gun violence not only requires regulating access to firearms but also addressing how systemic racism and environmental factors cause this form of bloodshed to run especially rampant in communities of color. You cannot talk about gun violence without talking about police brutality, white supremacy, the broken criminal justice system, poverty, homophobia, access to affordable housing, or the often barriers separating disadvantaged populations from physical and mental healthcare.

So if you share this belief, join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session and become part of the movement to end gun violence in our lifetime.

events.title: Stop Microplastics Now! Campaign Meeting
events.description:
**Food & Water Action has launched a new campaign against microplastics, the tiny plastic particles that are now pervasive in our food and water.**

Last year, we filed a legal petition with the EPA urging the agency to monitor microplastics as a water contaminant. Our Stop Microplastics Now! Campaign aims to force the agency to act by getting state governors to join our petition. This is an important way to for state leaders to force the federal government to protect our water. 

On this campaign action call, we will dig deeper into the steps we can take to ensure seven governors join our petition to force the EPA to act. **Join us to learn what you can do in your community to make a big impact nationwide on protecting our drinking water!**

events.description:
The only national, youth-led initiative training young people to meet with lawmakers and advocate for urgently needed gun reform.
The Team ENOUGH Youth Advocacy Training Program, formerly known as the Team ENOUGH Lobbying Collective, educates and mobilizes young people, ages 13-26, to be advocates for gun violence prevention legislation in their own communities.

Led by National Coordinators Elizabeth Paul and Felix Hedberg, we are recruiting young people in FL to join our Youth Advocacy Training Program. Program members will attend a series of webinars and trainings where they meet with policy experts to hear more about the bills being considered in their community and become equipped with the skills they need to have impactful conversations with lawmakers. 

After attending training, program members will be accompanied by experienced advocates as they meet directly with lawmakers to advance priorities in the movement to end gun violence. With gun violence being the leading cause of death for young people in America, it’s imperative that our leaders hear directly from us on this issue. 

Each week throughout our application period we are hosting these informational calls so you can learn more about the Youth Advocacy Training Program, ask questions about the program and see if you would like to apply. 

You can learn more about the program and apply at https://www.bradyunited.org/take-action/join-movement/team-enough/youth-advocacy-training-program

Team ENOUGH is a youth-led program whose mission is to educate young voices about gun violence and mobilize them to take meaningful action against it. Supported by Brady United, we harness the expertise and experience of today’s youth to advance our intersectional work across the country.

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

For us, preventing gun violence not only requires regulating access to firearms but also addressing how systemic racism and environmental factors cause this form of bloodshed to run especially rampant in communities of color. You cannot talk about gun violence without talking about police brutality, white supremacy, the broken criminal justice system, poverty, homophobia, access to affordable housing, or the often barriers separating disadvantaged populations from physical and mental healthcare.

So if you share this belief, join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session and become part of the movement to end gun violence in our lifetime.

events.title: Food Scraps Collection: Encino Farmers' Market
events.description:
As a volunteer, you’ll be right in the action, collecting food scraps from market-goers—the first step in a crucial process that turns waste into nutrient-rich compost. These scraps, gathered at local markets, are then processed at nearby green parks or gardens. Throughout your shift, you'll be guided by an experienced LA Compost staff member, who will act as your Compost Manager, offering insights and helping you share the benefits of composting with the public. The best part is that during your volunteer shift, you can take some time to shop at the market. Join us and be part of the composting movement that's transforming LA—one food scrap at a time!

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
As a volunteer, you’ll play a hands-on role in guiding market-goers through composting, ensuring their food scraps are clean of stickers, compostable, and ready to be turned into nutrient-rich compost. You’ll monitor for contamination, assist with tracking data, and serve as a friendly, welcoming host to our composting community. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You'll be stationed at the LA Compost booth under a pop-up canopy within the farmers' market. There will also be seating available.
* You may be asked to assist with moving filled bins of material weighing 60+ pounds. We always offer team lifts; you will never be asked to lift bins if you prefer not to.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* Bathrooms are accessible.
* If you sign up, please show up! We rely on volunteers like you to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 
VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-wavier at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

#### AGREEMENT TO PARTNER OUTREACH:
This event is hosted in partnership with California Climate Action Corps, a program of California Volunteers, Office of the Governor. By registering for this event, you agree for your name and email address to be shared with the California Climate Action Corps (CCAC), a program of California Volunteers, Office of the Governor. You will be part of the California Climate Action Corps and receive exciting volunteer opportunities and updates of the work being done statewide and how you can affect climate change in your community.

🌟Unlock the Joy of Phone Banking: Free Class for Aspiring Volunteers🌟

Election Night still lingers in our minds—the heartbreak 💔, the fear 😰, the uncertainty 🤔—but none of that will dictate our future.
BlueVote.org embodies our promise to rebuild, fight back, and ultimately prevail. Though our challenges are immense, together we rise ✊✨. Now is the time to recharge, regroup, and prepare for the next phase of this fight 🔋⚡️.

Are you passionate about saving democracy, but feel a twinge of anxiety at the thought of phone banking? Fear not! We’re here to turn your hesitation into excitement with our FREE class designed specifically for those looking to support democracy in 2025 and beyond 🎉. Dive into the world of voter mobilization from the comfort of home 🏠—with enthusiasm and confidence! Star your next chapter of civic action now! ⭐️✅

📞 Why This Class?

Overcome Phone Bank Anxiety: We understand that the idea of making calls to strangers can be daunting. Our class is tailored to help you overcome these anxieties and turn the experience into lot of fun!

Expert Guidance: Benefit from the wisdom of an instructor, Dr. Christopher Kavanau, with decades of experience in phone bank campaigning and volunteer mobilization. His insights will not only prepare you for the task at hand at helping save democracy, but will inspire you too!

Fun-Filled Learning: Discover how phone banking can be more than just making calls; it's about connecting, engaging, and making friends while you contribute to the cause of saving democracy that you believe in.

Make a Real Impact: This is your chance to play a crucial role in saving our democracy. With each call you're making a difference!

🌈 What You'll Learn:

Strategies to ease into phone conversations without stress.
Easy techniques to keep conversations engaging and fun.
How to handle a variety of responses with grace and effectiveness.
Tips to make your phone banking sessions enjoyable and fulfilling.

🎉 Who Should Join?

This class is perfect for anyone eager to support democratic efforts, regardless of your experience level. Whether you're new to phone banking, a little bit rusty, or perhaps looking to improve your skills while enjoying the process, we've got you covered.

What you need is a comfy place in your home and access to Zoom.

Are you a young person between 13 and 25 years old who is interested in taking action around preventing gun violence? Join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session to learn more about the different ways you can engage.

Team ENOUGH is a youth-led program whose mission is to educate young voices about gun violence and mobilize them to take meaningful action against it. Supported by Brady United, we harness the expertise and experience of today’s youth to advance our intersectional work across the country.

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

For us, preventing gun violence not only requires regulating access to firearms but also addressing how systemic racism and environmental factors cause this form of bloodshed to run especially rampant in communities of color. You cannot talk about gun violence without talking about police brutality, white supremacy, the broken criminal justice system, poverty, homophobia, access to affordable housing, or the often barriers separating disadvantaged populations from physical and mental healthcare.

So if you share this belief, join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session and become part of the movement to end gun violence in our lifetime.

events.title: Time to Act!
events.description:
Are you unhappy with all the damage that the Trump administration is doing, including cutting vital services and taking away our constitutionally guaranteed rights? If so, you’re not alone.  

Most recently, federal cuts mean that almost 50 million people will lose their access to food benefits on November 1. We need to speak out. It's Time to Act!

Join us to learn how to stand up for American values of democracy and equal rights for all. Learn how we can fight to make sure our taxpayer dollars are going to help our neighbors and communities, not to billionaires or corrupt foreign governments.

In this session you'll learn how to:
 
-          Contribute to mutual aid efforts in your community
-          Ensure every ballot is counted in these critical elections
-          Resist illegal immigration acts

 During the call, we'll each make our own Action Plan to guide our steps for the following week.

Past attendee Lisa F. said, "This was an excellent training--organized, clear, and positive. I left inspired, and with a specific idea of the actions I wanted to take."

At Seattle Supports Democracy, we've trained thousands of individuals over the last five years, activating them and helping them write letters, send texts, make calls, help others, and show up to defend our democratic freedoms and make their voices heard. Join the movement!

events.title: Food Scraps Collection: Burbank Farmers Market
events.description:
As a volunteer, you’ll be right in the action, collecting food scraps from market-goers—the first step in a crucial process that turns waste into nutrient-rich compost. These scraps, gathered at local markets, are then processed at nearby green parks or gardens. Throughout your shift, you'll be guided by an experienced LA Compost staff member, who will act as your Compost Manager, offering insights and helping you share the benefits of composting with the public. The best part is that during your volunteer shift, you can take some time to shop at the market. Join us and be part of the composting movement that's transforming LA—one food scrap at a time!

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
As a volunteer, you’ll play a hands-on role in guiding market-goers through composting, ensuring their food scraps are clean of stickers, compostable, and ready to be turned into nutrient-rich compost. You’ll monitor for contamination, assist with tracking data, and serve as a friendly, welcoming host to our composting community. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You'll be stationed at the LA Compost booth under a pop-up canopy within the farmers' market. There will also be seating available.
* You may be asked to assist with moving filled bins of material weighing 60+ pounds. We always offer team lifts; you will never be asked to lift bins if you prefer not to.
* No prior composting experience is needed; everyone is welcome!
* Bathrooms are available
* If you sign up, please show up! We rely on volunteers like you to achieve our mission.  
* We’ll follow up with details via email, so be sure to provide your best contact email when signing up.

#### AGE REQUIREMENT:
This volunteer activity is best suited for volunteers aged 16 and up. Minors under 16 should come accompanied by a parent or guardian unless other arrangements are made. Contact ashleigh@lacompost.org for more information.

#### IMPORTANT: 
VOLUNTEER WAIVER: Please make sure you have signed the volunteer waiver. Access the e-wavier at https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

CODE OF CONDUCT: All volunteers are expected to adhere to our volunteer code of conduct. Please visit https://www.lacompost.org/codeofconduct to review.

#### AGREEMENT TO PARTNER OUTREACH:
This event is hosted in partnership with California Climate Action Corps, a program of California Volunteers, Office of the Governor. By registering for this event, you agree for your name and email address to be shared with the California Climate Action Corps (CCAC), a program of California Volunteers, Office of the Governor. You will be part of the California Climate Action Corps and receive exciting volunteer opportunities and updates of the work being done statewide and how you can affect climate change in your community.

events.title: Swing Left Maricopa County Monthly Meeting
events.description:
Join Swing Left Maricopa County for our monthly meetings and help grow our D/democratic grassroots community and power!

During these virtual ZOOM “C.A.L.L.S.," you'll hear from Candidates and about upcoming Actions; Learn about the issues and initiatives, and find out about the “Light a Fire” opportunities that will make a difference in Maricopa County, for Arizona, and beyond…

Together we can stay engaged, support each other, and continue to fight for the rights of all people. As the singer/songwriter/activist Joan Baez said, “Action is the antidote to despair.” And Swing Left is a national network that offers high impact ways to support Democratic candidates in races that will flip the balance of power, protect our freedoms, and create a more inclusive and equitable government and society for us all. 

So, please, bring us your interests, your skills, your passions, and the time you have available to Swing Left Maricopa County, and together, let’s make our impact felt! We look forward to meeting and collaborating with you…

events.title: Take a Stand: Pennsylvania Friend & Phone Bank
events.description:
Help us defend democracy—right from your couch! 🏛️ We’re using Scale-to-Win to connect with Pennsylvania voters and encourage them to speak up to their state and federal representatives about the issues that matter most.

❤️ Why It Matters
Every call you make empowers voters to raise their voices—supporting policies that strengthen democracy and pushing back against legislation that threatens it. 🗳️

💻🍿 What You’ll Need
A computer with reliable internet

A comfy, quiet spot (snacks encouraged!)

💡 How It Works
Hop on Zoom (link sent after sign-up) a few minutes early

Get a quick training on Scale-to-Win + talking points 🗣️

Start making calls to inform, motivate, and mobilize Pennsylvania voters 📞

Encourage voters to call their reps—so their voices echo loud and clear 🔊

Take a stand with us—let’s fight for democracy and never obey in advance! ✊✨

events.title: Free Speech Team Meeting
events.description:
From book bans and Don't Say Gay to anti-protest laws and the defunding of DEI programs, our first amendment rights are under attack here in Florida.

Join our monthly Free Speech team to connect with other Floridians and strategize on how we can protect and defend free speech values in our own communities. We'll discuss direct actions, plan Know Your Rights trainings, and more. 

Together, we can build power and protect our civil liberties!

events.title: Unload & Unwind

Unload & Unwind is our monthly get-together to vent, ask questions, and support each other during these stressful times we're currently living in. Unload & Unwind is a safe space to chat with like-minded people and is especially helpful for those who feel isolated in red areas. 

Who is Indivisible Centex? 
We are a grassroots organization based in central Texas. Our mission is to create a community of like-minded, pro-democracy people, provide a safe space for those being targeted, and fight fascism by fighting mis/disinformation as well as taking practical action.

events.description:
**Support Senator Kelly at our Dec 1st event!**  Bring signs thanking him for doing his job (supporting our military in honoring their oath to the Constitution) as we **peacefully** continue our demand for Schweikert to do his job.

Register here to help us with an accurate count for planning purposes.

We recommend:

- **Bring non-perishable food items to help brighten the holidays** to the food drive sponsored by MoveOn

- Bring a **letter** or a postcard message to drop off at Schweikert's office

- Bring signs! 

- The building and parking lot are on private property. Building management has asked us from time to time not to park in their parking lot. You may want to take advantage of street parking or park in Kohl's parking lot 1/2 block east on Raintree Rd.

Come any Monday. We are outside David Schweikert’s office from 8-9 am.

Our CD1 Coalition Partners include: Move On, Optimists Resist Indivisible, Stand Indivisible, the Democrats of LD4, LD3, LD2, LD8, LD5, the North Scottsdale Democrats, the Fountain Hills Democratic Club, Fountain Hills Independent Indivisibles, Desert Progressives Indivisible, Swing Left Maricopa County, and Honest Arizona.

events.title: TUES @12:30ET ON ZOOM: Lunchtime Calling Clinic! Dial electeds in community w/ Target Majority NYC
events.description:
For many folks, the idea of calling an elected official and stating a point of view, not to mention a strong one, and asking to vote in line with your values can seem pretty daunting, or just plain pointless. But we're here to reassure you--just about everyone who gives it a try finds it empowering and really easy, too!

Join us for a quick 15 minute gathering a couple times a week at lunchtime to check in with each other, visit the [Action Hub](https://bit.ly/resistresources) maintained by Target Majority NYC, and then go on mute/volume down and call together!

We'll answer any questions you have about the calls our group recommends, and enjoy some like-minded community in the middle of the day :-)

Think of it as a training-social-accountability circle gathering all rolled into one. See you there!!

Join us to rally in support of democracy and against the coup engineered by Musk, Trump, and Peter Thiel's Palantir! Bring a sign and a friend!

We practice peaceful non-violence and non-confrontation. Although we are all very concerned about Elon Musk' s activities and unconstitutional meddling in our democracy, we protest peacefully and with comradery among those who support refusing to go along with Trump and Musk.

Join Common Cause for an important phone bank as we mobilize voters to take action against dangerous legislation in state houses and Congress. We will focus on the most urgent campaigns that need our help. Some of these campaigns may include stopping bills that will make it harder for millions of Americans—especially students, seniors, and veterans—to cast their ballots. We need your help to ensure voters across the country call their elected representatives and make their voices heard.

No prior experience is necessary—our team will provide full training at the start of each shift!

* A step-by-step walkthrough of our Phone Dialer tools.
* Expert tips on effective communication with voters.
* Opportunities to ask questions and connect with other like-minded volunteers.


Sign up today and take the first step toward empowering voters and protecting democracy in 2025!

Public education is under attack. From attempts to defund public schools through voucher scams, to efforts aimed at censoring educators and whitewashing history, the Trump Administration and its allies are threatening the future of education as we know it. On February 4th, media reported that the administration has even begun efforts to dismantle the Department of Education.

We can’t stay silent. Public School Strong has launched a Letter to the Editor Campaign to amplify voices calling for strong, fully funded, and equitable public schools.

**TAKE ACTION: Click on the *Get Started* button to the right for a sample Letter to the Editor that you can adapt for your local newspaper or media today!**

Writing a letter to your local paper is one of the most effective ways to reach allies as well as local and statewide decision-makers. Get started today to organize your local community and flood local media with real voices and perspectives.

Together, we can push back against these dangerous attacks and show that our communities are united in support of public schools.

# Organize the Church: Resisting with Our Soul, Mind, Body & Spirit  
### Presented by Live Free USA and Black Church Freedom Fund

Join Live Free USA and the Black Church Freedom Fund for **Organize the Church**, a recurring gathering for faith leaders, organizers, and justice advocates committed to transforming communities. Each session focuses on equipping leaders with strategies to resist systemic injustice, build power, and reclaim the moral narrative.

Our discussions center on faith-rooted organizing, community healing, movement-building, and tackling the most pressing justice issues of our time. This is more than a conversation—it’s a call to action.

events.title: Clinic Defense Training Dates
events.description:
We appreciate your interest in clinic defense and patient escort work. We are looking for people 18 years and older to participate.

You will be helping patients access safe and legal abortion healthcare in Hillsborough or Pinellas Counties. We hold online training periodically to ensure you are fully aware of the roles and practices taken to ensure everyone's safety.

We will walk through our Clinic Defense roles and information to keep you safe while supporting women's access to healthcare.

Clinic Escort: Stay on the property to shield patients with umbrellas, fabric screens, and signs. You only interact with patients, not protestors. 

Clinic Defender: Stay at the perimeter, blocking protestors' signs with pro-choice messaging.

Sign Waving: Sign Waving: Show support by waving signs, raising awareness about reversing Florida's 6-week abortion ban or supporting reproductive rights. You can choose not to engage with patients or protestors.

We don't physically engage with protestors but ensure patients can enter the clinic with minimal harassment.

Once trained, you can access the Sign up pages for specific clinic locations and times.

Thank you for your support!

events.title: Wisconsin Disability Vote Coalition

sponsor.name: REV UP, American Association of People with Disabilities (AAPD)

events.description:
The Wisconsin Disability Vote Coalition (WDVC) is a non-partisan effort to help ensure full participation in the entire electoral process of voters with disabilities, including registering to vote, casting a vote, and accessing polling places.

The Coalition is on the frontline providing training and support to voters with disabilities, family members, and service providers. While much progress has been made in improving the accessibility of our elections, many opportunities for improvement remain.

Disability Vote Coalition Goals
Educate the disability community about voting rights and access issues.
Increase voter turnout among people with disabilities and their allies.
Work with elected officials and other policy makers to advance policies and practices that support accessible elections.
Encourage organizations to conduct local get-out-the-vote drives and outreach.

Disability Vote Coalition Leadership
The Coalition is coordinated by Disability Rights Wisconsin (DRW) and Wisconsin Board for People with Developmental Disabilities (BPDD). It includes over 40 community agency partners as well as self-advocates and other community members.
View a list of Coalition leadership and community agency partners (accessible PDF).

events.title: Sem Dems Virtual Writing Circle: Holding Space in Difficult Times
events.description:
Join us for a time of reflection and freewriting—no writing experience or talent necessary!

We will lead a virtual writing circle for those who are concerned about the state of their country and could use some time to express those feelings with likeminded folks.

This event will begin with individual check-ins, when attendees will let the group know how they’re doing. Then we’ll proceed to a silent writing time based on reflective prompts. After that, everyone will be invited (but not required) to share their writing with the group. 

This event is meant to help attendees process emotions that are hard to handle, experience the bonds of community, and move forward with a focus on what they are creating in the world.

We hope you can join us as we write our way towards hope.

***For this event, we ask that all participants be willing to show themselves on camera for security reasons***

Right now, we know you may be feeling discouraged, dismayed, and even depressed by the current state of our politics and our nation; we’re feeling this way, too. Yet this is not the time to step back or look away. Together we can stay engaged, support each other, and continue to fight for the rights of all people. As the singer/songwriter/activist Joan Baez said, “Action is the antidote to despair.” And Swing Left is a national network that offers high impact ways to support Democratic candidates in races that will flip the balance of power, protect our freedoms, and create a more inclusive and equitable government and society for us all.

So, please, bring us your interests, your skills, your passions, and the time you have available to Swing Left Maricopa County, and together, let’s make our impact felt! We look forward to meeting and collaborating with you…

events.title: Sign-up For Democracy Action Network / Indivisible LA
events.description:
The Democracy Action Network (DAN) was founded in November 2024 by David Comfort in response to the re-election of Donald Trump. Emerging as a grassroots organization dedicated to defending democratic institutions, promoting civic engagement, and fostering inclusive democracy, DAN has quickly become a prominent force in the pro-democracy movement. With a nonpartisan ethos and a commitment to nonviolent resistance, DAN seeks to address threats to constitutional governance while building a broad-based coalition for democratic renewal.

Mission and Vision
DAN’s mission is to protect and strengthen democratic institutions, resist authoritarian tendencies, and promote an inclusive vision of democracy that upholds universal human rights and dignity. The organization operates on the principles of nonviolence, transparency, and participatory decision-making while fostering hope-centered messaging and constructive solutions. It aims to create sustainable organizing structures that empower communities and build long-term resilience against democratic backsliding.

Early Achievements
Since its inception, DAN has demonstrated its capacity for impactful action:

- February 22nd 2025: Organized a successful march and rally in West Hollywood, drawing hundreds of participants advocating for government accountability and democratic principles
.
- February 2025: Played a key role in coordinating protests at SpaceX, bringing attention to issues tied to corporate influence and public policy.

- Held weekly organizing meetings with 300 to 400 people attending.
- Developing a core group of activists and organizers

- March 22nd 2025: Held a really successful "March for our Constitution" at the Federal Building in Westwood / Los Angeles. Had over 2,000 participants and hosted speakers such as Martin Sheen and Maxine Waters


These events have helped establish DAN as a credible voice for democratic activism while galvanizing public support for its mission.

re Board of Supervisors:

The County Board of Supervisors are elected to four-year terms and provide direction to the County Administrator and several other county departments. 

The board is like the City Council, except its jurisdiction covers all the county and unincorporated areas. 

Board members decide the county tax rate and approve the county budget. 

The County Board of Supervisors oversees health, road, parks, libraries, law enforcement, and other municipal services. The Board also has the power to fill vacancies in the county and legislative offices, other boards and commissions, pass resolutions, and enact ordinances and regulations as authorized by state law. 

The Board has the authority to make decisions on a variety of issues, such as zoning changes, resolutions, and ordinances. 

Additionally, the board of supervisors has the power to remove and replace election precincts, appoint election inspectors and judges as well as canvass election returns, declare election results, and issue certificates.

events.title: Four Corners in Lenexa  Standing Rally
events.description: As citizens, we can’t let the policies and actions of the Federal Government and unelected billionaires be normalized, but we can only stop what’s going on by coming together.  A STANDING RALLY  will draw attention to the situation, encouraging our neighbors to join with us. We will rally every Saturday morning from 11 AM – 12 PM.  Stay for the full hour or come by when and for how long you can. We will peacefully line the sidewalk on all four corners of 87th Parkway and Maurer Road,  holding signs on issues that are most meaningful to us or just simply standing in support of our neighbors and our country.  If sitting is more comfortable for you, you are very welcome to bring mobility or lawn chairs!! There is room for everyone!
events.accessibility_notes:
Please be especially mindful of parking.  For example, if you live relatively nearby, please consider walking.  If you drive, there is street parking on the residential streets to the north and also a bit further on the south.  About ½ mile down on the west, there is a large civic campus garage at 17201 W 87th St. Pkwy.  In addition, on the SE, SW, and NW sides of the intersection, there are restaurants and shops with big, but commercially owned parking lots meant for customers, if you are one. Note that Lenexa Point on the NW side has recently put up signs, saying they will tow non-customer cars.  If you cross from one side of the street to another during the rally, please pay particular attention to cars turning right as you cross! 
Participants should bring their own signs (if they want to hold them).  Note that sticks supporting the signs can’t be pointed at either end.  Also, in designing content for the signs, please remember that children will be present.  Please stand only along the sidewalks parallel to the street and not on the grass.  However, also be sure to allow pedestrian access to the sidewalk and businesses.   We are not expecting issues, but keep in mind that a core principle behind our events is a commitment to nonviolent action.  Remember to de-escalate any potential confrontation with someone, who disagrees with you. And of course, follow directions from our excellent Lenexa police, if asked. We will not have speakers (but do expect lots of cars with horn honking in agreement). Finally, please note that all our organizers will be wearing lanyards and neon vests, if you have questions. See you soon.  Let’s show our neighbors “what Democracy Looks Like”!!
P.S.  If you want to post an inspiring (!) story about your experience, please add #FourCornersLenexa to your post!

events.title: Miami Voter Phone Bank
events.description:
Help Make Our Local Democracy More Representative - CALLING ALL MIAMIANS!

It’s time to push forward and ensure that Miami voters have the voice and representation they deserve. Join the ACLU of Florida virtually to call residents of the City of Miami to get out the vote for the upcoming municipal election, urge voters to pass the pro-democracy Referendum 3, and to support an amendment for next years ballot that would:

•Move city elections alongside statewide elections: To increase voter participation, making it easier for working families to take part in our democracy, saving millions of dollars in taxpayer money.

•Expand the City Commission: To provide greater representation and ensure every community in Miami has a voice in how our city is run.

•Ban Commission districts from being gerrymandered: To prevent corrupt politicians from abusing the political process for personal gain.

This amendment will make our local elections fairer, more accessible, increase voter participation, and make our city government more reflective of the communities it serves. 

Whether you are a phone banking expert or have never phone banked before, we make getting started as easy as possible and work with you every step of the way. This is your chance to take direct action, protect civil rights, and shape the future of our local community!

Rev. Barber has prayed against the Republican-passed "Big Beautiful Bill Act" while in the Rotunda of our US Capitol because it hurts poor people to benefit rich people. He has noted: “Forty-three percent of women and almost half of all children are poor and low income. Somebody ought to say something … Somebody gotta challenge this budget.”

We are holding "Moral Monday" street rallies to voice our challenges.

We oppose the Republican-adopted federal budget resolutions that harm the poorest and most vulnerable of Americans in order to give trillions in tax breaks to the richest and most privileged of Americans.

We oppose cuts to health research, education, housing assistance, community development, child care, and other federal programs for needy veterans, the elderly, and children.

These funding cuts are not just bad public policy choices.

These funding cuts are morally wrong. 

Please join with us to "say something".

events.title: Attend Woodstock City Council Meetings
events.description:
Location: Woodstock City Hall, 8534 Main St, Woodstock, GA 30188
Time: 7:00 PM 
Parking: Free parking nearby

These meetings decide what happens in our community—from zoning and development to public safety, housing, and library funding. If we don’t show up, others get to shape those decisions without us.

Indivisible Woodstock CAN attends City Council meetings to stay informed, hold leaders accountable, and ensure all residents—not just the loudest voices—are represented.

You don’t have to speak, but if you want to, arrive early to sign up for public comment. It usually happens near the beginning of the meeting.

For reminders or support, email: woodstockcan@proton.me
Instagram: @indivisiblewoodstockcan

🏛️ Woodstock Planning Commission Meetings – Included in the City Calendar, but NOT City Council
Planning Commission meetings are included in the city’s public meeting calendar, right alongside City Council—but don’t get confused: they are a separate body, and they matter a lot.

These are the meetings where zoning decisions, development proposals, and variance requests are first heard. If we don’t show up here, developers get a clear runway. By the time something hits City Council, it’s often too late to stop or change it.

📆 Upcoming Planning Commission Meetings (7:00 PM at Chambers at City Center):

- Thursday, June 5, 2025
- Thursday, July 10, 2025
- Thursday, August 7, 2025
- Thursday, September 4, 2025
- Thursday, October 2, 2025
- Thursday, November 6, 2025
- Thursday, December 4, 2025

🧭 Planning Commission vs. City Council
Purpose:
Planning Commission reviews zoning and development. City Council votes on final approval.

Power:
Planning Commission is advisory. City Council makes the call.

Who Attends:
Developers always show up to Planning. Residents usually don’t—and that’s a problem.

Why It Matters:
Planning Commission is your best shot to stop bad development or push for better outcomes. If we wait until City Council, the fight’s already halfway lost.

Join us to turn information and connection with others into ACTION to strengthen our democracy.  We're focusing on hard things, but we'll lead with humor and hope and we'll let positivity and a belief in our indomitable American spirit fuel our work rejecting authoritarianism.

** 2nd Tuesdays of Every OTHER month **

Nov. 11- Don't Talk About Politics: How to Change 21st Century Minds by Sarah Stein Lubrano

Democracy is dying because we are clinging to a dangerous and outdated myth: talking about politics can change people's minds. It doesn't.
In a world where politics keeps getting more irrational, dishonest, violent and chaotic, it's getting much harder to reach people with words alone. So people who really care about democracy must ask: how can we stop arguing and do the deep work to build stronger foundations for political life, and a better world for us all?


Jan. 13- The Persuaders: At the Front Line, Fight for Hearts, Minds and Democracy by Anand Giridharadas 

The lifeblood of any free society is persuasion: changing other people’s minds in order to change things. But America is suffering a crisis of faith in persuasion that is putting its democracy and the planet itself at risk. Americans increasingly write one another off instead of seeking to win one another over. Debates are framed in moralistic terms, with enemies battling the righteous. 

As the book’s subjects grapple with how to call out threats and injustices while calling in those who don’t agree with them but just might one day, they point a way to healing, and changing, a fracturing country.

events.title: Evergreen Organizing Skills: The Hard 1:1
events.description:
Much of activism is devoted to trying to spread the word and "visibility" of an issue. But the step between agreement and action is a huge one!

How do you convince someone who isn't already on your side, is skeptical, or even hostile to join your cause? Join us as we learn about and practice the skills needed to have a Hard 1:1 (aka a structured organizing conversation)

Learn the techniques and tips necessary to convince your community to join the fight! And then practice the hard parts of the hardest conversations.

This is an organizing fundamental and key to building the future we deserve!

events.title: Democracy Rush Hour Rally: 8am Every Tuesday at University/Farley
events.description:
Every Tuesday, citizens have been reaching commuters on University Ave in Madison, WI with pro-democracy messages and a targeted theme each week. During morning rush hour hundreds of commuters have to sit at this red light and look at our signs! This is an opportunity to pierce through our current news (and disinformation) ecosystems with concise pro-democracy ideas, messages, and calls to action.

In your confirmation email, you will receive a link to a google doc and my email so you can get the weekly topic. If you don't know the topic of the week or want to use the same sign every week, you can always just make one telling drivers to call their senators and rep! We will also have cardboard/markers available.

This is a non-violent and non-confrontational event. All participants are encouraged to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We have a lot of fun and feel free to join us for any amount of time!

events.title: Gleaning the Woodstock Farmers Market!
events.description:
Thank you for signing up to glean at the Woodstock Farmer's Market! We look forward to partnering with you to help reduce food waste and feed our hungry neighbors.

📅 Date: Every Saturday (rain or shine), until December 20th

⏰ Time: 11:30 am-12:30 pm

📍 Location: Volunteers will park in the rear parking lot of Bank OZK, 8770 Main St, Woodstock, GA 30188. The market is less than one minute away from the parking lot.

✅ What to expect: Volunteers will collect excess produce from various vendors at the Woodstock Farmers Market before closing at 12:00 pm. They estimate that around 40-65 lbs of produce will be available to be gleaned each Saturday, post-market.

🙋🏽‍♀️🙋🏽‍♂️ We are looking for more volunteers who believe in our mission of reducing food waste on the farmer's market level & feeding those in need in the local area. We are asking for a 1x/month commitment from each volunteer. Volunteers will be given all the necessary information, a walk-thru of the market, vendors introduction & gleaning equipment. 

Please bring water and wear comfortable clothing & shoes, sunscreen and a hat.

Looking forward to gleaning & making an impact with you! 🌱🌍

events.title: Texas Blue Action Block Captain Program Information
events.description:
Have you attended a Blue Action Network Onboarding? Have you grown your personal network using our organizing tool?

Now you might be asking - How do I grow my network further? How do I get plugged into door knocking and reach even more voters? This is where the Block Captain program comes in.

Blue Action Block Captains facilitate deeper connections with the people in our neighborhoods who are open to voting Democrat down the ballot. This is not your typical get-out-the-vote door knocking. Blue Action will supply you with a home turf (permanent list of the 50 mid-propensity) Democratic voters near you, as well as a year-long strategy to build meaningful relationships with your neighbors.

Come to this virtual event to learn more and take data-driven coordinated ACTION against the MAGA movement for the 2026 Primary and General Midterm Elections.

events.title: Weekly Darrell Issa Office Rallies!
events.description:
Join us every Friday from 10:30 at Darrell Issa’s Escondido office. We’ll meet first at the office and then walk as a group to the public sidewalk on Lincoln Blvd. Bring your protest signs and a folding chair if you can’t stand for an hour or so. Consider a double-sided sign so that you can have one message for Issa and another for the motorists.

We will have a food drive benefiting Interfaith Community Services in Escondido the last Friday of every month. Please bring non-perishable, new food items. https://interfaithservices.org/

Rallies are a great way to meet other like-minded community members. They remind us that we aren’t alone and it feels good to be civically engaged. Action is the antidote to despair. We guarantee you will feel better about the state of affairs when you leave this event.

Please note that there is a mental health services business in Issa’s office. Please allow a direct path the elevator for patients at all times. Refrain from banging on the glass doors as it has been reported to upset some of the patients. Please follow all posted rules and traffic laws when attending a rally. Safety is always our first priority. Safety patrol volunteers will be wearing bright vests - please comply with their requests at all times.

events.title: Saturday Protests in O’Fallon, IL
events.description:
In solidarity with communities around us and in conjunction with local, grassroots Indivisible groups, join us for Saturday Morning Protests!

Every Saturday from 10-11am, we’ll gather in front of City Hall in O’Fallon, IL, for a peaceful protest to let our government officials and community know that we stand against the awful actions of the current administration.

Whether you care about cuts to Medicare, attacks on science, or the cruelty of our current immigration system—choose an issue, make a sign (just cardboard and marker is fine), and meet us in O’Fallon on Saturdays!

Why protest? 
(1) Protests are effective - We saw their effectiveness in Serbia in 2000, Ukraine in 2014, S. Korea in 2024, etc. 
(2) Protests change the narrative, bring-in new people, foster community, and spread courage. 
(3) Protests cause MAGA loyalists to defect and refuse to comply. 
(4) Protests make repression backfire. 
(5) Protests involve mass participation that brings Power, and that Power enables larger actions such as boycotts, mass non-cooperation like a General Strike, etc.

#### Sorting Soup: Turning Ideas Into Action - Join Weekly - every Thursday  Zoom @5PM central

This Week continuing  “2025” starting a book club .. ENJOY the read.

_Feeling overwhelmed by the constant stream of ideas, strategies, and information in the pro-democracy movement? You’re not alone._

That’s why we created Sorting Soup— a weekly space to process, connect, and turn information into real-world impact. Inspired by the dynamic NWSOFA 9am Coffee & Conversation network, Sorting Soup is your opportunity to ground yourself, build community, and decide what’s truly worth your time and energy.

#### Let us know you will be attending … RSVP here-> https://mobilize.us/s/1162kb

Join us every Thursday at 5PM (CST), Each session begins with a Decompression Hour, where we check in, share what’s on our minds, and spot the patterns emerging across our work. Then, we dive deep into a timely topic—something urgent, overlooked, or full of potential. Whether you’re ready to research, present, or just ask great questions, your voice is welcome.

We wrap up with a Deep Dive Debrief, assigning research tasks, brainstorming future speakers, and mapping out next steps. Our goal? Not just understanding, but activation. Sorting Soup is about thinking together—and then bringing those insights back to our communities to inspire real change.

events.title: NO NUKES VIGIL - Every Friday
events.description: The Santa Fe chapter of Veterans For Peace started this vigil in 2002 and have continued it every Friday at noon for 23 years. Its purpose is to bring awareness to the hundreds of billions of our tax dollars going to the production of new nuclear weapons here in our state. Many people, even many New Mexicans, are unaware that Los Alamos National Lab is currently building several new bomb factories to increase production of nuclear bomb cores (known as plutonium "pits") to reach a goal of 30 to 120 new pits per year. Each pit, on average, has the destructive power of 20 Hiroshima-sized bombs. Loud public outcry may be able to halt this waste of federal money, or at least slow it down until we elect a saner administration. Life on Earth is at stake.

events.title: Standing up for Democracy and Social Justice - Estacada - Every Saturday From 11am to Noon
events.description:
Every Saturday from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM, we gather for an hour of peaceful visibility on the corner of Highway 224 and City Hall in Downtown Estacada.

We’d like to believe we’re standing in peace — but these days, we’re standing in protest and for our democracy.

It’s fun. It’s energizing. And honestly? It’s better than doing nothing.
This may be our last chance to stand up for our rights — locally, visibly, and together. No one’s coming to save us. It’s up to us to lead. And the best place to start is right here in our own community.

✨ What to expect:
– Supportive honks and waves from passing cars
– Friendly conversation and good company
– Bring a sign if you want — or just bring yourself
– It’s only one hour, but it means something

It might feel small — but it’s something. And sometimes something is everything. Please join us. There’s real power in showing up

events.title: December Meeting: 2026 Kickoff!
events.description:
It's a momentous occasion-the first anniversary of the Indianapolis PDA. We've been meeting every Second Sunday since the pivotal November 2024 election, a testament to our resilience and commitment. 

What have we accomplished? How do progressive politics win in 2026? 

Our featured guests will be two of Indiana's most inspiring progressive voices and strategists. We will hear from Lindsay Haake and Destiny Wells.

Lindsay knows the Indiana State House better than any other Hoosier. She appears regularly on local media talking politics. Her columns appear in the Indianapolis Business Journal. Lindsay has been a leading voice and a consistent presence in the fight to hold Indiana's regulated utilities accountable and to transition Indiana to clean energy. 

Destiny Wells is a leading voice for Hoosier democracy. She came within just two votes of becoming the chairperson of the Indiana Democratic Party in March. It was a broken process in which the fractured Indiana Democratic Party establishment pulled every string to hold onto what little power it had left. She is a veteran and an active member of the Indiana National Guard, having won twice for a statewide office and consistently outperforming her peers. 

We must gear up for the crucial 2026 elections. This is an opportunity we cannot afford to miss. Lindsay and Destiny will provide a clear-eyed analysis of the lessons learned from last year, guiding us towards winning progressive politics in 2026!

Your presence is crucial in this energizing conversation. RSVP today, and be an integral part of a community that's standing firm, one year later—and ready for what's next.

events.title: Food Scraps Collection: Culver City Farmers' Market
events.description:
As a volunteer, you’ll be right in the action, collecting food scraps from market-goers—the first step in a crucial process that turns waste into nutrient-rich compost. These scraps, gathered at local markets, are then processed at nearby green parks or gardens. Throughout your shift, you'll be guided by an experienced LA Compost staff member, who will act as your Compost Manager, offering insights and helping you share the benefits of composting with the public. The best part is that during your volunteer shift, you can take some time to shop at the market. Join us and be part of the composting movement that's transforming LA—one food scrap at a time!

#### ABOUT ACTIVITY:
As a volunteer, you’ll play a hands-on role in guiding market-goers through composting, ensuring their food scraps are clean of stickers, compostable, and ready to be turned into nutrient-rich compost. You’ll monitor for contamination, assist with tracking data, and serve as a friendly, welcoming host to our composting community. 

#### MORE INFO: 
* You'll be stationed at the LA Compost booth under a pop-up canopy within the farmers' market. There will also be seating available.
