events.title: The Right to Be Safe, A Call to Faith Leaders: Access the Toolkit. Sign the Petition.
events.description:
# The Right to Be Safe  
### A Call to Faith Leaders: Access the Toolkit. Sign the Petition. Take a Stand.

**BLACK SAFETY. BLACK FAITH. BLACK RESISTANCE.**  
*A Sacred Alert for Safety, Preparedness, Community Care, and Faith*

**Sign the petition to affirm that safety is a sacred right. Then download the toolkit to prepare your congregation, protect your people, and take faithful action.**

---

## The Crisis Is Here

Black communities are under coordinated attack.

ICE raids. Surveillance. Book bans. Defunded safety programs. Environmental violence. Criminalized protest.  
None of this is isolated. And none of it is new.

This isn’t just about immigration — it’s about power, protection, and who gets to live freely, safely, and seen.

> “The assault on our freedoms isn’t coming — it’s already here.”

---

## The Response: A Toolkit for Churches, Leaders, and Communities

To meet this crisis, we are equipping faith communities to act — not from fear, but from faith.

**_The Right to Be Safe: A Black Faith Toolkit_** was created to help churches, clergy, and community members prepare and protect — spiritually, strategically, and communally.

It includes:
- Emergency church safety plans  
- ICE and 287(g) assessments  
- Know Your Rights training  
- Sanctuary signage  
- Legal and scriptural grounding  
- Community care protocols  
- Family preparedness tools

**Sign the petition to declare your belief in the sacred right to be safe — then download the toolkit to lead with care, readiness, and courage.**

---

## What You’re Signing

This is a **petition** — a public statement of belief and commitment.

By signing, you affirm:

- **Safety is a sacred right**, not a privilege  
- Black people and other marginalized communities are being disproportionately targeted by coordinated violence  
- This includes raids, surveillance, displacement, environmental harm, policing, and legal rollback  
- You are committed to preparing your church and protecting your people  
- Faith is not neutral — and silence is not an option

---

## The Petition: A Declaration of Faith

We are living in a time where the state no longer pretends to be merciful.  
ICE raids are rising. Families are being torn apart in broad daylight.  
Protest is punished. Books are banned. Safety is denied.

This is not chaos. It is policy.  
And this is not just political — it is spiritual.

We remember a Jesus born under empire.  
Counted by Caesar. Hunted by Herod. Displaced. Detained.  
If He were born today, He would be called “illegal” before He could even speak.

This is not metaphor. This is scripture.

We will not spiritualize suffering while state violence grows.  
We will not preach freedom on Sunday and ignore detention on Monday.  
We will not wait to act until they come for our own — because they already have.

We believe:

- Safety is sacred  
- Protection is love  
- Preparation is power  
- And faith without justice is not faith at all

---

**Sign the petition. Download the toolkit. Take a faithful stand.**

> “If they come for you in the morning, they will come for me at night.” — James Baldwin

**Stand in covenant. Protect your community. Be ready.**

events.title: #TeslaTakeDown Protest - Charlotte
events.description:
For Saturday 11/22 only: wear black for Signs of Fascism protest.  OK to bring your regular sign/flag.

NEVER FORGET MUSK'S DAMAGE: The many will defeat the money! Authoritarians thrive when we are overwhelmed, shut down and afraid to act- so we add joy to the resistance! It’s the most fun you’ll have standing up for our freedoms, our families and our future!

- Guidelines for participants:

- Where is it? https://maps.app.goo.gl/AAX8RkvLm1k4j3Rm9

- ICLT is committed to nonviolent action, and we expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with us. Signs and chants must not incite violence. 

- We are welcoming, safe, non-violent, and committed to building community as we oppose this corrupt, incompetent regime. We don’t verbally challenge Tesla customers or disrespect drivers or counter protesters. We don’t block driveways. Our joy is contagious and powerful. 

- Parking will be TIGHT. There is NO parking at Tesla. dealership. Park where you feel comfortable. NOTE: do NOT park in the Boston Market lot even though it is closed. 

- One parking location might be the CATS Park and Ride just south of Boston Market. Location: https://maps.app.goo.gl/nLwhi5cFjxsf6H7R6  

- NOTE: We DO NOT have explicit permission to park in any business's lot.

- DO NOT park and walk across 74 not at a crosswalk. This is unsafe.

- DO NOT walk or drive onto the Tesla property, even for protestor drop off. We MUST remain on public land.  

- Wear your ICLT shirt if you want.

- Know that there are inherent risks to protesting.
 
SAFETY DOs and DON'Ts for Friday: 
* Know your rights: The right to peacefully assemble is fundamental.  
* Be aware: be aware of your surroundings and bring attention to something you think seems off
* Bring supplies: Bring water, hand sanitizer, a hat, and sunscreen.
* Wear comfortable clothing: Wear nondescript clothing and comfortable shoes. 

IF there are counter protestors:
*Maintaining social distance: Keep physical distance from people who aren't in your group. 
*Being respectful: Show respect to others, and don't argue when tensions are high.
Signs:
* NO Nazi imagery, even in a negative light.

events.description:
We're collaborating with [Lead PA](https://www.leadpa.org/) to recruit candidates for every state house seat in Pennsylvania and we need your help!

Too many of these seats are held by Republicans and could go uncontested unless we find people willing to step up!

Participants should be comfortable communicating through Slack and using user-friendly new apps such as the Action Builder database. The 2026 filing deadline is coming up fast, so we need all hands on deck for the next 60 days.

Attendees will have the choice to learn the Call Team role or the Research Team role at this event. Attend again next time to learn the other role if you want to do both!

Join us at the corner of Main & Imperial to protest the inhumane actions of the Trump administration!

This will be a family-friendly, dog-friendly, non-violent, no-vandalism, community event. We'll be staying on the grassy areas and out of the roads. Please keep it friendly, and if there is any negativity or counter-protestors, don't engage. We'll have folks on hand who can help de-escalate any situation if necessary.

What this event is:

* This is a stationary, “honk and wave” visibility event at a location that sees a lot of weekend traffic. Bring signs!

* This is a positive, peaceful, community-focused, and family- and dog-friendly event.

What this event is not:

* This is not a march, and there is no programming/planned speaker.

* This is not a civil disobedience event. We will not block roads, sidewalks, or the entrances of any buildings.

* We will not be engaging with any hecklers. The El Segundo Police Department is aware of the event and available to help assist to keep everyone safe if there are counter-protestors.

There are many other Indivisible events across LA, so if this doesn't sound like what you're looking for, please feel free to attend a different event.

Details:

* 10 AM to 12 PM

* Grassy area in front of the El Segundo sign at the corner of Main & Imperial in El Segundo. We will expand to the grassy area across Main if necessary.

* There is street parking along Imperial Avenue (not Imperial Highway) within El Segundo, as well as on the surrounding streets south of Imperial Ave.

* Please do not park illegally (i.e. blocking driveways or in the local businesses’ lots). We want to bring people in to our movement, not turn them off!

We can't wait to see you. We are looking forward to making our voices heard together!
This a local Indivisible event!

events.title: Every Saturday Pullman Rally for Sanity #Indivisible #NoKings #HandsOff #MoveOn #50501

location.venue: On the sidewalk in front of Neill Public Library
address_lines: North Grand Avenue & Northeast Olsen Street

events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Hello, people who care about democracy! 

My name is Syd and I call myself the reluctant activist, because I'd really rather be home resting, crocheting and managing my health issues but instead I'm forced to fight fascism in America. I'll be the one with the walker and the loud voice. 😁

With the rapid assaults on our rights, the government cuts designed to hurt the poor and vulnerable, along with endlessly funding genocide and much more, it would be easy to feel hopeless. I feel it's important that we protest this insanity and remember we have the power.

I have a rally every Saturday. We meet from 12-1 on the sidewalk in front of the Neill Public Library. It's at the intersection of N Grand and Olson NE across from the Cougar Plaza.

This Big Beautiful Killer Bill is the opposite of what our government should do for the people. Republicans are choosing to let people go hungry, lose insurance and frankly, die. Not to balance the budget, they're doing it to reward the wealthiest.

We won't give up our rights to peacefully protest. We need to remind this administration that it's the people who have the power, it's supposed to be Congress that writes laws and declares war, that protest is legal but human trafficking is not.

I know these are scary times and I appreciate your bravery. I have rallied here multiple times and usually the most negative thing I have experienced is a few harsh words from a moving vehicle (that I usually can't hear). I simply reply with "I love you!" as loudly as I am able. It's fun and it prevents any hate from sticking to us. Mostly we get a lot of honking and waving. I find it invigorating, especially when we are surrounded by a lot of other rally-goers.

If someone does tries to instigate trouble don't confront them and remain peaceful. Come get me. You can also leave if you need to. Record video if you are able, so that authorities will be able to ID the agitator. It's also extremely important that our protest remain on the sidewalk and not block the traffic or crosswalks so we don't give the police a reason to arrest anyone.

I'm not downplaying the new steps towards full fascism this administration has taken and I don't want you to. Please take the necessary steps to protect yourself.

Again, I expect no problem at our little event, I expect colorful, creative signs, some chanting and numbers of like-minded people who care about our country. If you have any streamers or pinwheels to attach to your signs, please do.There's almost always a breeze. Get your feelings out on your signs, enjoy the marker fumes and chalk dust. Bring water. 
If you have any questions contact me here

p.s. Despite what Tr*mp and Fox News say, I have never received a paycheck for rallying against his theft of power, but I have noted his history of projection. Has he paid people to rally for him?

events.title: Standout for Veterans & All Federal Workers!
events.description:
Stand with us at the entrance to the regional headquarters of the VA Central Western Massachusetts Healthcare System to support our veterans and all federal workers! VA workers are the backbone of the VA system, ensuring veterans get the care and support they earned. 

We are in a high traffic area at a busy light that offers great visibility, with veterans and employees turning into the VA driveway. About a third of all federal workers are veterans adversely affected by the federal government’s major restructuring and job slashing. 

Our weekly standouts let federal workers know that we support them, while we protest DOGE/Project 2025 cuts and the abrupt cancellation of union contracts. We won’t sit by idly while the Trump regime works to privatize the VA, which would hollow out a system that provides health care and support tailored for the special needs of our veterans.

Join us to show that ordinary people can raise our voices against the chaos and destruction of the current regime. Help remind your neighbors that they, too, can summon the courage to stand up for their principles. Join the many veterans and their family members who aren't on board with the "cruelty as entertainment" behavior of Trump and the GOP.

events.description:
QPP is an action-oriented community for queers and allies joined together in solidarity, providing mutual aid-based survival work — rooted in principles of racial justice, gender justice, disability justice, economic justice and class justice — and creating a place of true belonging and community.

🌈

Here are our group norms:

Respect Worth/Dignity: We respect the worth and dignity of others and that guides our interactions with everyone in the group.

Intent: We assume others are acting with good intent. If someone says or does something insensitive or hurtful, we help them learn.

Accountability: We know that we can all make mistakes, and we endeavor to act with grace to acknowledge them and repair any damage done.

Embrace Growth Mindset: We strive to see mistakes or conflicts as opportunities to learn and grow.

Intergenerational Respect: We acknowledge that, while the lived experiences of group members of various ages will differ, we will give everyone's thoughts and actions due consideration. No one is too young or too old to contribute or to have great ideas.

Confidentiality: We agree that stories stay and learning leaves. We can apply what we learn from others in the group, we cannot share their stories.

Step Forward/Step Back: We strive to promote equitable participation in the group using the "step forward/step back" framework. If you frequently speak up in conversations, consider stepping back to make room for other voices. If you typically remain quiet in conversations, consider stepping forward to make your voice heard.

Leadership Rotates: We do not have a hierarchical structure. Working groups (including leadership!) are all made up of volunteers, and involvement in them is not set in stone. If you want to be involved in a working group, please let someone in that group know. (Planning consists of volunteers.) Choose how you best think you can contribute, and let someone know.

Please note: Our team is taking a break the week of Thanksgiving, and we won't be out on the streets of Scranton on Monday, November 24th. We will be back at it on Monday, December 1st — and watch for a special holiday edition on Monday, December 15th!

**🚁 Speak out against soaring costs! 🚁**

Join us weekly in front of Senator Dave McCormick's Scranton office to speak out against the federal agenda that is making corporations and billionaires richer while the rest of us face soaring costs every day!

We will also make our way over to Congressman Rob Bresnahan's office regularly to ask why he's not holding in-person town halls to face questions from his constituents and why he keeps selling us out while he gets richer and richer.

🏢 We’re gathering outside McCormick’s office, and we’ll take field trips over to Bresnahan’s office. Because guess what? Bresnahan’s office is conveniently located just around the corner!


**This is what democracy looks like—NEPA style.**


Action Together NEPA is proud to host these actions as part of the Pennsylvanians Together coalition, working together to create a commonwealth where we all can thrive, not just survive. We work to hold our elected leaders accountable and empower constituents to take action.

events.title: Tell Lackawanna County Commissioners: Protect Our Queer and Unhoused Neighbors!
events.description:
Join us as we tell Lackawanna County Commissioners to protect our queer and unhoused neighbors by codifying a non-discrimination ordinance that includes gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, and housing status. 

Whether you are housed or unhoused, part of the LGBTQ+ community or not, we all deserve equal opportunities to thrive in our communities. Lackawanna County has the power to implement a non-discrimination ordinance that protects all of us. 

But in order to get it done we need to ensure that our voices are heard loud and clear by our elected officials! Meet us at Black and Brass Coffee at 101 Penn Ave, Scranton at 9am for coffee and we'll walk to the County Commissioners meeting at the Lackawanna County Administration Building as a team. If you can't join us for coffee but can join us at the meeting, we'll see you there at 10am!

Can't make it but still want your voice to be heard? Sign our petition that we'll present at the County Commissioners meeting: https://www.mobilize.us/pastandsup/event/815397/

events.title: John Lewis "Good Trouble" Teach-In: The Racial Injustice of Gun Violence
events.description:
In honor of John Lewis Day, our teach-in examines how systemic racism drives and sustains the crisis of gun violence in communities of color. Far from random, this violence is rooted in decades of policy decisions, from redlining and housing segregation to underfunded social services and unequal law enforcement.

In this video training, we will explore how these interconnected systems have created conditions where gun violence thrives, making it a powerful form of racial injustice, and dive into how President Trump’s policies and funding cuts have exacerbated these inequalities. Join us to uncover the structural forces behind the headlines and carry forward John Lewis’s legacy by demanding lasting, systemic change, civil rights for all, and a democracy that works for everyone.

The training is given by Rachelle Hunley, Brady's Senior Director of Strategic Engagement, Aalayah Eastmond, our Cultural Community Engagement Manager, and JP Thomas, our Director of Organizing.

events.title: Indivisible Sausalito Monthly Meeting
events.description:
Join us for our March meeting on zoom!  We will share what we know, what we're doing, and what we need. 

We'll cover the current constitutional crisis, the federal budget crisis, the immigration crisis, any other to-be-named crisis, and we will even dare to celebrate and laugh a little.  The best antidote to fascism is to come together in community, to organize and mobilize and that's what we do best. 

We have been an Indivisible group since 2016,  support the strategies in the Indivisible Guide, and believe in the power of community and in local action. Over the years we have built a brilliant community of people who care, who show up, and who support each other. 

Whether you're new to this or cannot believe we are still at it, you are welcome to join. 

We meet every month on zoom, the fourth Wednesday, from 6pm-7pm.

events.title: Disappeared in America Visibility Event:  Yolo County - Three Cities

address_lines: 23 Russell Blvd, Davis OR 1000 Main St. Woodland OR West Sacramento, at the corner of Jefferson Blvd. and Park Blvd.

events.description:
In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison. Disappeared in America is a Yolo County day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga.

🚨 On the 1st Wednesday of the month, we’re showing up in Yolo County to say: In America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.🚨We will gather at three locations:  In Davis in front of City Hall at 23 Russell Blvd; in Woodland in front of the new courthouse at 1000 Main St. and in West Sacramento at the corner of Jefferson Blvd. and Park Blvd. Bring your signs and your voices. 

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

events.description:
Weekly Demonstration ~ What do you stand for? 
What are you willing to get into good trouble to support?

We meet every Thurs, late afternoon until sunset
near the Buffalo Bill statue, Washington Ave & 10th St, Golden CO

Come STAND with us one deep on the sidewalks thru Golden. We will start at Washington Ave and 10th St & spread out, as far as we can go.

This is a peaceful rally. One of the important principles is the idea of de-escalation. We aim for a nonviolent protest. And we aim to be counted. We will also have the opportunity to talk with our neighbors about the important issues of the day. 

IndivisibleTableMountain@gmail.com

We have to respond to the attacks posed on our civil and human rights by the current administration and to remind them that in America, the power lies with the people. 

We’re sending a clear message -- In the United States, the power lies in the hands of the people. We demand an end to
•	The extreme crackdown on our civil rights by the Trump administration, from our right to vote to our right to protest and free speech
•	The attacks on black and brown Americans, immigrants, trans people, and other communities
•	The slashing of programs that working people rely on, including Medicaid, SNAP, and Social Security

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Weekly Vigil for Democracy at the Brooklyn Metropolitan Detention Center
events.description:
WEATHER NOTICE: Rain is in the forecast today, 11/25, so we expect a smaller turnout for tonight's vigil. We still plan to be out there with candles to share. If you will join us, bring your umbrella!

Join us in standing up for our neighbors, held at the notorious prison in our own back yard. For years, the Metropolitan Detention Center has had a reputation for inhumane conditions: rancid food, lack of heating in winter and oppressive heat in summer. In 2020, an inmate named Jamel Floyd was killed by corrections officers by excessive use of force. Now, ICE is using the Metropolitan Detention Center to house our immigrant neighbors -- mothers, fathers, sons and daughters -- who have been taken from their homes, schools, and workplaces and held in detention.

Our fellow organizers at Good Shepherd Lutheran Church in Bay Ridge are holding for a weekly vigil outside the MDC to call for the release of ICE detainees, and to stand against the inhumane treatment of our neighbors. Supporters are invited to bring signs, to sing or play music, and to solemnly bear witness in solidarity. Together we will build and strengthen the vital community connections.

* We gather first at the corner of 3rd Avenue and 29th Street.

events.title: Honk For A Change
events.description:
Hey friends,

We’re turning up the volume every Tuesday in Baton Rouge — and we need YOU out there with us.

The Tuesday Rush Hour Honkers are hitting the streets to Honk for Change — a weekly pop-up protest to make some noise, hold signs, and remind the city that we’re still here, still fighting, and still watching.

 Where: Perkins Road & Kenilworth Parkway

 When: Every Tuesday, 4:00 – 5:30 PM
 Yes, there’s shade along the protest line!

Bring a sign. Bring a chair. Bring a friend.
Whether you can stay the whole time or just stop by for a few minutes, your presence matters. Let’s turn as many voices into the many reasons we keep fighting for justice, equity, and accountability.

Let’s be loud. Let’s be seen. Let’s remind Baton Rouge that people power doesn’t clock out at 5.

events.title: Money Out of Politics - Recruitment Packet Party
events.description:
Come hang out with us while we recruit volunteers and assemble intro packets to onboard volunteers and enlist endorsees and community partners. There will be lunch, music, and the chance to get to know other volunteers with Michigan United Action.  It's okay if you're new to this campaign, we'll teach you all about it! 


Come and go as you please - if you need to come late or leave early, it's all good!


Michigan United Action is part of **Michiganders for Money Out of Politics (MMOP)**. We are going to fight back against corporate control of our government.

**Our goal:** Pass a citizen-led ballot initiative that bans political contributions from regulated monopoly utilities (like DTE and Consumers Energy) and corporations that seek or hold large state and local government contracts (over $250,000)

**Why?** Simple: We want to stop corporations from buying off our democracy.

**Is this a campaign you support?** Just ask yourself: Do we want a government that serves us — or a government bought and paid for by corporations?

If you have any questions about the campaign or would like to get involved, please reach out to MMOP@miunited.org

events.description:
**Join us for our monthly Pike-Wayne Chapter Meeting!**

Our work continues because action is the antidote. Hope to see you there!

**DECEMBER MEETING DETAILS**

We'll be meeting virtually for the next few months, so join us on Zoom! Sign up today to get the link.

We are excited to see you at our next Pike/Wayne virtual meeting. I can't wait to reconnect with you all. And believe it or not … the Pennsylvania budget is actually done. Wild, right? We’ll be diving into what this new budget actually means for us here in NEPA. Kristin Volchansky, ATNEPA’s brilliant Advocacy Director, will be joining us to break it all down. We’ll also catch up on what’s happening across our region, from transit and healthcare to environmental protections and mutual aid efforts. And of course, we’ll run through what’s coming up  including our weekly “Show Up/Speak Out” in Scranton on Mondays (2–3 PM), and our Annual Regional Brunch on December 7th at Sands Golf Course in Drums. It’s always such a highlight! Good food, good company, and some much-needed end-of-year joy.

## Clatsop County Wolf Pack: Howl 'n' Growl Monthly Meeting

**Come howl with us!** The Clatsop County Wolf Pack is organizing monthly **Howl 'n' Growl** community meetings to build **working-class power** from the ground up. These gatherings are led by _Clatsop County members_ of the **Oregon Working Families Party**, and are open to anyone who believes in fighting for a political home for the multiracial working class.

#### Every month, we rotate meeting locations across Clatsop County to make space for more neighbors to plug in. These meetings are about more than updates — they’re about building real relationships, planning meaningful local actions, and growing our movement. Whether you’re a seasoned organizer or brand-new to the WFP, there’s a role for you here.

##### 🌲 What to expect:

- Meet others who care about building grassroots power in Clatsop County

- Help plan events, actions, and campaigns that matter to our community

- Learn how to get involved in the statewide movement to win governing power for the multiracial working class

### 📍 Meeting location changes each month!
We’ll update this Mobilize page with the new location ahead of each meeting — so make sure to check back before you come!

Together, we’re building something bigger than any one event. We’re building a political home _by_ and _for_ **working people** — rooted in **Clatsop County**, and rising across the state.

events.description:
We love democracy. We love crafts. We love snacks. And we love civic engagement.

You too? Join us for **Anti-Fascist Craft Night** in Lititz—a low-key hang where we cut up cereal boxes and old magazines, make wild collage postcards and letters, and send our thoughts (and shade) to our elected officials. Make your voice heard in a weirdly therapeutic and hands-on way!

**What to bring:**

* Clean cardboard (cereal/snack boxes) or card stock

* Old magazines, catalogs, newspapers, greeting cards, etc.

* Scissors, glue stick, markers, stickers, crayons, etc.

* Envelopes if you plan to send letters (legal size)

* Stamps (postcard or first class) if you’ve got ’em

* Optional but welcome: Sass and a snack to share 💌🔥

We'll provide mailing addresses for elected officials, scripts/examples, extra cardboard, and extra stamps.

This is meant to be a THRIFTY endeavor. If cost is a concern, no need to buy anything new—just bring whatever you have around the house! On the flip side, if you're able to bring extra supplies for others, please do!

Not an *artiste* but want to support this crafty endeavor from afar? You can [make a donation here](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/warwickdemspa?refcode=mobilize) or [contact us](mailto:hello@warwickdemspa.com) to donate supplies or stamps.

events.title: IND Cobb - Board of Commissioner (BOC) Meetings
events.description:
Join our IND Cobb member liaisons who regularly attend the BOC meetings because all politics is local, and this has never been more true. Here's why you should start plugging in to local politics.

County commissioners make real decisions that affect your daily life - like taxes, law enforcement budgets, zoning, public health, and infrastructure. Yet most people never show up. Here’s why you should:

🔎 Accountability
When you’re in the room, it is harder for officials to make shady or unpopular decisions. 

🗣️ Your Voice Matters
At the local level, one person speaking up can actually shift policy. Commissioners notice when people show up - especially when they speak. But you don't have to speak. Your presence alone speaks volumes and our Democratic majority of Commissioners appreciate you making the effort to attend.

💰 They Control Your Tax Dollars
Millions in public funds are decided here. Want better services or to stop wasteful spending? This is where to start.

🔥 They Count on You Staying Home
Most meetings are empty. Your presence alone disrupts that status quo and reminds them who they work for.

🏛️ Local is Where Big Change Begins
Many bad (or good) policies start at the county level - like surveillance, book bans, or housing rules. Spot them early, and fight back locally.

August meetings:
Tues Aug 12, 9a - BOC Regular Meeting
Tues Aug 26, 7p - BOC Regular Meeting

Bottom Line:
If you don’t show up - they assume you don’t care.
Be there. Speak up. Keep them honest. Start with a Regular Meeting until you feel comfortable going to more.

events.title: IND Cobb - Board of Education (BOE) Meeting
events.description:
Join our IND Cobb School Board liaisons at the August School Board meeting.

📚 Why Attend Cobb County School Board Meetings?
Your voice matters. The school board makes decisions on school safety, budgets, curriculum, and tax millage rates - all of which impact students and families across Cobb County.

Join us to:
🔍 Ensure transparency around decisions like book removals, safety policies, and data use
💬 Speak or observe public comment sessions - especially now that they're no longer broadcasted live, so it matters even more to be in the room 
🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Show support for fair representation - Cobb’s school board map has been legally challenged for diluting Black and Latino voices 
💡 Track policy changes on DEI, student discipline, diversity programs, and more

Why your attendance makes a difference:
Even one person makes a difference. At each meeting, board members face minimal public scrutiny unless people show up. Together, we can spotlight unsafe policies, push for transparency, and hold elected officials accountable.

Be there. Be heard. Shape our children's future.

events.description:

Immigrants
Autism/Disability Community
Federal Workers -and more!

Safety tips for attending rallies in hot weather:
wear a wide brimmed hat and light colored, breathable clothing
drink plenty of water
at the first sign of heat illness (dizziness, muscle cramps, headache, nausea) move to a cooler location and slowly drink a cool beverage. Seek medical attention if you do not feel better. (WA State Dept of Health)
Your safety is our top concern. If you need assistance, please reach out to the organizers. If you are concerned about your ability to stand or walk outside during hot temperatures, please stay home!
About Indivisible Greater Vancouver (IGV)
Indivisible Greater Vancouver (IGV) is committed to promoting nonviolent advocacy and activism to create lasting social and political change. Founded in 2017 as a chapter of the national Indivisible movement to resist the Trump agenda, IGV has since expanded its focus to include local and Washington state grassroots organizing.
We work in partnership with organizations that share our values, including Clark County 50501, MoveOn Clark County, LULAC, Pasitos Gigantes, and the Vancouver chapter of the NAACP. Together, we build community power rooted in justice, equity, and solidarity.
IGV is deeply committed to nonviolence as both a principle and a strategy. We at IGV strongly believe that peaceful, nonviolent activism offers social movements the most power to effect change. Through peaceful protests, we set an example of making our voices heard with dignity, empowered by truth. IGV does not condone intimidation, threats, vandalism, interference with access to business or any other lawless actions. If instigators or opponents attempt to violate our commitment to non-violence, we will try to de-escalate and end the event if needed to maintain a safe environment.

You can read more about Indivisible’s national commitment to nonviolence here:
🔗 indivisible.org/commitment-nonviolence
We also value and are guided by the research of Dr. Erica Chenoweth, whose work shows that nonviolent movements are significantly more successful than violent ones in achieving lasting social and political transformation:
🔗 Paths to Resistance – Harvard Kennedy School
Together, we stand strong, peaceful, and resolute—because nonviolence is not passive. It is powerful.

Join Indivisible Greater Vancouver for a Banner Drop over I-5!

We’re making a bold, visible stand to defend our democracy and push back against the Trump administration’s illegal and unconstitutional actions. During peak commuting hours, we’ll raise our banners high over I-5 to show that our community is awake, united, and ready to fight for what’s right.

Starting this month, “No Troops on Our Streets” will be the focus of our weekly Banner Waving Over I-5 event.
Trump has deployed 2,000, armed National Guard troops to the streets of Washington, DC, supposedly to “fight crime.” Even though violent crime is at a 30-year low there. Even though the mayor objects to it. Even though a law says the military cannot be used to police civilians on US soil.
The troops are not stationed in the part of the city that has the most crime. They are not trained in law enforcement. And the deployment takes them away from their families, their jobs, and their normal duties of helping their states during natural disasters. It also is costing $1 million a day.
Worst of all, Trump is not really using them to fight crime. He is using them to intimidate his political opponents, to squelch dissent and to get us all used to the idea of living in a police state. And he plans to deploy more National Guard troops to 19 other states.
This is not normal, and it must be stopped.

re Board of Supervisors:

The County Board of Supervisors are elected to four-year terms and provide direction to the County Administrator and several other county departments.

The board is like the City Council, except its jurisdiction covers all the county and unincorporated areas.

Board members decide the county tax rate and approve the county budget.

The County Board of Supervisors oversees health, road, parks, libraries, law enforcement, and other municipal services. The Board also has the power to fill vacancies in the county and legislative offices, other boards and commissions, pass resolutions, and enact ordinances and regulations as authorized by state law.

The Board has the authority to make decisions on a variety of issues, such as zoning changes, resolutions, and ordinances.

Additionally, the board of supervisors has the power to remove and replace election precincts, appoint election inspectors and judges as well as canvass election returns, declare election results, and issue certificates.

events.title: Demand Your Representative Support the We the People Amendment (H.J.Res.54)
events.description:
**Corporate money is corrupting our democracy, and our lawmakers know it.**

For decades, billionaires, lobbyists, and big business have bought access and influence while everyday people are ignored. Through a combination of court rulings like Citizens United and unchecked loopholes, our political system has become rigged in favor of the ultra-wealthy.

The We the People Amendment (H.J.Res.54) is a bold, constitutional solution to take our government back.

For years, Congress has failed to rein in big money, hiding behind weak bills and partisan gridlock. The Supreme Court opened the floodgates with atrocious decisions like Citizens United, and our lawmakers have done next to nothing to stop it.

This amendment pulls no punches. It:
- Declares that constitutional rights belong only to human beings, not artificial entities, including corporations and PACs
- Establishes that money is not speech, giving the people the power to regulate campaign spending
- Requires full transparency of all political expenditures—no more dark money, no more secrets

This amendment is backed by a massive majority of Americans across party lines—**more than 80%**. But Congress continues to delay, deflect, and protect the very system that enriches them. **We the people are fed up.**

**That’s where you come in.**

We're building a movement to demand change and to hold every lawmaker accountable who stands in the way. Use this form to send a powerful message to your elected officials demanding they cosponsor, publicly support, and advance H.J.Res.54. **It takes just one minute to make your voice heard, but the impact is real.**

**We're done waiting. Flood their inboxes. Flood the streets. Let’s take our country back.**

events.title: Rally to Protect Democracy--Congressman Joyce, How Bad Are You Going to Let This Get?
events.description:
Come and join members of Ohio District 14 as we stand together to protest the harmful actions of the Trump Administration. We gather every Friday from 10-11:30 along Mentor Avenue in Eleanor Garfield Park to say that we do not approve of Donald Trump tearing families and communities apart by forcibly removing and inhumanely detaining non-dangerous immigrants in our communities.  We do not approve of Trump's plan to cut funding for vital programs like Medicaid and Snap.  We do not approve of Donald Trump's giving 4.5 trillion in tax breaks to his wealthy friends.  Trump said he was not going to implement Project 2025, but it is nearly 50% complete.

https://www.project2025.observer/en

We have reached out to Congressman Dave Joyce with our concerns about the harm of the Trump Administration, but we have not heard back with specific and reassuring responses.

Congressman Joyce, we want you to stand up for the health, wellbeing, and safety of your constituents. Please come and join us. We need your help saying "NO" to the harmful behavior of the Trump administration.  HOW BAD ARE YOU WILLING TO LET THIS GET???

Attendees: Please bring friends and family and family-friendly signs.

Feel free to bring a chair, and join for any amount of time you are able. Please park in the lower lot and walk up the hill to our protest site if you are able. Leave the upper lot open for elders and families with young children. Please do not park on the grass as vendors need to set up in this area for the Mentor Farmers Market.

If you are able, please bring non-expired food and personal care items to donate to our local food pantries. Food items include canned proteins, peanut butter and jelly, canned fruits and vegetable, and shelf stable food items such as grains, pasta, and cereal. Personal care items include hand soap, toilet paper, tissues, paper towels, tampons, and diapers.  Food pantries are experiencing federal and state level funding cuts.

A core principle behind all events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants not to engage with drivers, passers-by, and counter protestors who have different ideas than ours and show this unkindly. We will not return the hurt and anger. We have an opportunity to show kindness and bridge the divide. Let's take this opportunity. Our nation needs this.

This event is hosted by Ohio District 14 Partners--A coalition of pro-democracy groups in Ohio District 14.  

***Note--Why is this event on a Friday?  This event used to be held in front of the building that houses Congressman Joyce's office--8500 Station St., The Matchworks Building. We used to enter the building in small groups to talk with the staff members in the Congressman's office while others protested on the sidewalk in front of the building. Our group grew from 3 people to 60 people in 8 weeks. We were not permitted to park in the lot in large numbers, so we decided to move to Eleanor Garfield Park.

Individuals are permitted to park and enter the Matchworks Building to talk to staff members in the Congressman's Office on the third floor on M-F from 9-5. We strongly encourage you to do this. This action is a great way to protect and improve democracy.

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

What is NVDA [Non-Violent Direct Action]
What a marshal is and why they matter
How to cork intersections and control flow
Leapfrogging techniques to support mobile protests/marches
De-escalation tips and safety awareness
Signal App 101 for secure group communication
How to support accessibility and inclusion on the ground

Our communities in the 9th District deserve to be heard.

That’s why we launched Show Up / Speak Out, a weekly campaign to deliver letters and petitions, share our stories, stand up for our communities, and demand action from our legislators. **Congressman Dan Meuser has gone far too long without being held accountable to his constituents, but we’re not going to let him get away with that anymore.** 

📣 If we can’t get in the door, we’ll make our voices heard outside.

✊ Whether constituents get a visit or it’s strictly a protest with a purpose, we’ll be there — every week.

🗓️ Fridays from 3pm to 4pm – Outside Congressman Dan Meuser’s office (330 Pine Street - Williamsport, PA 17701). Moving forward, we’ll be there – same time/same place – every week.

🏢 We’re gathering outside Meuser’s office, but it’s about more than any one elected official. It’s about holding our representatives accountable at the federal, state, AND local level and fighting for what we deserve.

**This is what democracy looks like here in northeastern PA - we show up and we speak out.**

We’re excited to work alongside Williamsport 50501 for Fight Back Fridays! Action Together NEPA is proud to host these actions as part of the Pennsylvanians Together coalition, working together to create a commonwealth where we all can thrive, not just survive. events.title: Whittier Indivisible Chapter Weekly Strategy Meeting
events.description:
Come one, come all! We are the Whittier Indivisible Chapter, and we meet weekly on Zoom to discuss, share, plan, and listen. We engage in local, in-person efforts in our community as well as national initiatives. The majority of our members are from surrounding cities in addition to Whittier, CA. 

This a local Indivisible event! We strictly abide by and follow Indivisible leadership and protocol, and do not tolerate any behavior that is disrespectful, discriminating, or hateful in any way. 

Whittier Indivisible is a Southern California-based grassroots group committed to defending democracy, resisting authoritarianism, and standing up for the dignity and rights of all people—documented or undocumented. Rooted in Whittier and welcoming to all from surrounding communities, we are proudly pro-immigrant and oppose ICE overreach, racism, and any policy that dehumanizes or divides. We advocate for social and economic justice, environmental protection, and individual freedoms, while standing firmly against fascism and authoritarianism in all forms. events.title: The Problem with Plastic by Judith Enck: an Author Talk [Livable Future LIVE]
events.description:
Join us for a virtual conversation between **Food & Water Watch Founder and Executive Director Wenonah Hauter** and **Judith Enck**, author of *The Problem with Plastic: How We Can Save Ourselves and Our Planet Before It’s Too Late*.

*The Problem with Plastic* examines this material, first celebrated for its innovation and now recognized for its devastating environmental and public health impacts. This compelling narrative reveals how plastic pollution contributes to poisoned oceans, polluted air, a warming planet, and overwhelming waste, particularly affecting marginalized communities, which bear the brunt of petrochemical pollution. The book highlights the pervasive presence of microplastics in the environment and the human body, challenging the belief that recycling can solve the crisis.

More than a critique, *The Problem with Plastic* emphasizes the urgent need for action against plastic’s toxic legacy. It highlights powerful stories of frontline resistance in places like Louisiana, Texas, and Appalachia, and equips readers with practical tools — including a “Household Waste Audit” to track and reduce plastic consumption, as well as model policy guides for driving legislative change.

Urgent, eye-opening, and ultimately empowering, *The Problem with Plastic* reminds us: plastic is a problem — but together, we can be the solution.

Judith Enck is the founder and president of Beyond Plastics, whose goal is to eliminate plastic pollution everywhere. In 2009, she was appointed by President Obama to serve as regional administrator at the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and served as Deputy Secretary for the Environment in the New York Governor’s Office. She is currently a professor at Bennigton College, where she teaches classes on plastic pollution.

events.title: The Underground: LIVE FREE California Statewide Organizing Huddle
events.description:
# The Underground: LIVE FREE California Statewide Organizing Huddle  
## Gather. Plot. Move.  

The Underground is where California comes to **plot repair, representation, and power.**  

**Thursdays at 7 PM PT**, this statewide huddle brings communities together in rhythm:  

- **Repair** → The fight for real repair: land, housing, education, dignity, and the policies that make them real.  
- **Representation** → More than one election—this is about voice, maps, votes, and defending democracy itself.  
- **Training** → From pulpits to campuses to neighborhoods, we sharpen skills and multiply actions until they echo statewide.  

## Join LIVE FREE CA for The Underground: Statewide Organizing Huddle

**Every first Thursday · 7 PM PT · Zoom (Statewide)**  
Register once → [livefreeusa.org/events](https://www.livefreeusa.org/events)

Join **LIVE FREE CA** for **The Underground** — our statewide huddle where we turn moments into movements.

Every first Thursday, communities across California come together to meet the moment, build power, and move for repair, representation, and justice. The Underground is where faith leaders, organizers, and neighbors align around what’s happening now and how we act together.

Our rhythm is simple and powerful: **Ground → Educate → Act.**  
**Ground** in truth, reflection, and the stories that root us in community.  
**Educate** through training and awareness—tools, definitions, and analysis that connect lived experience to systems change.  
**Act** together in real time—taking collective steps that show what organized people can do.

Everything we do centers three pillars:  
**Repair. Representation. Power.**

**Repair** means care, safety, and economic dignity in our communities.  
**Representation** means voice, visibility, and civic participation.  
**Power** means organizing people, resources, and ideas to transform systems at their root.

**Bring two people. Take two actions.**  
Register to join us.

events.title: The Autonomy Project: Reproductive Rights Crash Course

sponsor.name: Planned Parenthood of Tennessee and North Mississippi

events.description:
How can we advocate for reproductive freedom if we don’t truly understand it?

This 4-month series, designed for young adults (high school through college age), gives participants the knowledge and tools to better understand their bodies, identities, and rights. Meeting twice a month, we’ll explore topics like consent, birth control, STIs, healthy relationships, and advocacy for reproductive freedom. 

Every session is queer-inclusive, interactive, and focused on building both personal autonomy and community power. Sign up for any session or all the sessions!

Oct 6 – Holistic Sexuality -
Explore sexuality as more than just sex—how it connects to identity, values, relationships, and overall well-being.

Oct 20 – STIs & Safer Sex -
Learn the facts about sexually transmitted infections, how to protect yourself and your partners, and where to get testing and care.

Nov 3 – Birth Control & Pregnancy Options -
Understand the range of birth control methods and the options available if someone becomes pregnant.

Nov 17 – A Queer New World -
Celebrate LGBTQ+ identities, history, and culture while discussing inclusive approaches to sex and relationships.

Dec 1 – Consent, Boundaries, & Supportive Relationships -
Practice how to set, respect, and communicate boundaries in healthy, safe, and affirming ways. Identify the qualities of supportive friendships, family dynamics, and romantic relationships—and how to build them.

Dec 15 –  Reproductive Justice - You’ll learn how the movement began, who led it, and how it connects to today’s fight for health equity and bodily autonomy. Together, we’ll explore key moments and voices that shaped the ongoing struggle for reproductive freedom and justice.

Jan 12 – How to Talk About Abortion -
Break down myths, stigma, and facts about abortion and practice how to have open, respectful conversations.

Jan 26 –  Community Organizing 101 -
Discover the basics of community organizing and advocacy—how to use your voice and take action for change.

events.title: Conozca Sus Derechos (Know Your Rights, Spanish)
events.description:
# ¡TODOS TENEMOS DERECHOS!

## Seas ciudadano o no, la ley te protege.

Únete a nosotros el **18 de Septiembre** a las **6PM EST** en una capacitación gratuita para:

- Conocer tus derechos frente a oficiales de inmigración (en casa, en la calle o en un vehículo).
- Aprender cómo protegerte y preparar a tu familia.
- Informarte sobre las nuevas leyes en Florida que afectan a nuestra comunidad.

 En Florida, todos los condados firmaron _acuerdos 287(g)_ con ICE, lo que significa que la policía local puede actuar como agentes de inmigración incluso en paradas de tráfico. Además, nuevas leyes aumentan las penas contra inmigrantes y limitan el acceso a la educación para estudiantes indocumentados.

Pero no estamos solos. Al informarnos y compartir este conocimiento, podemos cuidarnos entre todos.

En este taller recibirás una Guía de Conozca Sus Derechos (KYR) clara y práctica para protegerte y apoyar a tu comunidad.

events.description:

events.title: Clay County Weekend of Action: Vote-by-Mail Phone Bank
events.description:
Join the Florida Democratic Party for our **Statewide Weekend of Action** to help Clay County as we continue our year-round effort to reconnect with Democratic voters and help them stay vote-ready.

**Note: You’re not expected to make calls for the entire shift. The listed time just shows when phone banking is available. Feel free to hop on and make calls anytime during that window, for however long you’re able.** ☺️

No experience necessary—just a willingness to make a difference. We’ll provide the training and support you need.

As of January 1, more than 1.2 million Democrats have been removed from Florida’s Vote-by-Mail rolls. During this phonebank, we’ll contact voters who had a mail ballot in 2024 but haven’t yet re-enrolled helping them take the steps to stay on track for future elections.

This is how we strengthen our grassroots infrastructure and build momentum for the elections ahead.

events.title: Freedom Fridays and Stand For All Wilson

address_lines: Raleigh Road Parkway West & Airport Boulevard Northwest

events.description:
Join us every Friday 3:30 to 5 at the Intersection of Raleigh Road Parkway W and Airport Boulevard in Wilson, NC.  

Our events are peaceful, positive, and nonviolent, and open to Democrats, Independents, Republicans and anyone else. We are standing up for human rights and to protect our democracy. And since we are here to promote unity in our community, diversity, equality, inclusion, and social justice, please bring positive signs!  

Some examples of positive signs are: Instead of "Stop defunding science,” say “Protect research funding.” Instead of "Stop fascism,” say "Save our democracy.” Other ideas are: “Protect Medicaid,” “SNAP feeds kids,” “Justice for All,” “No ICE,” etc. Make signs about what you're standing up for -- whether that is SNAP, Due Process, VA Rights, Medicaid, DEI, healthcare, women’s rights, LGBTQIA+, etc. Please no mocking signs and no swastikas as we aim to create an inclusive and welcoming environment for all. 
Bring a chair, bring a flag, or bring a sign!  Simply show up when you can if only for a few minutes!  I love that when it happens!  
Signing up helps me to connect with you if a change occurs such as last minute change of plans due to weather.  And sign up to stay updated because we will be rotating corners in the future and to keep you updated on holiday plans. Thanks. 

We started these demonstrations July 18 and we heard you Wilson!  I heard some people in Smithfield want to join us Nov 21!  How great is that?  Smithfield, Rocky Mount, Elm City, Sims, Greenville and towns in between, grab a friend and come Stand For All with us!  And start your own hometown demonstrations!  I have some resources to help get you started. It’s fun and getting better every Friday!  

We are standing up for human rights because no one deserves to live in fear and no one deserves to be denied rights. Individually, we can’t campaign on everything we wish were different, but together we are strong!  
Keep doing what you are doing because it matters and stand with us because it’s fun!  You will meet people like yourself who care, are concerned and are making a BIG difference in Wilson!  

We are a nonpartisan grassroots group of individuals most of whom live in Wilson, NC who love going to peaceful demonstrations and standing up for human rights. We hope to empower more folks in our hometown to stand up and speak up. Check us out. Meet us at the corner on Friday. We are a growing and we invite you to stand with us on the corner or for brainstorming stuff on what matters to you!  
What matters to you?  Let us know. We want to hear you. 

Thank you.  


Stand For All Wilson is on fb. It’s a private group but you can ask to join: 

https://www.facebook.com/share/g/1JR4kL3VAs/?mibextid=wwXIfr

Follow me, Becca Warren, on Facebook: 
https://www.facebook.com/share/1BAowZSrsG/?mibextid=wwXIfr

**You are not alone!** Join your community members every week in a peaceful, pet & family-friendly grassroots rally for solidarity against tyranny, supporting all of Orange County and adjacent areas, hosted by **[50501 Movement Orange County](https://linktr.ee/50501oc)** and **[OC Indivisible Coalition](https://linktr.ee/ocindivisiblecoalition)** (not affiliated with any political party).

They are betting on your silence. They are counting on your inaction. Prove them wrong!

### This Week's Theme ###

#### Sunday, November 30 ####
Weekly Rally for Democracy
Boycott Billionaires: Say NO to Cyber Monday!

### Mutual Aid Food & Essentials Drive ###

Requested items include:

- cereal, pasta, rice, beans
- sugar, salt, oil, flour, coffee
- canned food, bottled water
- soap, body wash, shampoo
- toothbrushes, toothpaste, deodorant
- toilet paper & paper towels
- dish & laundry detergent
- menstrual care products
- baby diapers and wipes

### What to bring: ###

- Your voices  
- Your friends  
- Water & snacks  
- Sunscreen  
- Signs (optional; a sign-making station is available with free materials and inspiration)

### More Info ###

For those who need a place to sit, there are multiple benches available outside the City Hall building, or bring a folding chair. Marching/walking optional. Parking is available at City Hall as well as at Bill Barber Park.

The event will take place rain or shine. Please check the weather forecast in advance and prepare accordingly for rain or heat, bringing items such as umbrellas, fans, personal misters, or extra water as needed. Participants are responsible for assessing their own health conditions and taking appropriate precautions. Those joining the event do so at their own discretion and assume responsibility for their personal well-being.

Remember, your right to protest is covered under the First Amendment. No permit is required for this gathering. Please do not disrupt traffic.

events.title: Woodrow Wilson Birthday Association of Cumberland County 100th Year
events.description:
You Are Cordially Invited  to the 100th Anniversary Celebration of the
Woodrow Wilson Birthday Association of Cumberland County

Sunday, December 7, 2025
12:00 – 3:00 PM
West Shore Elks, 108 N. St. Johns Church Rd., Camp Hill, PA 

Join us in commemorating a century of reflection, scholarship, and civic tradition as we mark the 100th anniversary of the last remaining Woodrow Wilson Birthday Association in the United States.

This milestone event will feature the nationally recognized speaker, Richard Striner, Ph.D. Professor Striner is the author of over a dozen books. Several of his books were about presidents - Wilson, Lincoln, and Eisenhower. He also taught history at Washington College in Chestertown, MD, for thirty years, during which time he received numerous accolades for his teaching. Professor Striner lives near Annapolis, MD.

The event will also include the presentation of the Association’s Student Essay Contest winners on the topic of “Woodrow Wilson, A Mixed Legacy”.

A buffet lunch will be served for $35/person with a cash bar available. The buffet menu will feature:

    Stuffed chicken
    String Beans
    Scalloped Potatoes
    Vegetarian Lasagna
    Salad
    Seasonal Desserts

Host-level patrons will be recognized in the Program:

    White House level - $300 includes 3 tickets
    Princeton level - $200 includes 2 tickets
    Staunton level - $100 includes 1 ticket

Please RSVP before December 1 by mailing your check made payable to The Woodrow Wilson Birthday Association of Cumberland County, to Charlie Wilson, 226 N. 27th St., Camp Hill, PA 17011. Alternatively, you may hand-deliver cash or check and place it in the mail slot. Sorry only cash or checks accepted. For questions,  email  Charlie Wilson at arundelynn@gmail.com.

events.title: We the People Believe in Democracy and Justice for All
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Join us on Saturdays 12pm-2pm to Stand Out and Up with your signs of protest and support. As a small and passionate community, this high visibility location is very impactful and fulfilling. Meet fellow citizens to join your voice in Solidarity and for Justice.

Hosted by: Hopkinton resident, a small and growing group of local and concerned Massachusetts citizens who live in Hopkinton and surrounding towns. Our mission is to build trust and relationships between local communities as we face the growing risks of:

Rising authoritarianism, bigotry and hate. The erosion of civil liberties - no due process. The worsening economy with fewer jobs. Climate change and health crisis.

Remember to bring water and hat It gets hot out here!

It's best to park around The Common to then stand at the Spirit of the Boston Marathon Statue & Start Line, 93 East Main Street, Hopkinton.

Here are some important ground rules. We cannot disrupt traffic. Please stay out of the street, and always use crosswalks. This is a peaceful protest. If someone becomes aggressive towards one of us, we should all be ready to de-escalate the situation (don't respond to the aggressor, walk away and if necessary, get support from the Hopkinton Police). Please look out for each other. The Hopkinton Police has been notified of event, and they support our right to PEACEFULLY protest. Thank you. 

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

events.description:
**We are back again this year for the last time as your State House Representative for the 73rd Annual Winter Park Christmas Parade on Saturday, December 6th from 8:15am to 10:30am!**

Join your favorite state lawmaker, Representative Dr. Anna V. Eskamani, with silver bells as we take the streets of Winter Park in this seasonal tradition dedicated to all things merry. We will be decking the halls of Park Avenue with cheer as we head into the holidays!

events.title: Beyond the Headlines: Engaging Domestic Violence Offenders to Prevent Future Violence
events.description:
Last year, gun homicides dropped across Pennsylvania--except in one area. Domestic violence.
When a firearm enters a domestic violence situation, the risk of homicide increases by five fold. But what happens before that moment? Often, domestic violence doesn't start with a firearm--it escalates over time. Juan Carlos Arean has worked for years with domestic violent offenders, examining the intersection between fatherhood and the violence, to break the cycle before it becomes deadly.

His work around intervening with those who used domestic violence has launched new programs, and influenced existing programs like the violence intervention program at Women’s Center & Shelter of Greater Pittsburgh. Join CeaseFirePA's next Beyond the Headlines Webinar for a conversation between Juan and the Center's CEO, and CeaseFirePA Board Member, Nicole Molinaro.

At the end, we'll provide a short update on policy solutions moving in the General Assembly to prevent future domestic violence with firearms across Pennsylvania.

events.title: 13th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence
events.description:
Each year since 2013, the Newtown Action Alliance Foundation (NAAF), the charitable arm of the Newtown Action Alliance (NAA), and numerous partners in the gun violence prevention community have sponsored the National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence on or near the anniversary of the Sandy Hook shooting tragedy. These multidenominational events, held in Washington, D.C., at the National Cathedral and St. Mark’s Episcopal Church, bring together survivors of gun violence, victims’ family members, concerned citizens, faith leaders, lawmakers, leaders of gun violence prevention organizations, and activists from across the nation. 

The 13th Annual National Vigil for All Victims of Gun Violence will be held in person on Wednesday, December 10, 2025 from 7-9:30pm ET at St Marks Episcopal Church on Capitol Hill, Washington, D.C. 

The national vigil service in D.C. will anchor the #FreedomToLive Nationwide Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence Vigils/Events to #EndGunViolence in communities across the nation. We encourage all to host a local event - of any size or type. 

December 14, 2025 is the 13-year mark of the Sandy Hook tragedy. By this December, 1.3 million Americans will be killed or injured by guns since the Sandy Hook shooting tragedy. We urge you to join the gun violence prevention community in our collective effort to continue to shine a light on the devastating epidemic of gun violence in our nation until these gun deaths and injuries are reduced. 

The victims, survivors and the families impacted by gun violence are often forgotten. Therefore, the Newtown Action Alliance Foundation and the Newtown Action Alliance, in partnership with 160+ organizations will host the annual national vigil service of mourning and loving remembrance for all who have fallen victim to the ongoing epidemic of gun violence in America. 

The theme of this year’s vigil is #FreedomToLive—the simple, powerful idea that every person deserves to live free from the daily threat of gunfire. Together, survivors, families, advocates, and allies will raise our voices to ensure that FREEDOM means the right of every person to live, learn, work, worship, speak, vote, and gather without the daily fear of gun violence.

Please visit our website for more information: https://www.newtownactionalliancefoundation.org/national-vigil-for-all-victims-of-gun-violence.

events.title: Citizen Civics Club
events.description:
# Citizen Civics – First Tuesdays  

Hosted by **Rage for Democracy**, *Citizen Civics* is a monthly community meetup where neighbors come together to talk about the issues that shape our democracy.  

Each month we follow a simple, open format:  
1. **Announcements** – updates on local events and actions  
2. **Questions** – space for civic and community questions  
3. **Topic Discussion** – a focused conversation on a key civic theme *(this month: The First Amendment)*  

This isn’t a lecture, it’s a conversation. Whether you’re new to civic engagement or already active, your voice matters here. Together we can learn, share, and build stronger connections in our community.  


*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Florida NOW Screening: Paris Is Burning
events.description:
Paris Is Burning is a 1990 American documentary film directed by Jennie Livingston. Filmed in the mid-to-late 1980s, it chronicles the ball culture of New York City and the African-American, Latino, gay and transgender communities involved in it.

Critics consider the film to be an invaluable documentary of the end of the “Golden Age” of New York City drag balls, and a thoughtful exploration of race, class, gender and sexuality in America.

In 2016, the film was selected for preservation in the United States National Film Registry by the Library of Congress as being “culturally, historically or aesthetically significant”.

We’ll follow the screening with a community discussion on how the legacies of ball culture continue to shape struggles for liberation, visibility, joy, and self-determination today.

events.title: Reunión Mensual Comunitaria de MamásConPoder / MomsRising
events.description:
¡Al fin! El cierre del gobierno más largo de la historia de Estados Unidos ha terminado y lo sobrevivimos… a duras penas. 

Y ahora, ¿qué sigue? 

¡Estamos en la temporada de inscripción abierta de los seguros de salud! Es una época muy especial del año (es decir, llena de ansiedad) en la que seleccionamos los planes de seguro de salud y calculamos cuánto serán nuestras primas. Por eso, es imprescindible que asistas a la próxima reunión en Zoom. 

Estamos encantadas de anunciar que la líder Stacey Abrams participará en la llamada del jueves 20 de noviembre para explicar lo que significan los recientes cambios en la atención médica para todos nosotros y cómo podemos unirnos para luchar para proteger una atención médica económicamente accesible. 

Sí, el cierre del gobierno ha terminado, pero para muchas familias todavía hay mucha incertidumbre financiera, especialmente en lo que respecta a su atención médica. El reciente proyecto de ley de asignaciones del Congreso no extendió los créditos fiscales mejorados para atención médica de los que dependían muchas personas (¡millones de personas!), dejándolas sin saber cómo navegar el periodo de inscripción abierta. Como resultado, **se espera que aumente el precio de las primas de seguro (¡más del doble!) para millones de personas y que muchas personas no puedan pagarlas, haciendo que se queden sin cobertura.** 

Demasiadas personas están en peligro de perder su atención médica asequible, en especial las personas de la clase trabajadora, de las comunidades inmigrantes y de los hogares que tienen un solo padre de familia. 

¡Salvamos la atención médica en el pasado y es hora de movilizarnos de nuevo por nuestras familias! ¡Asiste a nuestra reunión comunitaria en Zoom este jueves 20 de noviembre a las 8:30 pm ET/5:30 pm PT! Confirma tu asistencia a esta reunión comunitaria en línea ahora.

En esta reunión virtual podrás:

- Tener la excepcional oportunidad de escuchar directamente a la líder Abrams que ha estado en el frente de batalla de la lucha por el acceso a atención médica y de la defensa de nuestras comunidades. 

- Conocer lo que puede significar la expiración de los subsidios de salud federales para las primas y la cobertura de millones de familias.

- Escuchar a expertos y a importantes defensores hablar de lo que puede hacer el Congreso para tomar medidas inmediatas; conectar en comunidad sobre cómo entrar en acción y saber cómo puedes hacer que tu gente se involucre después de la reunión. 
 
- ¡Encontrar formas de compartir tu historia! Cada historia fortalece nuestro movimiento.  

¡Por favor, envía este mensaje a todas las personas que conozcas y que estén listas para entrar en acción y fortalecer el poder para los tiempos difíciles que tenemos por delante y pídeles que también asistan a la reunión!

Juntos podemos crear un futuro más brillante y optimista. ¿Puedes acompañarnos? 


**Este evento se realizará en inglés y tendremos interpretación simultánea al español disponible.


-------------------------------------
*************************************
-------------------------------------

Estamos organizándonos para construir un futuro mejor. ¿Puedes ayudarnos? 

**El cuarto jueves de cada mes,** mamás, padres de familia, proveedores de cuidados y familias de toda la nación se reunirán virtualmente en las reuniones comunitarias mensuales de MomsRising/MamásConPoder. Cada mes exploraremos un tema distinto; escucharemos a invitados especiales expertos, a líderes y a defensores; celebraremos las victorias y la esperanza, nos informaremos, organizaremos y entraremos en acción.

Es hora de que todos nos pongamos manos a la obra. Necesitamos que todos se unan, informen y den pasos significativos para proteger a nuestras comunidades, a nuestras instituciones y a nuestra economía. Estas reuniones son para más que compartir información, son para fortalecer el poder, la comunidad y la esperanza. Porque cuando nos unimos somos poderosos.

**Levantémonos juntos. ¡Confirma tu asistencia ahora para acompañarnos! Incluso te puedes inscribir para participar varios meses seleccionando varias fechas.**

¡Por favor, comparte esto con todas las personas que conozcas que estén listas para entrar en acción y para fortalecer el poder para los tiempos difíciles que tenemos por delante y pídeles que también asistan a la reunión!

Juntos podemos crear un futuro más brillante y optimista. 

**Este evento se realizará en inglés y tendremos disponible interpretación simultánea en español.**

events.title: Indivisible LT Monthly Meeting

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Work with others to stand up for democracy and resist fascism. Our times call for concerted, communal, and local action. Come to our monthly meeting to connect and get involved!

Indivisible is a national movement of thousands of group leaders and more than a million members taking regular, iterative, and increasingly complex actions to resist the GOPs agenda, elect local champions, and fight for progressive policies.

Lancaster Together is one of several local chapters. Each chapter has its own flavor and we all work together on bigger projects. You can join any or all of them -- whatever works best for you. Our chapter meeting is in East Hempfield and many members live in Lancaster City, Lancaster Township, and parts south and west, although we welcome anyone from any part of the county.

We organize protests and rallies, hold our elected officials to account, speak up and support those who can't, and most of all, work together with other Indivisible chapters and mission-aligned local and national partners to increase our impact. All of our activity is meant to spread awareness and make change happen.

Most of our day-to-day work takes place OUTSIDE of our monthly meeting. You can start a new project right away, or join an existing effort. But the meeting is the best way to meet everyone and see what your role can be. We use it to update, connect, onboard, discuss, and decide. We also promise it will last only ONE hour.

##Here are five things to know about our grassroots organization:

- **We Are Indivisible** We are stronger in unity. We emphasize partnerships and collaboration to stand in solidarity with those most affected by right-wing policies, while also seeking to build awareness about and change those policies.

- **Strong Leaders, Strong Groups, Strong Movement** Indivisible is decentralized, fostering leadership at the local level. Our volunteers can lead and take independent action, while coordinating with national campaigns for maximum impact.

- **Inside/Outside Strategy** We engage with existing political structures while simultaneously applying pressure from the outside. This dual approach involves working within systems like Congress while mobilizing grassroots pressure on elected officials to advance progressive goals.

- **A Virtuous Cycle of Advocacy and Elections** We believe in electing progressive candidates and progressive policies. We hold our elected officials to account and work to elect progressive candidates who can resist tyranny and promote democracy.

- **A Real Democracy** The organization is driven by a vision of a democracy that serves everyone. We aim to defeat right-wing political agendas and build an inclusive democracy that reflects the needs and values of all people.

- **Nonviolence** A core principle behind all Indivisible activity is a commitment to nonviolence.

*If these principles align with your values, please join us!*

events.title: No Kings Westfield Weekly Standout
events.description:
Note: during DST you can join us starting at 3PM!

We vigil every Tuesday in Park Square until someone takes the oath of Presidential office who does not seek to be a king!


### Our Commitment
No Kings Westfield is committed to peaceful, lawful resistance. We defend democracy through the power of organized community action, not confrontation.

### Core Principles
  - Non-violent resistance is strategically effective

  - De-escalation protects our movement, our community, and our message

  - Peaceful persistence builds the broad coalition needed for lasting change

### At Events

  - Remain calm and composed, even when provoked

  - Do not engage with counter-protesters or hecklers

  - If tensions arise, step back and find an organizer

  - Our strength comes from disciplined unity, not individual reactions

  - Remember: we're modeling the democracy we seek to protect

### Why This Matters

Research shows non-violent movements are twice as likely to succeed as violent ones. Every act of discipline strengthens our cause and our community.

### If Confronted

"We're here peacefully exercising our constitutional rights to defend democracy. Thank you for your concern."

  Questions or concerns? Contact an organizer immediately.

### We stand out in Westfield:

To show our neighbors they are not alone

To show our neighbors we will not be silent in the face of authoritarianism

To build community and resiliency with existing organizations

All are welcome. Please refrain from profanity on signs.

Tyler Minton with OKC Democratic Socialists of America. Tyler Minton was born and raised in Oklahoma, where his family has resided since before statehood. He graduated from Kingfisher High School as a National Merit Scholar and state champion in policy debate, a passion which he carried with him into his time as a Philosophy student at the University of Oklahoma and competitor on the national champion Shannon Self Policy Debate team, as well as through almost two decades of coaching and youth development. events.description:
We will be knocking doors in Eagan to talk to voters about what issues are on their minds, how we can best advocate for them as we head into the midterms, and whether they'd be interested in joining us by getting involved with the local DFL party. This is not traditional door knocking where we're encouraging people to support a specific candidate, but these conversations are crucial as we start to build capacity for our BLUE WAVE next year!

A brief (~20 min) training is provided and new canvassers will always be paired with someone more experienced, so don't fear if you've never knocked doors before! We also have water, sunscreen, and snacks on hand. Door knocking is typically a 1.5-2 hour commitment.

It may seem silly, but studies have shown that knocking on doors and meeting voters directly is one of the most effective ways to ensure that people stay engaged in their communities and vote in elections. We hope to see you there!
