events.title: Join Us for a Broccoli Glean ~ Hastings, FL 🥦
events.description:
We will be gleaning broccoli at Smith Farms!

Join us for a Society of St. Andrew Gleaning Event, where we’ll glean fresh produce for families in need. It’s a hands-on way to give back, enjoy the outdoors, and share in meaningful community service.

📅 Date: Mondays Beginning Jan 12th, 2026
⏰ Time: 9 am - 12 noon 
📍 Location: Smith Farm

🌱 What to Bring:

✅ Closed-toe shoes (required)

✅ Comfortable clothing that can get messy

✅ Hat, sunscreen, and gloves (optional but helpful)

✅ A reusable water bottle to stay hydrated


### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

#### 1. What is gleaning?

- Gleaning is collecting leftover crops from farms that would otherwise go to waste. These fresh fruits and vegetables are then donated to food banks and hunger relief groups.

#### 2. Who can attend?

- All are welcome—no prior experience needed! Perfect for families, small groups, or anyone looking to serve. (Kids must be with an adult.)

#### 3. Are tools provided?
- Yes! We’ll supply any tools and bags you’ll need to glean.

#### 4. What if it rains?

- We’ll monitor the weather and let you know if anything changes. Safety first!

#### 5. Where does the food go?

- All the produce goes directly to local food banks and community partners feeding those in need.

#### 6. How can I stay in the loop?

- For event updates, visit: https://www.mobilize.us/endhunger/

#### 7. Other FAQs :

- NO smoking, NO pets
Please note- there will not be any restrooms right at the field. Please plan accordingly.

📢 Questions? 
Contact:
Megan McEwen
📞 (863) 224-0403
📧 fl-glean@endhunger.org

events.title: Virtual Meeting with Indivisible Baltimore County
events.description:
Join us for our monthly virtual meeting!

Indivisible Baltimore County (IBC) is affiliated with the national Indivisible organization and shares its mission to elect progressive leaders, rebuild our democracy, and counter harmful policies that threaten our values.

IBC is a progressive, grassroots organization committed to peaceful civic engagement and collaboration with like-minded organizations and individuals. Our core aims include:

- responsive and accountable government at all levels,
- social, environmental and economic justice,
- policies and laws that promote and protect the rights of all people,
- defending democracy and the rights of every individual as written in the Constitution, and
- electing officials qualified for their roles and committed to making real, immediate, and concrete improvements in people’s lives.

We meet twice a month: 2nd Saturday on Zoom, and 4th Saturday in-person and sponsor multiple opportunities a month to engage with members.

Indivisible Baltimore County does not collect dues and exclusively relies on donations to support members in their pro-democracy actions.

Visit our website for more information at https://www.indivisible-baltimorecounty.org

Indivisible Baltimore County supports and exercises the constitutional right to peaceful assembly and free expression. We do not condone violence, property damage, or actions that interfere with public safety. Each individual is responsible for their own conduct.

events.description:
Join us on the first Wednesday of each month virtually at 8-9pm for group updates, upcoming protests and events, volunteering opportunities and community building.

Our group name is transitioning to Appalachian Edge Ohio Indivisible and will be fully transitioned by October 30th as well as our community events and activities group.

Edit: It seems to be some folks are confused on what kind of group we are and we are a resistance group fighting to save democracy. We are a resistance group against the Trump Regime. You can find more on the main Indivisble page indivisible.org or our website as well. Hope this helps and clears some things up. Join the resistance and if you also don’t think the Democratic Party is doing what they should be for us, you should be attending their meetings and having your voice heard there as well. Thank you and hope to see you at a meeting or the protests.

events.description:
Ready to turn your passion into action? Join the ACLU of Indiana in it's people-led popular education training - Organizing to Protect Democracy.

This session offers a free, high impact, in-person training that is built to ignite your activism and give you the tools to organize, mobilize, and lead in this critical moment. Our communities need bold action, and we need you in the fight. 

You'll learn how to: 

-Organize effectively in your community. 
-Have persuasive conversations that move people to action. 
-Build lasting connections with others who are ready to rise to the moment. 

Space is limited, so sign up now to reserve your spot. All we ask is that you commit to attend and share info about this training with friends and family. Organizing is relational, and the path forward depends on all of us. 

Now is the moment to stand up for our democracy, so join us for this training and be part of the movement for change.

WHEN: Saturday, December 6, 2025 ALL DAY

RSVP NOW and Join us!

events.title: Community Pumpkin Smash at Cottonwood Urban Farm
events.description:
Don’t Let Your Pumpkin Haunt the Landfill!

Each year, around 1.3 billion pounds of pumpkins in the U.S. are sent to landfills after Halloween, where they release harmful methane gas that contributes to global warming. 

Don’t toss your Halloween pumpkins in the trash, bring them to our Pumpkin Smash! Join us for our Annual Pumpkin Smash on November 29th, 2025, from 9 AM - 12 PM at Cottonwood Urban Farm. Smash, chop, or break your pumpkin and add it to our compost piles. You’ll cut down on landfill waste and give your pumpkin the chance to return to the Earth!

### What to Expect

-  At this event, it is encouraged to BYOP (bring your own pumpkin). However, if you don’t have a pumpkin, you are more than welcome to observe or share a pumpkin with a fellow attendee.
-  Meet our staff and learn about the incredible work happening at Cottonwood Urban Farm, where thousands of pounds of food scraps are transformed into nutrient-rich compost each month. 
-  Then, it’s time to smash those pumpkins and add them to the compost pile! 
-  Stick around to volunteer (no experience needed) or explore the hub and the beautiful farm. 

### Can't Make It On November 29th? 
We’re also hosting Pumpkin Smashes at four other locations! Check out www.lacompost.org/pumpkinsmash for more details on additional events near you.

### Minors
All ages are welcome to observe at our Pumpkin Smash events however **minors under 16 must be accompanied by a parent or guardian**. 

### Event Waiver
All participants are required to sign a waiver before smashing pumpkins.

Access the e-Waiver here: https://www.lacompost.org/waiver

### Frequently Asked Questions
Need details before signing up? Visit our FAQ: www.lacompost.org/pumpkinsmash.

events.title: Boston Ice Party
events.description:
Join the Boston ICE Tea Party!

We call upon all patriots to join us on Dec 16th, 2025, the 252nd anniversary of the Boston Tea Party, to retrace the footsteps of this historic protest and declare once more - America has No Kings!

We will gather at 7:15 pm at the Irish Famine Memorial Plaza, across from the Old South Meeting House. We will march to Waterfront Plaza, by the Boston Tea Party Ships & Museum. And we will dump ice into Boston Harbor, to declare loud and clear: No Kings! No Tariffs! No ICE!

There will be clean ice provided for dumping. **Please do not bring your own ice.**

For over 250 years, Bostonians have refused to bow down to tyranny. When King George III forced soldiers into Boston’s streets, levied unjust taxes on imported tea, and refused to hear the people’s voices, the colonial patriots took a stand. On December 16, 1773, hundreds of
colonists hurled tea into Boston Harbor in protest of King George’s tyranny, in what some call the single most important event leading up to the American Revolution.

Today, a President who behaves like a king occupies the White House. He has sent ICE to harass our city and kidnap our friends, families, and neighbors. He has levied unjust tariffs, and made our tea, our coffee, and our lives more expensive. Let us rise once more to take down
tyranny!

We are trying to get a large crowd on the Last Saturday of every month 2025/2026.

Not just NO KINGS 2.0, but every month! We need way more people consistently if we are to stop treating immigrants as criminals, curb gun violence and establish health care for all American citizens. WE NEED EACH OTHER. This may be a way that WE the people will be heard.

Many are looking away, many didn’t vote. But this will not work. We can’t look away if we want change. We must vote! Even if we do not get everything we as individuals want, better is good. Expanded Healthcare, Child Tax Credit, Gun Control, SNAP, Building Housing, Climate Action…. Please don’t look away. This is OUR Legacy.

"In the United States, a critical mass for sustained political change through nonviolent protest is considered to be around 3.5% of the population, which translates to approximately 12 million people, according to research on successful historical movements. While there isn't a single, fixed number, this threshold suggests that mobilizing roughly 3.5% of the U.S. population in peaceful protest can create a powerful dynamic, making it extremely difficult for the government to ignore the movement's demands and increasing the likelihood of achieving significant political change."

"Understanding "Critical Mass"
It's a tipping point:
Critical mass refers to the minimum number of people needed to start a cascade of participation and create a widespread, impactful movement.

Network effects:
In a network, like a protest movement, small groups of early adopters can trigger a larger number of people to join as more of their connections are involved."

If WE the PEOPLE in this country can do this we will help all our causes collectively.

NO KINGS - 12 Million Plus ….Every Last Saturday, EVERY MONTH, Every State… 2025/26

events.title: Weekly Taylor St Bridge Bannering Over I-8 | Saturday Mornings
events.description:
Park in front of The Remy (north side) or at the Taylor Street Park and Ride (south side).

We provide large physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Bring a sign for cars on the bridge or just wave to the cars passing below. You can also bring a flag, chair, bubbles, music, or anything else you want in order to have a good time!

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.

3. We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.

4. We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.

5. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.

6. If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.

7. We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.

8. Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.

9. Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!

10. The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.

Feel free to reach out to VisibilityBrigadeSanDiego@gmail.com with any questions.

events.title: Sign/Share Change.org Petition | Repurpose San Pablo’s $47M Regional Police Hub As A Community Space

sponsor.name: Stop Cop City Bay Area (Tours + Teach-Ins)

events.description:
San Pablo, CA — a small, working-class city just 2.6 square miles wide, located on unceded Ohlone territory — is being turned into a regional training hub for police departments across the Bay Area.

🏗️  City officials are spending $48M to build a 42,000 sq ft police complex (~1 acre) that includes:
1. A 20-lane indoor shooting range
2. Infrared saunas, sleep pods, and a luxury gym
3. A drone command center and launch pad
4. A VR use-of-force simulator, SWAT and K-9 facilities
5. Two classrooms and extensive office space
6. 0.6% of the building for a county-wide mental/behavioral health desk use (despite news coverage focusing on this, A3 can operate from anywhere).


🏗️ This would be San Pablo’s fourth police facility, their 2nd training facility (2019), and, in a city of 30,000 people, serving less than 150 city staff members. Despite not requiring voter approval, the project is funded by tax payer's money and long-term debt:

1. $30.47M 30-year loan (a special bond, that didn't require voter approval, as it takes revenue from our city services to pay off the debt)
2. $10.43M from the city’s general fund (taxes, casino revenue, etc.)
3. $4.35M in COVID-19 relief grant funds under "revenue loss" (resident's wanted to go towards business grants, our senior center, and essential services)
4. $800K from our Parks & Recreation savings/budget

🏗️ The site was originally promised to the people as “The Avenue” — a mixed-use vision for: (a) Affordable housing, (b) Creek restoration and green space, (c) Indigenous land acknowledgment, and (d) Community-centered infrastructure as it is PERFECTLY placed next to the library, WIC office, health center, and new housing. We seek to reclaim this original vision and advocate for responsible financial stewardship that prioritizes the community's democratic voice, choice, and leadership.


🏗️ This is (Stop Cop City Bay Area) Is Bigger Than One City: With $2M annual bond payments due, police departments reaching as far up as Santa Rosa have already signed usage agreements. If this complex is being built to serve the entire region for the next 30 years, then people across city lines — and across generations — deserve a say. This is not just a local fight, this is a Bay Area-wide call to demand centering community voice in local governance, reclaim our futures, and fund the people + root causes of crime. 


📢 Together, we demand:
1. A pause on construction
2. Host public town halls
3. Launch a community task force to reassess the use of the space
4. Repurpose the facility into a community resource hub
5. Enacting a Sunshine Ordinance for transparency moving forward

TAKE ACTION NOW:
✍️ 1. Sign the Petition: www.change.org/stop-cop-campus

📧 2. Email San Pablo City Council: Got 1 Minute? Send a pre-written message or write your own to oppose the facility and demand it be reimagined for community care: www.stopcopcitybayarea.com/email

✅  3. WE'RE ON TOUR!! Invite us to speak or table at your business, cafe, church, community/political group, etc! www.stopcopcitybayarea.com/tour

🌐 Learn more & get involved
Website: www.stopcopcitybayarea.com
Contact: contact@stopcopcitybayarea.com
IG: @stopcopcitybayarea

Our Debt. Our Decision. Our Budget. Our Building. Our Funds. Our Future. 

As the "City of New Directions", 30 years from now, does we want San Pablo to be a regional center for militarized policing or a city that invests in our region's youth, people, housing, health, and futures? 

#StopCopCityBayArea #StopCopCampus #ReclaimTheBay

Making change starts with a simple conversation. That’s what this event is all about. We’ll be calling fellow Democrats in Pickens County to remind them they’re part of a strong and growing community.

It’s simply neighbors connecting with neighbors, sharing encouragement, and building momentum for the future we all want. It’s how we listen to Democratic voters, establish an ongoing connection with them, and recruit more volunteers so we can elect Democratic candidates up and down the ballot. 

You bring your laptop, cellphone, chargers, and headphones. We’ll give you everything you need, cheer each other on, and have some laughs along the way. Every call strengthens our numbers and brings us one step closer to the change we deserve. After you’re trained and comfortable on the phone, you can make calls from your home any day of the week. 

Hop on the phones, start dialing your neighbors, and let's get ready to Free America!

💙 Join us, bring a friend, and let’s call some Democrats, because together, we win.

events.title: The Season of Enough
events.description:
UPDATE: The Town of Rutherfordton has denied our permit application for December 6th, stating that the entire date is unavailable for any additional permitted activity due to the size of the Town’s parade and its associated road closures. This effectively places all public spaces in Rutherfordton off-limits for free-speech and First Amendment activity of any kind on December 6th, which is a form of prior restraint. We believe this is unconstitutional and have alerted the ACLU-NC. Our demonstration will proceed peacefully as planned, and we ask everyone to wear festive holiday attire and bring a sign reflecting the things every person deserves.

According to the Town’s ordinance, peacefully holding a sign without a permit could technically get you a citation or a Class 3 misdemeanor — which means we might all earn ourselves a festive little arrest record for the holidays. 🎄

Legally speaking, enforcing that against peaceful First Amendment activity would never hold up, and the ACLU-NC is already aware. But hey, if the Town wants to make “Free Speech for Christmas” a punishable offense, that’s on them, not us.

🎄❄️🎄❄️🎄❄️🎄❄️🎄❄️🎄❄️🎄❄️🎄❄️🎄❄️🎄❄️🎄❄️🎄

This holiday season, we’re reminding our community that enough is a gift worth sharing.

During the Rutherfordton–Spindale Christmas Parade, volunteers from Indivisible Rutherford NC will gather to celebrate a Season of Enough—enough food, enough shelter, enough safety, and enough dignity for everyone in our community.

Dressed in festive attire, we’ll be walking around sharing messages of compassion, inclusion, and economic justice, handing out information on issues that matter most to local families: living wages, housing security, food access, and human rights while also gathering donations for Operation Santa through the USPS, supporting letters from children and families in need that we’ve pledged to adopt this year.

The holidays should be a time when everyone has enough—and together, we can help make that a reality.

All are welcome — bring your energy, creativity, and commitment to protecting our planet. Participants of every race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, and background are encouraged to attend.

events.title: Juneteenth: A Day of Service and Solidarity
events.description:
Come Juneteenth 2026, Indivisible Rutherford NC is stepping back from the spotlight to stand beside—not in front of—our neighbors.

Rather than hosting our own protest or event, we’re pledging to spend the weekend volunteering with local Black-led organizations across Rutherford County, offering our time, resources, and hands in support of their ongoing work for freedom, justice, and community care.

Juneteenth reminds us that liberation is a shared effort—one rooted in listening, partnership, and action. Join us as we honor the spirit of the day by showing up where we’re needed, learning from those leading the way, and continuing the work toward a more just and equitable future for all.

If you’d like to take part, we’ll be organizing volunteer shifts throughout the weekend to match folks with local Black-led groups and community projects that need extra hands. Whether you can give an hour or the whole afternoon, your help makes a difference. Reach out to us to coordinate a time and location—together, we can make sure our support is meaningful, respectful, and right where it’s needed most.

events.title: Brookline Rally for Democracy, December 2025

Brookline Rally for Democracy

Every Saturday at 1:00 PM | Coolidge Corner

Join members of three Brookline pro-democracy groups — Indivisible Activist Evenings, Brookline Pax, and Speak Out, Seniors! — for our weekly rally at Coolidge Corner.

We gather to raise our voices and our signs in defense of democracy, justice, and decency — and to stand united against the abuses of the Trump administration and the forces that threaten our rights and freedoms.

We stand for:

• Immigrant rights, human rights, and racial justice

• Free speech, the Constitution, and the rule of law

• Access to health and healthcare for all

• Protection of our planet and the future we leave to the next generation

We choose empathy over cruelty, peace over violence, and hope over fear.

Our rallies are peaceful, spirited, and uplifting — a chance to connect, recharge, and stand up for what matters. Bring your friends, your voice, and your sign (or borrow one of ours!).

All are welcome!  The rally is multi-generational and family-friendly; those using walkers or other mobility devices may use them to sit to participate.

In the event of inclement weather, we’ll each use our best judgment about whether to attend. We hope you’ll do the same! 

Please join us, one rally at a time.  We’ll continue for as long as it takes.

events.title: Share Your Story Virtually!
events.description:
**Millions of families are about to find out that their health care costs are doubling**—all because Congress let key Affordable Care Act protections expire. It’s the biggest healthcare crisis since the ACA passed, and it’s hitting just as open enrollment begins on November 1.

[**SHARE YOUR HEALTHCARE STORY NOW!**](https://form.typeform.com/to/bpetGgfp)

We’re making sure policymakers and the press hear directly from **YOU**—the people most affected by this healthcare heist. Working families, small-business owners, and gig workers are facing premium spikes, Medicaid cuts, or the risk of losing coverage entirely.

[**Will you share your healthcare story with us right now?**](https://form.typeform.com/to/bpetGgfp)

Real people’s experiences help reporters tell the truth about what’s happening and help Members of Congress understand what’s at stake in their own districts. Once you submit your story, we'll  follow up to confirm your information.

[**Share your story now about why we need lower costs, not less care.**](https://form.typeform.com/to/bpetGgfp)

This is our chance to show who really pays the price for these cuts—and to demand better.

events.title: NO KINGS = NO COP CITY: Oakland / East Bay Area Virtual Teach-In

sponsor.name: Stop Cop City Bay Area (Tours + Teach-Ins)

events.description:
If No Kings is about rejecting authoritarian power at the national level, then stopping Cop City Bay Area is how we live that principle locally.

---

Join San Pablo residents and East Bay neighbors for a virtual teach-in focused on San Pablo’s proposed $47 million regional police complex and the community’s movement to reclaim and repurpose it.

This facility is planned to train police departments across the Bay Area, with confirmed contracts already reaching Santa Rosa, Richmond, Hercules, Pinole, and beyond. This would be San Pablo’s second police training center, built and financed *without voter approval* through a $32 million, 30-year loan (causing a $1.8 million annual debt).

The proposed 42,000-square-foot complex would serve fewer than 150 city staff and include luxury offices, a drone launch pad, a 20-lane gun range, and private gym/sauna suites.

Our collective goal is to repurpose this facility into a community resource hub and youth center that embodies the creativity, resilience, and vision of local residents.

Despite months of public calls for town halls, transparency, and accountability, San Pablo City Council members were advised to disregard their constituents. This teach-in responds by centering community education, visioning, and reclamation: a space to learn, imagine, and act together.

Together, we’ll examine how rising fascism, AI, hyper-surveillance, and propaganda masked as “public safety” are reshaping our region (and how residents are resisting through collective care, political education, and creative organizing).

💡 You’ll Learn
1. The facts about Stop Cop City Bay Area and the propaganda utilized to hide who pays, who profits, and who’s excluded.
2. The ways the Stop Cop City Bay Area movement connects to national policing and surveillance infrastructures
3. How authoritarianism grows locally through budget manipulation, long-term municipal debt, and the expansion of carceral infrastructure.
4. The community’s repurposing vision — transforming the publicly funded site into a democratic, multi-use community resource hub and youth center.
5. Why this fight is about protecting local democracy itself — ensuring our budgets, debt, and decisions serve and include the people. 

Authoritarianism builds walls; we’re building community. The "City of New Directions" invites you to freedom dream with us. Together, we can repurpose, reallocate, and reclaim our collective future. 


♿️ Accessibility: Auto-captions enabled • Camera off • Live chat moderation • Participation optional • Webinar format

🤝 Hosted by Stop Cop City Bay Area (Tours + Teach-Ins)
📧 contact@stopcopcitybayarea.com

🔥 About Us
We are a grassroots collective of San Pablo and East Bay residents organizing to stop a $47 million regional police complex and reimagine it as a community-owned hub for healing, art, and youth empowerment.

This teach-in is part of the Stop Cop City Bay Area Fall 2025 Tour—where we visit campuses, classrooms, cafés, and community spaces across the Bay to raise awareness, build people power, and co-create our liberatory future.


Explore these links and resources to ground yourself in the campaign:

events.title: Guerrero Median Beautification Day - 900 block and 1000 block
events.description:
Join Guerrero neighbors for a morning of pruning, weeding, and cleaning.

Volunteers will meet near 988 Guerrero St and then work on the median for the 900 block and 1000 block. SF Public Works will provide lane closure and tools. Please sign up so we can prepare enough tools.

Please note that this is not a regular gardening day. It's very fast paced and we need to switch between a few tasks. It is crucial that volunteers pivot and listen to DPW supervisor(s).

We typically start removing green waste at 10:45 AM or 10:35 PM. Mulching is not guaranteed and dependent on time, volunteer turnout, and if the green waste has been removed. On December 7, we will spread a compost-mulch mixture over both medians and mix it in with the existing soil. Please stay until the end so we can complete this time-consuming task.

### Agenda
- Safety talk and curb cut demo 
- Gardening, weeding, pruning, cleaning 
- Rake green waste into large piles 
- Load green waste into the trucks starting around 10:35 AM or 10:45 AM. 
- If green waste removal is completed by 11:10 AM ideally, we will spread a layer of compost-mulch mixture onto both medians and mix it in with the existing soil.

### What to Bring/Wear
- Bring a reusable water bottle 
- Wear sunscreen and closed toe shoes
- Dress in layers

### Community Partners
SF Public Works, District 8 Supervisor Rafael Mandelman, Guerrero neighbors

events.title: Phonebank for Aftyn Behn with Progressive Victory!
events.description:
We are hosting PHONEBANKS for Aftyn Behn up until December 2nd, 2025 in our Discord Server!

You can join us by signing up with Progressive Victory at https://progress.win/volunteer

When it's time to phone bank, you can join us in Organizing VC 1. Until then, feel free to join ahead of time and get to know members of the community!

--------- ABOUT US --------------

Built by the internet, for America.

Progressive Victory is a new kind of political institution: seamlessly marrying the electoral impact and volunteer power of traditional progressive organizations with the culture and community of digital third places.

Dedicated to pushing the Democratic Party to the left, we partner with left-aligned content creators to activate their disaffected, terminally online audiences converting them into lifelong, on the ground organizers. Providing the necessary structure & resources to empower viewers into volunteers, our innovative, community-first model utilizes familiar online spaces to introduce & demystify the world of political organizing.

Progressive Victory embraces queer & neurodivergent, new-to-activism volunteers of all backgrounds, ethnicities, and abilities. Over the long term, we aim to mainstream the online, progressive power block burgeoning within the Democratic Party and prove that it, and we, are too big to ignore.

events.description:

 We live in a consumer society where it is all about "me". We believe in equality and supporting small local business'. The wealth gap in America has seen a DRAMATIC increase. events.title: Resilience For Sustainable Activism
events.description:
Many of us entered movement work out of urgency and many of us are exhausted by it. The Resilience Toolkit offers an embodied, justice-aligned framework for sustaining activism over the long arc of the struggle. Rather than treating burnout, reactivity and conflict as personal failures, The Toolkit helps us understand them as predictable stress and trauma responses - and equips us with real-time regulation skills that expand our capacity to stay engaged without collapse or numbness. 

Together, we’ll explore:
How stress and trauma shape movement behavior (withdrawal, escalation, fracture) and how embodied stabilization interrupts those patterns in real time

Embodied solidarity: how listening, repair, and collective care become possible only when the nervous system has enough bandwidth

Rest and joy as conditions of political strategy, not rewards for after the work is done

Practical tools to increase steadiness and discernment into movement, organizing, and mutual aid work

This conversation connects the inner work of healing and reflection with the outer work of solidarity and action — helping us build movements that are both resilient and humane.

“How we breathe, listen, rest, and relate is political.”

Whether you’re a longtime organizer, new to activism, or simply seeking to 
live your values more fully, this session offers inspiration and embodied tools to help you put solidarity into action every day.

Harrisburg doesn't guarantee funding for our local buses - and that puts our Red Rose transit (and all transit systems in PA) at risk. We demand a dedicated and expanded state funding stream because we need MORE TRANSIT, NOT LESS. We're done with decline in Lancaster and were ready to fight for more.

Join Lancaster-area elected officials, riders, and workers for a rally to show you're ready to win the transit service we deserve. Gather at Queen St Station in downtown Lancaster to make our message heard.

### The background on transit's funding cliff. [Take Action Here](https://www.transitforallpa.org/takeaction/#letter) to call for better transit in Lancaster and across PA.

In January 2027, Red Rose Transit (and its sibling agency BARTA in Berks County) will hit their fiscal cliff, leading to service cuts and fare increases due to state funding shortfalls. It's only months after peers in the Lehigh Valley undergo their own cuts, and aligned with cuts in Monroe County and other agencies across PA. On Tuesday, December 2, transit riders, workers, elected officials, and other supporters will join together to show that Transit Moves Us in Lancaster!

events.description:
Please join Duluth Indivisible for the kick-off of our organizing film series!  We'll be showing "Rustin," a 2023 film about Bayard Rustin, the organizing genius (along with A. Philip Randolph) behind the 1963 March on Washington.  On August 28, 1963, Rustin, largely supported by a team of volunteers, and with just about three months of preparation, put together a march of over 200,000 people to Washington, D.C. Nine months later, the Civil Rights Act passed. 

Why (perhaps) have you never heard of him? His story and participation were suppressed because he was gay. 

As we organize our communities for effective action in 2025 and beyond, it's good to be inspired by and learn from masters of the art. Bayard Rustin is at the front of that line. Please come learn with us.

events.description:
When it comes to the future of Stanly County, no one knows the needs, challenges, and op-portunities better than the people who live them every day. That’s why community input isn’t just valuable, it’s essential. 

Whether it’s about public education, community growth and development, healthcare access, affordable housing, or small business resources, the people most affected by these issues must be at the center of the conversation. 

Join Indivisible Uwharrie for our first-ever Community Conversation. An open, honest space where your experiences, concerns, and ideas take priority. 

There will be no presentation, no speech, and no long lecture. Just real listening. This is your space to speak, share, and be heard. 
Our goal is simple: to listen deeply and take what we hear directly to local officials, so that the voices of everyday residents shape the decisions that impact us all. 

Far too often, decisions in local government are made without truly hearing from those they affect. This session is about changing that. 

	-If you’re a parent navigating our public school system 
	-A small business owner trying to thrive 
	-A neighbor facing housing challenges 
	-Or someone who cares about the roads, health access, or community wellbeing 

We want to hear from you. Come As You Are. Bring your thoughts, your experiences, your questions, even your frustrations. This is a space for all of it. 

Together, we can ensure our local leaders aren’t just making decisions for us, but with us. 

Mark your calendar for September 23rd. Let’s make our voices impossible to ignore. Follow us on Facebook for updates on time and location. Email us with questions or to get involved or click here to volunteer!

Can you help us spread the word to help save Democracy and stand up for the Constitution?

The Newark DE Solidarity Brigade is an opportunity to reach thousands and thousands of people in a short amount of time.  It can help us recruit new people and show a United Delaware to the masses!

Solidarity/Visibility Brigades are typically done on overpasses and pedestrian bridges to share our message with the passing cars.

There are Nationwide Solidarity/Visibility Brigades and hoping Delaware can catch up to the outreach we are seeing in other states. Let's show them size doesn't matter.  That's why they call us "The Small Wonder"!

They are happening throughout Delaware- Claymont, New Castle, Newark, Middletown, Smyrna, Milford and Rehoboth with more and more popping up!

We participate on the Chapman Road Overpass of I-95 (near 80 Chapman Rd, Newark DE 19713), Welsh Tract Rd Overpass of I-95 (near Folk Memorial Park 98 Welsh Tract Rd) the Meadowood Pedestrian Bridge (South Meadowood Rd & Capitol Trail Newark 19711) and we recently deployed a message on the Elsmere Pedestrian Bridge  (676 South Union Street Wilmington DE)!

If you like to dance, drum, wave,  sing, whatever your passion, we would love to stand beside you!
Reach out to    newarkdevb@gmail.com  with questions or to volunteer  and support the Brigades!   No experience or supplies necessary.

events.description:
Join us starting at 9:30am ET to write postcards, talk about the news, and hear from candidates and political leaders. If this is your first time joining this group, please sign on at least 15 minutes before the speaker start time listed below. 

Please answer the registration questions accurately and completely. Also, having your full name displayed will facilitate admission from the waiting room. We may request clarification from you in the waiting room chat. 

**Warm Cookies of the Revolution will join us on Tuesday, December 9, at 10:00am ET.** Evan Weissman is the founding executive director of Warm Cookies of the Revolution, the world's first Civic Health Club, that blends innovative arts and culture with crucial civic issues. His work with Warm Cookies includes creating over 400 arts-based civic programs (live events, installations, videos, music, and books). Since 2012, we have engaged more than 1 million participants through wildly innovative programs that actually get real people to engage in democracy and civic life. Our motto is Vote Every Day. We focus on the 364 days of the year that are not election day. People are busy. After a day of work and taking care of our families, there is a reason why Netflix, the NFL, and shopping are where most people spend their time and money. Instead of shaming people for not being more involved, we make civic life as irresistible and joyous as possible. We know that civically engaged people vote, volunteer, and live healthier lives.

We strive to build community, educate voters, and use our Sharpies to write to save democracy together. Write postcards with us or just join the conversation. If you need help getting started with postcarding, please visit our [FAQ](https://markersfordemocracy.org/postcarding/postcarding-faq).

If you are with the media and want to attend, you must notify us at markersfordemocracy@gmail.com at least two hours before the start of the event. All discussions are off the record.

RSVP here to join, and invite your friends! Together, we’ll use Vote Forward, an award-winning program that helps volunteers reach underrepresented voters and turn out voters in important upcoming elections.

Never written letters before? No worries! Go to votefwd.org, create an account, download 20 letters, and we’ll show you exactly how to write them at the event.

Every letter you write is a small, powerful step toward strengthening democracy, just like every hammer swing builds a home. We’re not looking for short-term gestures — we’re building impact that lasts.

Let’s show what happens when we put our hearts and hands to work for the long term. Can’t wait to see you there!

With purpose,
Randy Chase
No Kings. Just Homes

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Day of Service
events.description:
Date: Monday, January 19th
Time: 10:00 AM - 2:00 PM (with extended pantry hours until 6:00 PM)
Location: Yorkville Congregational United Church of Christ
409 Center Parkway

Join the Yorkville community in honoring the legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. through a Day of Service dedicated to compassion, community, and collective action. This event brings neighbors together to serve others, share resources, and continue Dr. King’s mission of justice and equality through hands-on volunteerism.

The day will begin at 10:00 AM with guest speakers who will reflect on Dr. King’s vision and its relevance in today’s world.

At 11:00 AM, participants can engage in Community Resource Connect or a session on Dr. King's continued legacy and teachings. Community Resource Connect is an opportunity to learn about and connect with local organizations offering essential services and volunteer opportunities.

A community lunch will be served at 12:30 PM, providing time for fellowship and conversation among volunteers and attendees.

After lunch, from 1:15 PM to 2:00 PM, volunteers will assist with pantry preparation, sorting and organizing donations for community distribution.
The day continues with a Pop-Up Pantry from 2:30 PM to 6:00 PM, where families and individuals can access food, snacks, and toiletries. Staying for this portion is not required but any help is always appreciated.

Attendees are encouraged to donate snacks and toiletries either before or during the event to support the Pop-Up Pantry. This is not required but any help is always appreciated.

For families, child care will be available starting at 9:30 AM, allowing parents to fully participate in the day’s activities.

Come together in service and solidarity as we celebrate the life and legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. through action, community, and care.

For all of Indivisible's info and events please see our linktree -
https://linktr.ee/IndivisibleKendallCounty

Join Our Weekly Equality Phone Banks!

Every week, EQMI will be hosting phone banks to connect with voters across districts all over the state, identifying and mobilizing Equality Voters who care about fairness, inclusion, and justice for all.

These phone banks are one of the most effective ways to build real momentum heading into next year’s midterm elections. By having direct conversations with voters, we’re not only helping people get engaged early, we’re also gathering critical information that will guide our strategy for the months ahead.

The data we collect now helps us understand which areas are energized, where we need to focus more outreach, and how to tailor our message to meet voters where they are. This groundwork will be essential as we ramp up organizing and voter mobilization efforts in the spring for the midterm elections.

Whether you’re a seasoned volunteer or brand new to phone banking, we’ll provide all the training and tools you need. Every call makes a difference and every volunteer helps build the foundation for equality and progress in the next election.

What to bring:

Please bring a laptop, phone, and headphones to each phone bank. We’ll provide all the training, scripts, and support you need to feel confident making calls.

If you can’t join us in person, no problem! We can set up a one-on-one training session at a time that works best for you so you can make calls from home at your own convenience. Just email acherry@equalitymi.org to set up one-on-one training.

events.title: Wednesday Walkouts for Health - Cambridge!
events.description:
#StandUpforHealth! 

Join us for Wednesday Walkouts for Health in defense of science and healthcare for all 5-5:30pm in Kendall Square! 


There are so many urgent health-related issues that demand our advocacy. The Trump regime has declared war on science, evidence-based policy, and public health. As healthcare workers and as Americans, we cannot stand by while our public health leadership, research institutions, and science-based guidelines are decimated. We must walk out to demand the resignation or removal of RFK Jr. who has led these reckless efforts.


But that is not enough. The administration has turned programs meant to nourish and heal our most vulnerable neighbors into political weapons. Americans have long chosen to invest their tax dollars in care ensuring that families can afford healthcare and food when they are most at risk. Programs like SNAP were created so that no child in the United States would go hungry, and Medicaid and Medicare so that all Americans could access healthcare in their time of need.


We cannot allow these programs to be manipulated for political gain any longer. It is time to show up, speak up, stand up, and walk out for science, for health, and for our shared humanity.


Wednesday Walkouts for Health aims to activate and engage healthcare workers, advocates, and their communities around political threats to health. Join others across the country in this coordinated weekly action!

This is a standout event. We stand under a streetlight on Broadway and 3rd and Main next to Galaxy Park. Join for any length of time. If this window of time or location doesn’t work for you, we encourage you to consider partnering with others to standout at another time/location on a Wednesday. 


Please share with your friends, family, and co-workers!


Yours in Solidarity,

events.description:
Let's do NO KINGS from Oct. 18th all over again !!

Like NO KINGS on Oct. 18th!

Not just NO KINGS 2.0, but every month! We need way more people consistently if we are to stop treating immigrants as criminals, curb gun violence and establish health care for all American citizens. WE NEED EACH OTHER. This may be a way that WE the people will be heard.

Many are looking away, many didn’t vote. But this will not work. We can’t look away if we want change. We must vote! Even if we do not get everything we as individuals want, better is good. Expanded Healthcare, Child Tax Credit, Gun Control, SNAP, Building Housing, Climate Action…. Please don’t look away. This is OUR Legacy.

"In the United States, a critical mass for sustained political change through nonviolent protest is considered to be around 3.5% of the population, which translates to approximately 12 million people, according to research on successful historical movements. While there isn't a single, fixed number, this threshold suggests that mobilizing roughly 3.5% of the U.S. population in peaceful protest can create a powerful dynamic, making it extremely difficult for the government to ignore the movement's demands and increasing the likelihood of achieving significant political change."

"Understanding "Critical Mass"
It's a tipping point:
Critical mass refers to the minimum number of people needed to start a cascade of participation and create a widespread, impactful movement.

Network effects:
In a network, like a protest movement, small groups of early adopters can trigger a larger number of people to join as more of their connections are involved."

If WE the PEOPLE in this country can do this we will help all our causes collectively.

Millions of Americans are still paying the price for political games in Washington. Congress may have ended the shutdown, but they failed to protect affordable health care — and now millions of families face higher premiums or lost coverage.


Here in West Michigan, Rep. Hillary Scholten is fighting hard to protect affordable health care, but Rep. Bill Huizenga has refused to stand up for working families. Help PAL restore and maintain the beauty of our parks and trails by signing up for the December 2025 Trail Stewardship event at Duncan Park! Taking care of our trails is a crucial part of keeping our system safe, welcoming, and fun to use, and volunteers play a huge role in making that happen.

Our December trail cleanup will focus heavily on invasive species removal - think English ivy, privet, wisteria, kudzu, and eleagnus. We’ll provide gloves, loppers, and hand saws, plus a brief presentation on identification and best removal practices.

We’ll also celebrate the folks who show up for our trails all year. Come see the reveal of our new Trail Steward shirts. Attending this event counts as step 1 of 3 toward earning your free shirt!

Last, but most certainly not least, join us in celebrating the legacy of Newt Hardie. We’ll have coffee and “birthday cake” in honor of Newt, founder of the Trees Coalition, whose legacy of trail and tree care we celebrate each December during this cleanup

events.title: Avelo Airline Protest Organized by Mesa Valley Indivisible

address_lines: South Gilbert Road & East Broadway Road

events.description:
## 🛫Avelo Airlines: Cancel your contract with ICE. 

### These flights are illegal, inhumane, & unconstitutional.

* Avelo Airlines is the first commercial airline to sign a deportation charter contract with ICE. Every day this $150 million contract stands, Avelo cashes in on tearing families apart — and every day it runs, deportation profiteering becomes more normalized. If they get away with it, other airlines will follow. Our leverage? Working with groups across the country to hit them on every front — at their airports, in the states and cities bankrolling them, and on the campuses that partner with them — until doing ICE’s dirty work costs too much to continue.

* These flights are secretive and unmarked, with no guarantee of legal counsel or due process for the people being removed. Every day the contract continues, Avelo is profiting from tearing families apart — and gambling its business on mass deportations.

* To keep the pressure on Avelo, Mesa Valley Indivisible continues to protest against Avelo Airlines operating ICE deportations on Saturday, February 21st!

### 📢 Important 

[Click here for virtual actions that you can also take against Avelo Airlines!](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14AtEJVcYUFfHBiiQCINwXnHDWFEhMEiXUCUIp11k7H4/edit?usp=sharing)
 
### Signs & Graphics

Please create signs and graphics that are relevant to Avelo & Mesa Gateway Airport! The messaging we put on our signs can do a lot to cut right through Mesa Gateway's bureaucratic smokescreen.

* Call attention to Avelo Airlines separating families
* Complicity of Mesa/Gateway airport
* Illegal deportations without due process
* Human trafficking

###  Protest Information

🅿️ Parking is available around the intersection 

☮️ As always, our goal is to have protestors on every corner! 

⭐ Please share with friends, family, neighbors, EVERYONE!

📷 When posting photos/videos online, please make sure to tag the Mesa Valley Indivisible social media page and clearly state Mesa Valley Indivisible as the protest organizer. The goal is to raise our group's profile which will make it easier for new people to find & join our community while also increasing our influence with government officials and the media! In order to have a greater impact on our city, people have to know we exist first!!

events.title: Bridging the Intergenerational Divide: Fostering Understanding Across the Generations
events.description:
Join Michelle Ward for this timely presentation.

We’ll explore how to break down the barriers between generations and build stronger, more cohesive communities. With rapid technological advancements and shifting cultural norms, it’s easy for misunderstandings to arise between older and younger generations. This talk will provide practical strategies to foster empathy, promote effective communication, and create opportunities for collaboration across age groups. By embracing the strengths of each generation, we can unlock new potential for innovation, mentorship, and social unity. Join us as we bridge the gap and learn how to connect, understand, and thrive together. No matter your age.

events.title: New Hampton Democratic Committee Meeting

location.venue: Gordon-Nash Library at New Hampton School- downstairs

events.description:
Karishma Manzur, candidate for US Senate will speak.

Karishma is a medical scientist with a Ph.D. in biochemistry and molecular biology. She spent over 20 years working on treatments for illnesses like Alzheimer’s disease, epilepsy, and depression.

Her commitment to public service didn’t stop in the research field. She is serving on the boards of NH Ranked Choice Voting and NH Open Democracy Action, and previously served on the board of NH Peace Action. Through these organizations, Karishma works to reduce the influence of corporate greed and political corruption in our government.

Disheartened by the housing crisis, rising cost of living, and broken healthcare system, Karishma is running as a Democrat for the U.S. Senate to ensure every person has a fair shot at a brighter future.


This communication does not imply an endorsement or favoritism of any kind by the New Hampshire Democratic Party to any Democratic candidates actively engaged in competitive primary contests.

events.title: Pacific Beach: Take Action For Democracy!
events.description:
Join us on the first Saturday of the month, from 10am to 11am, at the corner of Crown Point Dr. and Ingraham Street, for our monthly Take Action for Democracy sign-waving rally in Pacific Beach!

In addition to getting our voices heard, we will always have suggestions on meaningful ways that people can take action to save our democracy.

Let’s stand together with our neighbors to shout “Yes to Democracy!” and “No to Division and Destruction!” Together, we’ll send a clear, positive message that Pacific Beach stands for unity, justice, and the values that make our country strong — not the chaos and cruelty of the Trump Administration’s agenda.

These gatherings are peaceful, joyful, and family-friendly. They’re also a vital opportunity to expand our community coalition, raise awareness, and offer real actions people can take to defend and strengthen democracy.

Bring your creativity, your energy, and your favorite signs (find some ideas here: https://takeactionsandiego.org/docs/signs.pdf). Folding chairs welcome if you’d like to relax while waving.

Let’s make some noise, share some hope, and remind everyone passing by: Democracy is worth defending — and it starts right here, with us.

Organized by concerned PB neighbors and Take Action San Diego.

events.title: Day of Action: Stronger Miami
events.description:
It’s time to push forward and ensure that Miami voters have the voice and representation they deserve. Join community partners at this park December 6th to rally for the city of Miami to adopt common sense, anti-corruption, pro-democracy amendment that would: 

•Move city elections alongside statewide elections: 
To increase voter participation, making it easier for working families to take part in our democracy, saving millions of dollars in taxpayer money.

•Shrink city districts by expanding the city commission from 5 to 9: 
To provide greater representation and ensure every community in Miami has a voice in how our city is run.

•Ban Commission districts from being gerrymandered: 
To prevent corrupt politicians from abusing the political process for personal gain.

This amendment will make our local elections fairer, more accessible, increase voter participation, and make our city government more reflective of the communities it serves.

Join us to learn more, connect with other organizers, and help collect petitions to get this amendment on the ballot.

events.title: Cancel Spotify
events.description:
**Spotify is running ads recruiting agents for ICE**, the federal agency charged with mass deportation and surveillance of immigrant communities. These ads target vulnerable populations, promise signing bonuses, and normalize fear and intimidation in our neighborhoods.

Spotify claims these ads comply with their policy, but the truth is streaming hate is not neutral. It’s a choice. 

We refuse to fund it. We refuse to ignore it.

**Our Demands for Spotify**

Until our demands are met, we will withhold our subscriptions and our support. We are calling on Spotify founder and current CEO Daniel Ek, as well as Gustav Söderström and Alex Norström who will become the new co-CEOs starting in January 2026, to:

- Immediately terminate all ICE and DHS advertising contracts with Spotify.
- Spotify must update its Advertising Policy to prohibit government propaganda and hate-based recruitment campaigns.
- Spotify must commit to defending civil rights and standing up for communities under threat from authoritarian actions.


What You Can do

We are asking every listener and artist to take action:

- Cancel your Spotify subscription, TODAY until the ICE ads are removed.

- Tag Spotify publicly and urge artists, podcasters, and labels to denounce these ads and oppose the platform complicity.

- Use our [social media toolkit](https://app.sosha.ai/toolkit/spotify-ice-trump-fascism-7980) to post online.


**[Learn More and Get Instructions to Unsubscribe](https://indivisible.org/cancel-spotify)**

As of yesterday, the letter has been rewritten, and the vote retracting the letter stands. However, Amanda McKinney (County Commissioner) voiced her continued support for the racist language of the original letter and for it to have been sent to ICE.  For note: Jarrod Sessler attended and gave public comments supporting the language of the original letter, and sending it to immigration enforcement.

We were not given a copy of the new letter, written by commissioner Curtis. But he stated that he believes the local authorities, not immigration enforcement, should be enforcing health code violations.

events.title: Spotify is Running ICE Recruitment Ads. We're Canceling our Subscriptions until they Stop.
events.description:
### Spotify is running ads recruiting more agents for ICE.

ICE, the federal agency charged with mass deportation and surveillance of immigrant communities.  Masked secret police. These ads target vulnerable populations, promise signing bonuses, and normalize fear and intimidation in our neighborhoods.

Spotify claims these ads comply with their policy, but the truth is streaming hate is not neutral. It’s a choice.

We refuse to fund it. We refuse to ignore it. 

### Our Demand for Spotify - Stop!

Until ICE recruitment stops, we will withhold our subscription dollars and our support. 

### What You Can Do Now

We are asking every listener and artist to take action:

**Cancel your Spotify subscription, TODAY until the ICE ads are removed.**   Watch step-by-step instructions here. https://www.youtube.com/shorts/TKp7cx8kwh4

Tag Spotify publicly and urge artists, podcasters, and labels to denounce these ads and oppose the platform's complicity with the Trump regime..

Use our social media toolkit to post online.  https://app.sosha.ai/toolkit/spotify-ice-trump-fascism-7980


### Read on for more tools and info, including ways to join this action even if you aren’t a Spotify user, and tips on transferring your playlist.

**Spotify subscriber? **
We created a step-by-step video on how to cancel your Spotify Premium subscription, https://www.youtube.com/shorts/TKp7cx8kwh4

 And since we understand it’s tough losing your playlists and saved songs, we have resources to help make the transition to alternative music services smooth:  https://indivisible.org/cancel-spotify

When Spotify removes ICE ads and stops profiting from fascist propaganda, we can re-subscribe, if we like..

**NOT a Spotify subscriber?**
Chances are high that you know someone -- friend, child, or social follower -- who uses Spotify Premium, and we can all call on our favorite artists and podcasters to speak out with us.

Use our pre-made social posts to support the Cancel Spotify campaign online. Post to all your favorite social networks to raise awareness of Spotify’s complicity, our campaign, and how to cancel.

Urge artists, podcasters, and labels to publicly denounce these ads and pressure Spotify leadership. If you know anyone who creates music or content for Spotify, please reach out to them directly. If you don’t, use social media to publicly call on your favorite artists to join the fight.

Profit-driven media giants and their billionaire owners seem to think that going along with the authoritarian Trump regime is the easy thing. They’re following the profits and painting it as neutrality.

But in the face of an unjust regime, neutrality is complicity.

events.title: Speak at “Sunday Service”: Share your mission, an initiative, test your CTA, and meet ready-to-help
events.description:
**Organizers/advocates**: speak at _Sunday Service_*. 
Share your mission, test a clear CTA, and recruit allies in a supportive weekly room (3–5 min slot + brief Q&A). Comedy for catharsis, serious for solutions. Sign up with org, issue, and link.

*_[click here to see the marketing copy for these events](https://www.onthestage.tickets/show/birmingham-festival-theatre/6903c8f6689de6100ac8757a/about)_

## Who this is for
Organizers, advocates, mutual-aid teams, community groups, researchers, and issue-area experts who want a friendly weekly stage to:

- Practice a short, real CTA (join, sign-up, show-up).

- Announce a timely initiative or update.

- Find new volunteers, partners, or collaborators.

- Connect with neighbors who don’t suck.


## What happens 
(Fun + Inform + Share + Connect)

- **Political comedy + catharsis:** Comedian Matt Davis and other invited performers cast out the week’s nonsense with sharp, hilarious satire.

- **Mini-rally speaker slot (_you_):** 3–5 minutes to state the problem, make one clear ask, and tell people exactly how to help.

- **Testify & discuss:** Short audience stories and Q&A.

- **Fellowship:** Stay a few minutes afterward to meet people who want to take action.


## Why this helps you
Whether you're an experienced public speaker, or new message delivering, our _Sunday Service_ events are here to provide a supportive and enthusiastic environment to run your call to actions and initiate announcements. 

- **Practice your pitch** in a supportive room (no “both-sides” contortions required).

- **Get real-time feedback** on your call-to-action.

- **Grow your list** and recruit prospective volunteers/partners.

- **Cross-pollinate** with other local efforts and idea-driven folks.

## Format & Time Commitment

- Weekly opportunity; 60 minutes total + optional 15-minute post-show mingle.

- Speaker slot: 3–5 minutes + 2–3 minutes of Q&A.

## How To Participate

- Click **“Sign up/RSVP”** and choose **“I want to be a mini-rally speaker.”**

- In the notes, include: org name, issue area, one-sentence CTA, and a link to your sign-up/learn-more page.

- We’ll confirm a date and share simple guidelines to make your CTA clear and effective.

## Tone & ground rules

We co-opt revival language for satire (e.g., _Cast out the week!_), but the speaker slots are **serious**. We encourage scientific, humanist, pro-democracy, and community-minded messages. Hate, harassment, and disinformation are not welcome.

## Want more info on who is behind this?

### About Laughing Impact Project
This performance is staged as part of _Laughing Impact Project_ (L.I.P.), a civic-facing arts and activism project that produces participatory live events in partnership with grassroots organizations. Each Laughing Impact event includes a performance, pre- and post-show engagement with civic groups, and digital media intended to deepen public understanding and connection. While “Sunday Service” is its own independent creative work, it is presented inside these structured events to maximize civic and social impact. Learn more, including how to get your organization involved in this or future events, at  [https://laughingimpact.org](https://laughingimpact.org)


### About Birmingham Festival Theatre
Opened in 1972, and in its current location since 1973, BFT has staged performance runs for over 310 productions in its 53 years. The oldest black box theatre space in the State of Alabama, BFT began with and has continued a mission of supporting the exchange and development of theatrical talent, ideas and artistic visions, and by presenting shows that can only be seen in Birmingham on its stage. [https://bftonline.org](https://bftonline.org)


### About Matt Davis
Matt Davis is an award-winning comedian with a long C.V. of global comedy and arts festivals spanning 25+ years of touring across 70+ countries, including _Just For Laughs_ in Montreal, _Sketch Fest_ in San Francisco, _UICF_ in Utrecht, Netherlands, the _Bengaluru Comedy Festival_ in India, _Sydney Comedy Fringe_ in Australia, _HICF_ in Hong Kong, and many, many more. In 2015 his _World in Jest_ project helped to connect disparate emerging comedy scenes, including many where he was the first foreign artist to perform with local scenes (Mongolia, Macedonia, Pakistan, and Bosnia-Herzegovina to name a few). This work led to his previous hour, _BadFamiliar_, and an on-going effort of the same name that hopes to help connect artists interested in crushing the notion that “familiar equals good” within their own work. 

Matt’s early years of touring, mid-late 90s to 2015, were primarily in North America. During this time he was racking up 40 weeks a year on the road; toured as opening act for household names; was featured on Netflix in its early days; released 5 albums he does not care for now; and was regularly spun on Sirius / XM Radio. 

In early 2025, Matt founded _Laughing Impact Project_, the civic-facing arts initiative producing this event (see above). Matt frequently lends his expertise and experience and performs the role of host/emcee/show-runner for various rallies, protests, fundraisers, and other activist events.
For more on Matt: [https://mattdaviscomedy.com](https://mattdaviscomedy.com)

events.title: 💙 GOTV Canvass Launch with Our State Delegates: Let’s Keep Braddock Blue!

sponsor.name: Rachna Sizemore Heizer for Braddock Supervisor

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join Team Rachna Sizemore Heizer and our Democratic State Delegates for our final GOTV Canvass Launch just 3 days before Election Day! The stakes couldn’t be higher, and we need all hands on deck to make sure every voter in the Braddock District knows what’s at stake in this special election.

Our opponent’s campaign is backed by strong Republican support and misleading messaging! He’s using slogans like “People Over Politics” and claiming to share Democratic values, but make no mistake: Mr. Balbuena is a Republican. To make matters more confusing, this year’s special election ballot will not include party labels; no “D” or “R” next to the candidates’ names. That means we must make sure every voter knows to look for and vote for Rachna Sizemore Heizer, DEMOCRAT for Braddock Supervisor.

Fairfax County deserves leaders who share our values supporting working families, public education, affordable housing, environmental protection, and an inclusive, welcoming community. We can’t afford to lose this seat and hand control to someone who doesn’t represent our priorities!

So grab your walking shoes and join us at Team Central Braddock Headquarters for this critical canvass launch. We’ll kick things off with remarks from our state delegates and campaign leadership before heading out to knock doors, talk to voters, and make sure they know when, where, and how to vote.

💪 We’ve come too far to stop now let’s finish strong and keep Braddock blue! 💙💙💙

events.title: Cultivating Courage by Covering the Corners

location.venue: Corners all over the Triangle and beyond!

events.description:
Join us on Sunday, December 7th from 11am-12:30pm, we will host “Cultivating Courage by Covering a Corner” a peaceful visibility event designed to build courage and unity in support of democracy. Small groups will gather on consecutive corners along a key stretch of road, holding positive, pro-democracy signs. The purpose is to build motivation for folks to join us. By standing together on multiple corners at once, we show our community that courage is contagious—that even small acts of presence can inspire others to stand up for shared values.

Each participant plays an essential role: being visible, being brave, and encouraging others to do the same. The goal is to create a ripple of courage that spreads across our community and beyond.

We’re bringing this event to thirty-one locations across eight communities —APEX, CARY, DURHAM, FUQUAY-VARINA, GARNER, HILLSBOROUGH, RALEIGH, and WILSON.

Please sign up on mobilize and also sign up for your corner on SignUp Genius:  https://www.signupgenius.com/go/10C0549A5AA23A1F8C43-60269608-cultivate#/

People will need to bring their own signs. Please also consider bring an American flag along with one of several other flags (rainbow flag, Palestine flag, Mexican flag, Ukraine flag), to make it clear we are not MAGA. We have rainbow flags for those who cannot get them. 

Please make signs that say, “Stand up, you are not alone!” “Resist!” “Courage is contagious!” 

We will have a safety call for those participating on Thursday December 4th at 8pm: https://www.mobilize.us/engageddurhamitesfordemocracy/event/867097/


Please join our Substack: https://substack.com/profile/115484101-engaged-durhamites-4-democracy

For more ED4D Mobilize Events: https://www.mobilize.us/engageddurhamitesfordemocracy/

events.title: LA WFP End of the Restorative Wellness
events.description:
Join us for a post-election wellness session, facilitated by Susanna Barkataki, an Indian immigrant intersectional feminist teacher with over 20 years of experience in trauma-informed and justice-rooted spaces. This session offers a sanctuary for rest in motion.

This will be a nourishing evening of restorative movement, breath, and reflection designed especially for organizers, activists, and community builders.

What to Expect
Gentle, accessible practices to release tension, soothe the nervous system, and rebuild your inner reserves. No experience needed. This is about rest and renewal.

Collective Care, Not Burnout
This session is timed at the end of a very long year, where many of us have been working tirelessly on special elections, local campaigns, and defending our vulnerable communities. This work can be tiring and often leads to burnout if not addressed.

WFP appreciates the hard work you have dedicated, and wants to give a few hours for you to focus on yourself, restore with your community, and enjoy some warm tea and snacks. Join us!

events.title: Show Up Saturday
events.description:
In this critical moment for our democracy, it is imperative that we continue to engage in peaceful protest against the Trump administration and its policies. Peaceful protest is not only a constitutional right—it is a moral responsibility. When those in power promote policies or rhetoric that threaten equality, justice, and the rule of law, silence becomes complicity.
Peaceful protest allows us to amplify the voices of the marginalized, hold leaders accountable, and affirm the core values that define our nation: freedom, dignity, and respect for all people. History has shown that nonviolent resistance—rooted in courage and solidarity—has the power to bring about real, lasting change.
We protest not out of hatred, but out of hope. We gather not to divide, but to demand unity based on truth and justice. By standing together peacefully, we demonstrate that the conscience of the people cannot be silenced and that democracy thrives only when citizens are engaged, vigilant, and unafraid to speak out.

events.title: Organizer Lab: Keep Clinics Open
events.description:
Are you organizing a Keep Clinics Open campaign in your community, or interested in starting one? Join our bi-weekly organizer lab, a space for campaign leaders and organizers to bounce around ideas, ask questions, and move forward local campaigns to keep Planned Parenthood and gender-affirming care clinics open in their communities. 

More about Keep Clinics Open below! ⤵️

In the face of nationwide disapproval, the MAGA-controlled Congress pushed through Trump’s budget, initiating a series of devastating cuts to essential social services for women, queer, and poor folks. This budget guts medicaid funding for Planned Parenthood, putting 200+ Planned Parenthood clinics in danger of reducing services or closing entirely. These funding cuts for Planned Parenthood follow months of attacks on federal funding for hospitals that provide gender-affirming care to trans youth, causing clinics across the country to stop providing this life-saving care to young people.

We must fight back to KEEP CLINICS OPEN. 

Through our KEEP CLINICS OPEN campaign, we are organizing from the ground-up to demand our state and local governments, school boards, universities, and even student governments AFFIRM our right to reproductive and gender-affirming care and act to BACKFILL federal funding cuts to keep clinics open and accessible to all.

We are looking for young people to bring KEEP CLINICS OPEN to their communities. No matter how progressive or conservative, ALL of our communities are under attack. Regardless of your political landscape or organizing experience, we are ready to help you build a path to keep clinics open in your community, and help neighboring communities do the same. 

Learn more here: FeministGeneration.Org/Keep-Clinics-Open

events.title: Jordan Wood in Gardiner! Town Hall at the Gardiner Area High School!
events.description:
Gardiner! Democratic House Candidate Jordan Wood is coming to meet you. We'll be at the Gardiner Area High School. Come out to meet Jordan, learn why he's the strongest candidate to defeat Paul LePage, and hear about what his plans as your next Congressman: sweeping campaign finance reform, passing the Ultra-Millionaire Wealth Tax, enacting universal childcare and addressing the affordability crisis head on.

Bring your friends and family!

Location: Gardiner Area High School Library
40 W. Hill Rd
Gardiner ME 04345


Event begins: 6:00 PM | Doors Open: 5:30 PM

::::::

Jordan Wood was born and raised in Lewiston and then Gardiner. Growing up in a family that lived paycheck to paycheck, Jordan experienced firsthand the challenges of economic insecurity: from his mother leaving the workforce due to unaffordable childcare, to later rejoining it when his father's job stopped covering healthcare. Jordan only made it to college through need-based student loans, and these early struggles shaped his understanding that families like his were hurt by corporate influence in Washington, inspiring him to dedicate his career to fighting corruption.

As Vice President of End Citizens United, Jordan helped lead the No Corporate PAC Pledge, a first-of-its-kind national effort to get members of Congress and candidates to refuse corporate PAC money. Because of his work, we went from 1% to 20% of Democrats rejecting corporate money, despite party leadership opposition. He later served as Chief of Staff to Congresswoman Katie Porter, taking on Wall Street banks and powerful financial interests. After witnessing the January 6th insurrection while barricaded in Rep. Porter's office, he co-founded democracyFIRST, a bipartisan organization that has successfully defeated dozens of election deniers threatening the free and fair administration of elections.

Learn More about Jordan Wood at ElectJordan.com Read Jordan's 50+ Ideas and Platform at ElectJordan.com/Platform ::::::

No audio or video recording without prior authorization.

We reserve the right to refuse entry at our sole discretion.

events.title: Newark DE Solidarity Brigade- Welsh Tract Rd
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!  No experience or supplies necessary.

Can you help us spread the word to help save Democracy and stand up for the Constitution?

The weekly message we will be sharing will be emailed out to those who sign up.

The Newark DE Solidarity Brigade is an opportunity to reach thousands and thousands of people in a short amount of time.  It can help us recruit new people and show a United Delaware to the masses!

It takes a small amount of effort to make a HUGE impact!

Solidarity/Visibility Brigades are typically done on overpasses and pedestrian bridges to share our message with the passing cars.
Unlike Protests on City streets, these Brigades reach out to thousands of people passing through our State, maybe from Red States, and maybe. just maybe, we encourage them to engage!   All we know is doing nothing, engages no one!   The average number of cars passing the brigades is well over 6000!

There are Nationwide Solidarity/Visibility Brigades and hoping Delaware can catch up to the outreach we are seeing in other states. Let's show them size doesn't matter.  That's why they call us "The Small Wonder"!
They are happening throughout Delaware- Claymont, New Castle, Newark, Middletown, Smyrna, Milford and Rehoboth with more and more popping up!

We participate on the Chapman Road Overpass of I-95 (near 80 Chapman Rd, Newark DE 19713), Welsh Tract Rd Overpass of I-95 (near Folk Memorial Park 98 Welsh Tract Rd) the Meadowood Pedestrian Bridge (South Meadowood Rd & Capitol Trail Newark 19711) and we recently deployed a message on the Elsmere Pedestrian Bridge  (676 South Union Street Wilmington DE)!

If you like to dance, wave,  sing, whatever your passion, we would love to stand beside you!

Reach out to    newarkdevb@gmail.com  with questions or to volunteer  and support the Brigades!   No experience or supplies necessary.


*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

events.title: Signs of Fascism (Savannah)
events.description:
Join us for a powerful silent demonstration organized by Coastal Georgia for Democracy (Savannah Indivisible).

**When**

Mondays and Fridays in November (rush hour times; see details)


**Where** 

Abercorn Street Between Lee and Jackson Blvds., in front of Buddy Carter's office.

**What to Expect**

Participants in the Signs of Fascism visibility event will stand and/or walk in silent witness, holding signs that highlight early warning signs of fascism. This display serves as a visual reminder of the characteristics we must remain vigilant against in protecting our democracy. 

**Part of a National Movement**

Similar "Signs of Fascism" visibility events have been taking place across the country, with groups meeting regularly to raise awareness about threats to democratic institutions. This spring, over 30 Nobel Laureates and scholars from more than 30 countries signed an open letter warning about the return of authoritarian and fascist tendencies globally. Community groups nationwide are responding with peaceful demonstrations, educational events, and visibility actions like ours to defend democratic values.

Our signs reference characteristics identified in historical fascist regimes, including pronounced nationalism, disdain for human rights, identification of enemies as unifying causes, supremacy of the military, controlled mass media, obsession with national security, suppression of labor power, disdain for intellectuals and the arts, and other antidemocratic patterns.

**What to Bring/Wear**

Wear all black

Signs (red on a black background) will be provided

Water and sun protection recommended

**Our Commitment**

A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action.

Elected after 2008’s Hurricane Ike, Joe served as the 55th mayor of Galveston, Texas. Mayor Joe, widely regarded as the city’s most responsive and accessible mayor in its nearly two-century history, led Galveston’s transformative recovery from an epic natural disaster.
