events.description:
## Feeding the Block Today Builds Freedom for Tomorrow.

When the government shuts down, it’s our communities that feel it first and hardest. Across Tennessee, families are already being hit by the pause in SNAP benefits and the rising cost of food. So we’re stepping up to take care of each other, because if we don’t, who will?

This November and December, The Equity Alliance is launching Feed the Block, a statewide community love initiative providing hot meals, food boxes, and essential resources every week from **November 5 through December 17** in Nashville, **Clarksville**, and Memphis.


We’re asking churches, nonprofits, and local businesses to join us by plugging in the resources and support you already offer. 

1. Volunteering with your team or congregation to distribute food from one of our hubs.

2. Sharing information about your community programs or services and becoming a part of our resource hub.

3. Hosting or sponsoring a week of meals as a **Block Captain**


Together, we can remind our neighbors that they’re seen, supported, and surrounded by a community that shows up when it matters most.




### Every table, every meal, every block — powered by our community.

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Wish you could tell your state representatives what is important to your family without having to go to Tallahassee? Have you heard of delegation meetings yet? 

Well, a lot of folks haven’t, and it’s time we change that. 

Florida Senators and Representatives from each local district attend these meetings to hear from their constituents what their top concerns are this legislative session. People attend these public meetings to identify solutions and share concerns about what we are seeing in our communities. If you want to see your elected officials make positive changes and fight for the issues you most care about, your local delegation is an important tool in that ever-growing momma toolbox. 

Want to speak about child care, education, and other issues impacting our families, but want to talk it through with someone first or get support on the process? Sign up here, and I will reach out to you ahead of your local delegation meeting: https://action.momsrising.org/survey/DelMeetings2025/

Feel ready to go and want some quick tips? 
Check out these great talking points built by the MomsRising Team and talking points from Progress Florida if you need inspiration!
https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/s3.momsrising.org/images/Florida_Delegation_Meeting_Talking_Points_.pdf
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dh1xIJF6Et0

events.title: Virtual Teach-In with Sarah Lerner, co-founder of Teachers Unify to End Gun Violence
events.description:
Joyful Resistance is thrilled to host a conversation and teach-in with Sarah Lerner, co-founder of Teachers Unify to End Gun Violence. Sarah is an educator at Marjorie Stoneman Douglas who hid with her students during the horrific shooting on 2/14/18. Teachers Unify is an organization that bridges the gap between the education and gun violence prevention spaces by communicating the realities of gun violence in our schools and communities. Its mission is to "amplify the educator voice for change."

Given that gun violence remains the leading cause of death for children in America, Sarah's passion for this issue and inclusion of educations of all kinds (school folks current/retired/former who support, guide, teach children, and keep them safe) is both vital and timely. 

Share with all of your educator friends and family and bring your questions!

events.title: A Constitution For 2076
events.description:
You are invited to a transformative workshop on Tuesday, December 2 from 9am-1pm
at Hygge Coworking Space at 1026 Jay St in Charlotte, NC

A continental style breakfast and lunch will be served.

Join us and people from around the state as we come together to reimagine North Carolina! This workshop is for people from a wide variety of professional and personal backgrounds and experiences - artists, futurists, organizers, legislators, community leaders, academics, concerned citizens, faith leaders, anyone who is interested in visioning and building coalitions for North Carolina's future.

With our partners from Democracy 2076 we will seek to imagine and develop democracy that is effective and responsive now and for the next generation. A democracy that is representative, and resilient in the face of change. We believe this is what will enable us to build a more inclusive, responsive, and representative democracy. We hope by the year 2076, we can have an amended constitution that will reflect everyday Americans in the year 2076.

We look forward to your participation in this pivotal conversation!

events.title: Yes You Canvass -- Indivisible Chicago's Canvassing School
events.description:
Curious about canvassing? We've got answers!

As you may have heard, knocking on voters' doors and engaging them in one-on-one conversations is the single most effective way to win their vote. But maybe you're hesitant about canvassing. A lot of people are! Or, maybe it's been a while and you need a refresher or just have questions about how it works. 

Whether you've never canvassed or just need to shake off the rust, this live training class is for you. We show you what to expect; lead you through the process step-by-step; share tips accumulated over years of experience; and answer all your questions and concerns. And we bring friends from Chicago improv companies to add a little fun and a lot of communication savvy. 

Indivisible Chicago excels at organizing and training canvassers. We invite you to come learn what it's all about!

events.description:
Join the **ACLU**, the **ACLU of Indiana**, and the **Rise4Freedom coalition** for an activist education training in **Bloomington, Indiana**, on **Saturday, December 6th**!

We are in the fight of a lifetime to defend our rights, our freedoms, and our democracy. **The Power & Purpose - Popular Education Training** is a **FREE, high-impact, one-day** experience designed to give you the tools to organize, mobilize, and lead in this critical moment. Our communities need bold action, and we need you in the fight.

You'll learn how to:

*   Organize effectively in your community 
    
*   Have persuasive conversations that move people to action 
    
*   Build lasting connections with others who are ready to rise to the moment 
    

Anyone is welcome to sign up. Organizing is relational, and the path forward depends on all of us. 

**SPACE IS LIMITED**, so **sign up now to reserve your spot**. All we ask is that you commit to the full day, and if you can, bring someone with you and have them register as well. Please note that we won’t be allowing anyone in who is NOT registered in order to ensure the security of the event and its attendees. **No guests will be allowed.**

**Now is the moment to stand up for our democracy, so join us for this training and be part of the movement for change.**

_Exact address and location will be made available at least 48 hours before the training to those who sign up._

events.title: Listen to Win: Empathetic Conversations Training with SwingLeftHoCoMD
events.description:
Listen to Win: Empathetic Conversations Training with SwingLeftHoCoMD

Politics is about persuasion—reaching out, person to person, and bringing others along. But persuasion doesn’t mean you’re rattling off statistics, arguing about policy, or convincing someone to do a 180º on the spot. In fact, persuasion starts with listening.

In a fractured political environment, it is both more challenging and more important to engage with those who might not vote like us (or not vote at all!). We know talking with voters works, but more often than not, Democratic campaigns start too late and target too narrowly. They underinvest in persuasion conversations, and ignore 1 in 4 potential voters because they’re unlisted or mislisted in the data Democrats rely on. Swing Left's new Ground Truth canvassing program will change that. By starting early and having empathetic listening conversations with every voter, we’re uncovering concerns that campaigns need to address, earning trust in communities that might feel overlooked, and making sure Democrats are speaking to what people actually want. That’s how we help Democrats flip the House in the 2026 midterm elections.

This new approach to voter contact means we’ll be talking with all kinds of people, and we know that can be intimidating. Whether you’re knocking on doors in a swing district, simply talking with a friend, or anything in between, honing your empathetic listening skills will help us engage in productive conversations—and ultimately change the hearts and minds we need to win. 

Come learn more about how empathetic listening conversations work, and how you can get involved now to win in 2026.

—

In 2024, Democrats lost the House by only 7,309 votes, handing Republicans the narrowest majority in nearly 100 years. Winning the House in 2026 is doable—and it’s the most impactful thing we can do to stop Trump. A House victory will give Democrats a critical federal lever: more power and more oversight to investigate government actions and political corruption, effectively stopping the MAGA legislative agenda in its tracks. Check out Swing Left’s strategy to win back the House: [swingleft.org/house](https://swingleft.org/house)

events.title: Day of Empathy WA
events.description:
Join us on February 11, 2026, at 9:00 AM at the United Churches of Olympia for the Day of Empathy, a powerful event dedicated to raising awareness and fostering understanding for those impacted by the criminal-legal system. 

The program will feature:
- Stories of impact from survivors and formerly or currently incarcerated folx
- Updates on legislative efforts to reform the criminal-legal system
- Trainings on how to lobby your representatives
- Meetings with legislators to discuss community issues and advocate for solutions
- A rally at the Capitol steps to close out the event
- Light breakfast, snacks, drinks, and lunch for all registered attendees

Don’t miss this opportunity to be part of the change and stand in solidarity with impacted communities!

Please enter the legislative district you live in when you sign up. If you don't know your legislative district, [here is a link](https://app.leg.wa.gov/districtfinder) to where you can enter your address and find it! Just make sure you have "legislative" selected and not "congressional" before clicking the "Find My District" button.


Day of Empathy is the nation’s largest day of action for criminal justice reform, & this wouldn’t be possible without everyone’s collective effort in fighting for what’s right. It brings together people from all walks of life who have been negatively impacted by America’s criminal justice system – from survivors of violent crime to those who are currently incarcerated individuals to the loved ones on the outside who advocate for their freedom and systemic reforms, from children of incarcerated parents to people on mass supervision to all community members impacted by crime, public safety issues, and violence.

events.title: NVM 2025 December Volunteer Meeting
events.description:
Join us on Zoom for our December Volunteer Meeting! We will review and wrap up our work and progress in 2025, extend a special thank you to our volunteers, and preview what our work will look like in 2026, where we will dive straight into a General Assembly session and special elections. 

A Zoom link will be sent out the day before the meeting.



Community Rules of Conduct and Engagement:

By signing up for this event, we assume that you will fully abide by our Community Standards and Rules of Engagement. If a volunteer is in violation of any one of these standards, they will be removed and barred from future events at our discretion. We do this in order to protect our staff and volunteers as well as create a safe and welcoming environment.

I will respect NVM staff who have organized this meeting as well as my fellow volunteers by being conscious of our time restraints, avoiding using harsh/foul language, and giving everyone a chance to speak. We will assume the good intent of all participants and staff.

NVM organizes around and centers the needs of working-class communities of color. Please keep in mind that the strategies & messaging we use have been developed to keep those communities at the center of our work. Therefore, the strategies & messaging we use may not match up with your specific expectations and may be different from what you've experienced working with other volunteer organizations. Please keep this in mind as we work together to build a more equitable Virginia that is home to all.

I recognize the reality that there could be changes regarding the scheduling of this event and its agenda. We will do our best to give you advanced notice if and when changes are made.

I will NOT share the Zoom information or any internal documentation with anyone else. We ask this for our own security.

events.title: Dec 6th - Los Angeles - People Over Billionaires Rally & March
events.description:
On  Saturday, December 6th we will gather for a peaceful rally and march in the neighborhoods where some of our country’s wealthiest corporate billionaires live.  They try to insulate themselves from realities on the ground and the real life pain and suffering they are causing while they enrich themselves.  They need to hear from us.  These events are also happening in San Diego, Silicon Valley and San Francisco on the same day.

We need to let them know that if the country keeps moving in the oppressive direction it is going, they will not be able to count on the consumer participation and financial assurance they depend on. Companies like Tesla and Target have begun to learn this. 

Our families and communities are under attack, with the federal government grabbing people off the streets without due process  and cutting vital services such as food assistance and healthcare.  We face all this, while a small group of very powerful and wealthy corporate billionaires get even richer. 

We will not be focusing on any particular homes, but instead march peacefully in the community in the spirit of unity and love, not division and hate.  

December 6th is not a one-off action but the beginning of sustained campaigning to help the corporate billionaires open their eyes to the harm they are fueling.

events.title: What comes after no kings? Five things we can do for democracy
events.description:
## About this program:
**Danielle Allen**, convening chair of the Coalition for Healthy Democracy and author of *Justice by Means of Democracy*, presents her ideas on policy innovations needed for a healthy democracy. We're called to envision what we want our democracy to look like, how we want it to function, and who we want it to support—what Danielle calls “renovating” democracy.

## About Our Speaker: 
Danielle Allen is a seasoned leader, public policy and public affairs professor, author, democracy advocate, and mom. Whether in her research lab or as a civic leader, Danielle works on democracy renovation: a new way of thinking about and investing to strengthen our country. Democracy renovation reconnects people to civic life and redesigns our political institutions and civic infrastructure so people have the tools they need to be responsible and effective citizens— and politicians have the incentives they need to deliver responsive and accountable representation. 

Danielle is a founder of multiple civic organizations including the Civics and History Inquiry Partnership, Educating for American Democracy, and Partners In Democracy. She is the author of Our Declaration and Justice by Means of Democracy, as well as the forthcoming Radical Duke: how one aristocrat-and the American Revolution—transformed Britain. A former columnist for the Washington Post, she now writes for The Renovator. 
Danielle is also the convening chair for the Coalition for Healthy Democracy, a ballot committee seeking to put ballot initiatives for an all-party primary and public records transparency on the November 2026 ballot in Massachusetts.

events.title: San Diego - ¡Marcha! El Pueblo Arriba, Los Multmillonarios Abajo
events.description:
El sábado 6 de diciembre nos reuniremos para una concentración y marcha pacífica en los barrios donde viven algunos de los multimillonarios más ricos del país. Intentan aislarse de la realidad y del sufrimiento que provocan mientras se enriquecen. Necesitan escuchar nuestra voz. Estos eventos también se llevarán a cabo en San Francisco, Los Ángeles y Silicon Valley ese mismo día.

Debemos hacerles saber que si el país continúa por este camino opresivo, no podrán contar con la participación de los consumidores ni con la seguridad financiera de la que dependen. Empresas como Tesla y Target ya han empezado a darse cuenta de esto.

Nuestras familias y comunidades están siendo atacadas: el gobierno federal detiene a personas en la calle sin el debido proceso y recorta servicios vitales como la asistencia alimentaria y la atención médica. Nos enfrentamos a todo esto mientras un pequeño grupo de multimillonarios poderosos y adinerados se enriquece aún más.

No nos centraremos en ninguna casa en particular, sino que marcharemos pacíficamente por la comunidad con espíritu de unidad y amor, no de división y odio.

El 6 de diciembre no es una acción puntual, sino el inicio de una campaña sostenida para ayudar a los multimillonarios corporativos a abrir los ojos ante el daño que están provocando.

events.title: Team Talarico: Volunteer Shift at a North Texas Food Bank Mobile Pantry
events.description:
Come volunteer with fellow Talarico supporters at a North Texas Food Bank Mobile Pantry to support our neighbors during the holiday season.

IMPORTANT
You must register with the North Texas Food Bank in order to participate in this event. Find the "Register" button on this link:

https://ntfb.org/get-involved/volunteer/

AFTER YOU HAVE REGISTERED
Please RSVP to this event and we can add you to our volunteer team for this shift.

EVENT DESCRIPTION
We will help unload, set up and distribute food directly to clients in a fast-paced, outside environment. Volunteers must have good verbal skills and physically be able to stand for long periods of time, bend, stoop and lift at least 25 pounds repeatedly throughout their shift. Courtesy and helpfulness are expected! Jobs may include the following:

Hand out intake forms and golf pencils by slipping them in cracked windows.
Direct lanes of traffic in the parking lot
Assist recipients get the food to their car
Move boxes at the staging site as needed.
Other site-specific duties

All attendees must be 18 years of age or older, but 13-17-year-old may volunteer if a guardian or a group leader (who has secured permissions to participate) are in attendance.

Check in will begin at 8:45 AM and orientation will begin promptly at 9:00 AM. OUR HUNGRY NEIGHBORS ARE COUNTING ON YOU TO ARRIVE ON TIME AND TO STAY FOR THE ENTIRE SHIFT.  If you are unable to complete the full shift, then please log into your account and cancel your registration. We hope you can join us another time.



***Please also note, this event is an event hosted by volunteers with Talarico for Texas, and James Talarico will not be at the event.

events.title: Yoga + Activism: Restore and Resist!
events.description:
Join us at Sol Space Chicago to bring together two powerful forces for change: mindful movement and collective action. This event offers a chance to nurture your inner well-being, forge community connections, and honor your commitment to protecting democracy.

The event is **FREE** and open to everyone, regardless of yoga experience or political experience. Kids are welcome! Activities will be available for them.

**What to Expect**

- 45 minutes of Yoga Flow for all levels. Whether you’re new to yoga or have practiced for years, you’ll feel welcome and supported.

- 45 minutes of Activism. After class, we'll work together to complete postcards that will drive voter turnout for key Senate races in 2026.

**Why Yoga & Activism?**
With all the ways that the stress of this political moment can affect your mind and body, yoga offers a way to slow down, reconnect with yourself, and renew your spirit. Yoga teaches us to live with awareness, compassion, and courage. Activism can be an extension of that practice, giving us the opportunity to turn those values into action. 

By pairing mindful movement with civic engagement once a month, we’re creating a space where community members can gather, recharge, and then channel that renewed energy toward positive change and connection.

events.description:

Join us for a community meeting to participate in the launch of the #GasFreeNYC campaign!

Fossil fuel use in buildings is New York City's top source of pollution. While Local Law 97 is successfully reducing emissions from large buildings, it does not cover the City's many smaller buildings.

The #GasFreeNYC campaign is the next essential phase to moving off fossil fuels: Winning public funding and requirements to help small building owners replace dirty old boilers with efficient heat pumps.

At the meeting, we'll discuss our campaign goals and plans and how to get involved in winning a #GasFreeNYC!

Refreshments will be served.

events.description:
Join Indivisible Western Queens in our recurring Visibility Brigade action. Also known as "rush hour resistance," the Visibility Brigade model was born in 2020 out of a frustration due to the lack of physical messaging in the real world regarding the existential crisis we face as a nation. People need “social proof” to know how best to act.

Indivisible Western Queens is a local chapter of the national Visibility Brigade, and our goal is to remind people of the crisis and that they are not alone, and give drivers under the overpass and a chance to engage in a toot of activism. It may be small but it's yet another way to mobilize the community. We need as many people as possible to join us in this fight to protect democracy in the face of rising authoritarianism.

events.title: Ground Avelo: Cancel ICE Air at Albany County Airport
events.description:
Avelo Airlines has become the first commercial airline to contract with ICE for secretive deportation flights—flights with no guarantees of due process or legal counsel. Human beings are being chained hand to feet inside of Avelo jets, and denied adequate food, water, and movement. The conditions inside these jets are so dangerous that Avelo staff have complained to Avelo corporate about inadequate safety for the passengers aboard. 

Despite calls for the Albany County Airport Authority, the Albany County Executive, and the Albany County Legislature to kick Avelo out of our community, our elected leaders have failed to take action.  It is time to make our voices louder and DEMAND that Albany County leadership and officials cancel its contracts with Avelo. We will not tolerate a corporation that facilitates the kidnapping of people for profit in our community.

events.title: Calls from Home: A Virtual Screening and Q&A
events.description:
**Please join us on Human Rights Day (December 10, 2025) for a virtual screening of *Calls from Home*, an exceptionally strong portrait of the grassroots approach to address the issue of mass incarceration in Appalachia.** This screening will be followed by a Q&A & panel with the director of the documentary and hosts of the radio show from which the documentary got its name. 

**Since 1980, over 350 prisons have been built in rural America, with Central Appalachia being one of the most concentrated regions of rural prison and jail growth nationwide.** For over two decades, WMMT-FM 88.7 Mountain Community Radio, located at the Appalshop media arts center in Whitesburg, Kentucky (population 2,139), has been sending out toll-free messages over the airwaves, from family members to their loved ones incarcerated far from home.

In *Calls from Home*, a longstanding radio program sends familial messages of love to people incarcerated in Central Appalachia. Directed by Sylvia Ryerson, a former DJ for the show, the documentary follows the weekly broadcast through prison walls, portraying the many forms of distance that rural prison building creates — and the ceaseless work to end the racist system of mass incarceration and family separation.

Join us for a virtual screening of *Calls from Home*, followed by a Q&A with director Sylvia Ryerson, Appalachian activist and former Calls from Home DJ Amelia Kirby, and current Calls from Home DJ Beckie Bowman.

events.title: Lakewood City Council: Public Comments on ICE
events.description:
Lakewood Indivisible is asking community members from Lakewood and local cities to join us at our 12/9 city council meeting to bring attention to the city council regarding the direct impact federal activities are having on Lakewood residents. If you are a Lakewood resident, we are asking you to sign up to speak during the public commentary at the end of the meeting. 

Be sure to sign your name on the city’s roster before the meeting starts. You will need to sign in early and stay through the whole meeting until the public comment portion at the end. Each person is allowed up to 3 minutes  to speak. Share your stories, your suggestions, and your demands that city council take steps to protect our community. If you are not a Lakewood resident, please come be a part of the audience and support our speakers. We will be keeping the speaking going as long as we can, so bring snacks and water. 

Recommended talking points: 

- How long have you been a Lakewood resident? What is your experience with this city?
- How are ICE activities impacting Lakewood businesses and residents?
- What are you asking the city council to do? (We are urging the city invest in Know Your Rights trainings, acknowledge those who have already been taken by ICE in Lakewood, disallow ICE from using city property to stage, notify the community when ICE is in the area, join other cities in legal action against the federal government)

If you would like assistance with writing or practicing your comments, please sign up for our workshop here: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfrUGeOhJlf2_6GL0u3a_TBGv0zyJwu_f09A4UMnV0Qa59-ew/viewform

events.title: Tyranny Recovery Group: Recover and Cocreate a Healthy Nation
events.description:
Many of us feel under constant pressure to fight or to submit. We are mobilizing and getting out there. While this is critical to the movement, also necessary is imagining the world that we actually want to live in.

What is the healthy nation we imagine living in when we fully confront authoritarianism—beyond ousting the current administration? How do we bravely act in ways that create solidarity, build healthy relationships, and enable responsible servant-leaders?

A healthy nation becomes first imaginable and then possible when we hear stories of people who have already created a society where trustworthy behavior is normal. A society where, when issues come up, people have a way of dealing with them that maintains mutual respect.

In this four-part series, we invite you to share your story of trust and self-accountability and hear Will’s research on healthy nations where people thrive in cultures whose way of life maintains a baseline of mutual respect. Together we will discuss living in a society where leaders are accountable and the people don’t feel pressured to be submissive and obedient.

It is our goal that you come away from these Zooms feeling excited about practical ways you could work towards building healthy communities and a healthy nation, and more clear about how beautiful life in a healthy nation could be.

Join Indivisible leader Sheridan Hill and gentle revolutionary Will Randolph to discuss moving forward from the current chaos to the other side.

Sheridan Hill is a retired biographer and third-generation campaigner for justice. Will Randolph lived in intentional community for ten years and is the author of “The Deepest Revolution.”

PASSCODE 647705. This a national Indivisible Zoom series.

events.title: ACLU Petition Collecting - Early Vote Centers
events.description:
Help Make Our Local Democracy More Representative - CALLING ALL MIAMIANS!

It’s time to push forward and ensure that Miami voters have the voice and representation they deserve. Join Stronger Miami as we collect petitions at early vote centers ahead of the Miami Mayoral Runoff to create a brighter future for Miami. Stronger Miami’s charter amendment for the City of Miami would:

•Move city elections alongside statewide elections: To increase voter participation, making it easier for working families to take part in our democracy, saving millions of dollars in taxpayer money.

•Expand the City Commission: To provide greater representation and ensure every community in Miami has a voice in how our city is run.

•Ban Commission districts from being gerrymandered: To prevent corrupt politicians from abusing the political process for personal gain.

This amendment will make our local elections fairer, more accessible, increase voter participation, and make our city government more reflective of the communities it serves. Collecting signatures is easy, and we’ll make sure you have everything you need to feel confident. Whether it’s your first time or your tenth, we’ve got your back with training, materials, and support. Get involved today and take action to build a Stronger Miami!

Stronger Miami’s charter amendment for the City of Miami would:

•Move city elections alongside statewide elections: To increase voter participation, making it easier for working families to take part in our democracy, saving millions of dollars in taxpayer money.

•Expand the City Commission: To provide greater representation and ensure every community in Miami has a voice in how our city is run.

•Ban Commission districts from being gerrymandered: To prevent corrupt politicians from abusing the political process for personal gain.

This amendment will make our local elections fairer, more accessible, increase voter participation, and make our city government more reflective of the communities it serves. Collecting signatures is easy, and we’ll make sure you have everything you need to feel confident. Whether it’s your first time or your tenth, we’ve got your back with training, materials, and support. Get involved today and take action to build a Stronger Miami!

events.title: El muro fronterizo: actualizaciones e impactos para México
events.description:
[Read in English](https://www.mobilize.us/skyislandalliance/event/868927/) 

En la cobertura de la frontera entre Estados Unidos y México, la conversación a menudo se centra en los impactos y las voces dentro de Estados Unidos. Pero la infraestructura fronteriza también afecta a las comunidades locales, los pueblos indígenas y la vida silvestre en México.

Te invitamos este 8 de diciembre a las 10 a.m. a nuestro próximo Coffee Break virtual, un panel y conversación abierta en español sobre la nueva construcción del muro fronterizo en la región de las Islas del Cielo y los impactos sociales y ecológicos que está generando.

Los panelistas estarán representando distintas organizaciones mexicanas que cuentan con experiencia y perspectiva de la frontera, basadas en su conocimiento sobre la historia y el contexto actual del muro fronterizo, estudios sobre los efectos en la fauna y los ecosistemas que conectan ambos países, recomendaciones que se han hecho al gobierno estadounidense y los proyectos de construcción actuales en la región. ¡Tus preguntas y opiniones serán parte fundamental de esta conversación!

¿Sientes que no sabes mucho sobre los proyectos en la frontera o que el pueblo mexicano no tiene una voz en este tema que causa injusticias? Entonces, este webinar es para ti.

events.title: The Border Wall: Updates and Impacts for Mexico
events.description:
[Leer en español](https://www.mobilize.us/skyislandalliance/event/868926/) 

In coverage of the U.S.-Mexico border, the conversation often focuses on impacts and voices within the U.S. But have you ever wondered how border infrastructure affects local communities, Indigenous peoples, and wildlife in Mexico?

We invite you this Dec. 8 at 10 a.m. to our next virtual Coffee Break, a panel and open conversation in Spanish about the new border wall construction in the Sky Islands region and the social and ecological impacts it’s generating.

Panelists will be representing various Mexican organizations with experience and perspective on the border, based on their knowledge of the history and current context of the border wall, studies on the effects on wildlife and the ecosystems that connect both countries, recommendations that have been made to the U.S. government, and current construction projects in the region. Your questions and opinions will be a fundamental part of this conversation!

Do you feel like you don't know much about border projects or that the Mexican people don't have a voice in this issue that causes so much injustice? Then this webinar is for you.

events.title: Know Your Rights on SB 59: The Transgender Privacy Act
events.description:
SB 59, signed by Governor Newsom last month, makes all court records for name and gender marker changes confidential beginning July 1, 2026. The law also allows people who filed their petitions before July 1, 2026 to request confidentiality now through a simple, streamlined process. 

This webinar will answer common questions about the law and walk through exactly how you can file a request to make your records confidential before the automatic protections take effect.

During the webinar, you’ll hear from experts at Equality California, TransFamily Support Services, All Family Legal, PC, and California Rural Legal Assistance, who will:

- Explain what SB 59 does and when it takes effect
- Walk through how to ask the court to make your records confidential now
- Share step-by-step guidance and sample forms you can use
- Highlight where to get free or low-cost legal help

This event is open to everyone, especially trans and nonbinary community members, legal aid providers, and advocates who want to help people take advantage of these new protections.

events.title: Online Town Hall with U.S. Senate Candidate Graham Platner
events.description:
Join U.S. Senate Candidate Graham Platner for an online Town Hall on Zoom on Monday, December 15th at 5:00PM Eastern. 

GRAHAM: I hope you'll come and check out this movement we're building to defeat Susan Collins and her multi-billionaire backers. Come out, ask questions, and bring a friend or three. I'll see you there.

I was born in Blue Hill and raised in Sullivan. I served four infantry tours in the Marine Corps and Army. After a decade overseas in Iraq and Afghanistan, I came home to Maine. I moved in three doors down from where I grew up, and now I run a thriving oyster farm with my wife Amy.

Sadly, for far too many, it has become impossible to live in the place they grew up. People my age and younger simply can't afford to live here anymore. Hard work is no longer enough to survive in Maine. Meanwhile, a tiny number of billionaires have amassed an incomprehensible amount of wealth and power. We have a government of billionaires, by billionaires, for billionaires.

I never expected somebody like me could run for the U.S. Senate, but we aren’t going to defeat Susan Collins with a cookie-cutter politician.

We have seen Democrats run against Senator Collins and lose, again and again and again. We have to start listening to our neighbors, who are simply not interested in the same old same old politicians. It’s time for something different. Please RSVP, and I look forward to meeting you.

events.title: Postcarding & Conversation with Candidate Adem Bunkeddeko
events.description:
Join us starting at 9:30am ET to write postcards, talk about the news, and hear from candidates and political leaders. If this is your first time joining this group, please sign on at least 15 minutes before the speaker start time listed below. 

Please answer the registration questions accurately and completely. Also, having your full name displayed will facilitate admission from the waiting room. We may request clarification from you in the waiting room chat. 

**Candidate in the Democratic Primary for NY State Comptroller Adem Bunkeddeko will join us on Tuesday, December 2, at 10:00am ET.**
 Adem T. Bunkeddeko is a lifelong public servant with two decades of experience across finance, government, and the nonprofit sector, dedicated to expanding economic opportunity for New Yorkers. Born in Queens to Ugandan refugees who fled civil war, Adem was raised in a rent-stabilized one-bedroom apartment, where his parents turned hardship into their own version of the American Dream. Through scholarships to prep school and college, he became one of the first in his family to graduate with a B.A. from Haverford College, followed by an M.B.A. from Harvard Business School. Adem began his career as a grassroots organizer with the Working Families Party before serving Brooklyn through roles at the Bedford Stuyvesant Restoration Corporation and Brooklyn Community Services, where he built programs connecting residents to education, job training, and meaningful employment. In leadership positions at the Empire State Development Corporation and the Local Initiatives Support Corporation (LISC), he helped develop initiatives to expand affordable housing, support small business growth, and advance environmental sustainability across New York. After the COVID-19 pandemic, Adem was asked to help rebuild Coro New York as Executive Director. As the organization’s chief executive, he led a successful financial turnaround and expanded programming to a broader, more diverse group of emerging leaders working to build a more equitable, inclusive, and innovative society. Adem has also worked in finance, partnering with companies committed to a “double bottom line” of profit and purpose. He currently serves on the boards of House of SpeakEasy and the Center for Justice Innovation, previously served on Brooklyn Community Board 8, and has run for U.S. Congress in Central Brooklyn.

We strive to build community, educate voters, and use our Sharpies to write to save democracy together. Write postcards with us or just join the conversation. If you need help getting started with postcarding, please visit our [FAQ](https://markersfordemocracy.org/postcarding/postcarding-faq).

If you are with the media and want to attend, you must notify us at markersfordemocracy@gmail.com at least two hours before the start of the event. All discussions are off the record.

This event is co-hosted by [Markers For Democracy](https://markersfordemocracy.org), [Downtown Nasty Women Social Group](https://linktr.ee/DNWSG), and [Team Min](https://linktr.ee/teammin
).

Please read the following in its entirety as I have some important information to share regarding our efforts for the upcoming food drive on December 20th at our Democratic Headquarters in Columbus from 9am to Noon.

As all of you may be aware, our local food banks (and national) are at a critical state with the recent and increasing influx of individuals/families needing assistance. During our last EC meeting, it was decided we would streamline our next two collection efforts to assure our neighbors in need have access to as many of the holiday meal essentials as possible. 

The food banks have provided us with a list of their needs which I have listed below. The Democrats in Mitchell and Avery Counties are gathering to celebrate the holidays, and we hope you will join us! We plan to ring in the holiday season at The Dispensary & Upper Club (269 Oak Avenue) in Spruce Pine at 5:00-9:00 p.m. on Monday, December 8th. All are welcome!

We will have a fun-filled evening with delicious food, great holiday music, some fun and games, words of wisdom from some of our 2026 candidates, and wonderful fellowship with our friends and neighbors!

The Mitchell County Democratic Party (MCDP) will be providing the turkey and yeast rolls. It is our hope that you (if you are able) will bring your favorite holiday side dish (e.g. casseroles, scalloped potatoes, macaroni & cheese, deviled eggs, corn, and etc.) or dessert to share with us. You should contact our banquet manager, Danna Gibson (dannagibson60@gmail.com), to let her know what you will be bringing so that we can ensure that we have enough to feed everyone.

The MCDP is a supporter of The Beacon Center of Spruce Pine, an overnight warming center that offers protection from the cold weather when it is a Code Purple (30 degrees or below) night, The mission of the Beacon Center is to provide a warm, safe, non-judgmental space to sleep during extreme cold for the Mayland community and surrounding areas. This year, we are asking our attendees to bring at least one (or more) pop-top non-perishable food item(s) so that we can help the Beacon Center provide its guests with nourishment during their stay. Some items you might consider are:  cans of soup (any kind) or chili; Vienna sausage; baby cereal; Chef Boyardee spaghetti; individual packs of cookies or chips; small containers of puddings, Jello, or applesauce; individual packs or cans of tuna fish; and, canned vegetables. Please remember that all cans must be pop-top items.

We certainly look forward to seeing you on December 8th!

events.title: This Is What Democracy Looks Like - Decoding How Government Works
events.description:
Democracy Decoded: How Government Really Works and Our Role In It 

Have you wondered what qualifies someone to run for President—or how laws are actually made and passed? Are you curious why Congress sometimes gets stuck, or how the Supreme Court decides which cases to hear? If you’ve ever wished you understood how our government is supposed to work for you, this course is for you!

Introducing: Understanding Our Government - A multi-class educational series for anyone new to U.S. civics or seeking a clear, practical overview.

Engaged learning with real-time relevance on these and other subjects:  
•	The basics of presidential qualifications and elections
•      The roles courts, Congress, and the President really play
•	How bills move through Congress to become law [For Washington 
        residents, we will provide a separate event on how  
        the Washington State Legislature works]
•	What “checks and balances” really means (and why it matters)
•	How ordinary citizens can participate, influence, and stay informed
•	How the branches of government work (and where they sometimes 
        clash)
•	How laws and policies are made—and how you can influence them
•	Tools for staying informed and being heard as a citizen

As Senator Sheldon Whitehouse reminds us: “Citizens will always have the power to shape the future of their country.” 

Bring your curiosity and open mind, along with your questions, meet your neighbors, and discover how you fit into the story of our democracy.

Everyone is welcome. Let’s learn, discuss, and empower each other—one session at a time.

events.title: Donate the Day After Thanksgiving
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event!

On November 9th the headline on the Arapahoe County website read: “The Shutdown’s Silent Crisis: SNAP Benefits Halted, Neighbors Need Food Help NOW”. More than 75,000 families in our community are experiencing food insecurity. 

Instead of a rally this month, we will be accepting grocery and hygiene items to donate to IFCS (Integrated Family Community Services), a local food bank that has partnered with the community to alleviate hunger since 1964. 

We welcome ANY item you can find in a grocery store, provided those items are unopened with an expiration date in 2025 or later. Toiletries and feminine hygiene items are particularly appreciated. Please don't donate anything you wouldn't offer as a gift to a neighbor, as these ARE our neighbors! 

You can drop goods off in the Prince of Peace parking lot at 7000 South Windermere between 1:00 and 4:00 pm on Friday, Nov 28th. If you cannot make it during these collection times or you prefer to provide financial support, contact IFCS (ifcs.org) or a local food bank of your choice. 

Hunger doesn't end with a nice Thanksgiving meal. Celebrate your good fortune by contributing to neighbors who need our assistance. 

Thank you for supporting our neighbors!  Please Note: We will NOT be accepting financial contributions in any form. Search for "food banks in Littleton Colorado" and donate directly to your preferred organization, or contribute through ColoradoGives.org

events.title: Michigan for the Many Ballot Initiative Justice Captain Training

sponsor.name: Michiganders for Money Out of Politics

events.description:
Come join organizers at the Urban Core Collective to learn about how to be a **Justice Captain**, leading the fight on two exciting ballot initiative campaigns that will make Michigan work for everyday people rather than the wealthy few!

- [**Invest in MI Kids**](https://investinmikids.org/): raising over $1 billion annually for public schools in Michigan through a fair share income tax on Michigan highest earners

- [**Mop Up Michigan**](https://mopupmichigan.org/): banning utilities and state contractors from donating to MI politicians, closing the largest dark money loophole in state law (the issue ad loophole). 

Being a Justice Captain means stepping into your power and helping others step into theirs. It means believing that change starts with us: our voices, our stories, and our willingness to act for our communities.  By becoming a Justice Captain, you're not just collecting signatures. You're helping ignite a movement, one conversation, one connection, one courageous step at a time.

The 1.5-2 hour in-person training will provide information on each of the two ballot initiatives, practice on "pitching" the initiatives to potential signers, and comprehensive training on what makes a valid signatures. You will also receive petitions, clipboards, supplies, a free campaign t-shirt and totebag. Food is also provided (please fill out the Google form to confirm attendance and indicate dietary needs). 

Kids are welcome if their presence makes your attendance at training possible.  We have a small play area, as well as side rooms where kids can hang.  Feel free to bring them a tablet or other activities to keep them busy. 

NOTE: If you don't have time or capacity to come to UCC to be trained, please visit the [Invest in MI Kids volunteer hub](https://investinmikids.org/volunteer-hub) and follow steps 1 and 2 for a 10-minute virtual training on signature collection (and note UCC as the organization in the form for step 1).  The virtual training will be less comprehensive than the UCC version, but when you pick up petitions, you will get an info sheet with additional information about the ballots.

Voices & Values™ – A Civic Call to Action for Justice, Dignity & the American People

What to Expect:

Join Her Excellency Roné de Beauvoir and our national team for a peaceful, solutions-focused campaign event designed to elevate the voices of everyday Americans while defending the values that make democracy real: dignity, safety, healthcare, housing, education, and hope.

This is not a protest — it's a participatory civic gathering for those ready to be heard and ready to act.

Welcome + Campaign Overview
Learn how Voices & Values™ is uniting citizens through monthly civic action

Key Topic of the Month
A focused discussion on the month's issue (i.e., healthcare, housing, democracy, etc.)

Civic Action Toolkit
Learn how to take real action — from letter-writing to peaceful social media campaigns

Community Commitment Circle
Attendees share what they’ll do next to uplift their communities and defend democracy

Closing with H.E. Roné de Beauvoir
An inspiring message for the month ahead

Each month, we elevate one national issue with full public engagement: speeches, articles, livestreams, policy highlights, graphics, social media activations, voter education, and grassroots coalition-building. Under the guiding banners of the NO KINGS™ and INDIVIDUAL™ platforms, this campaign puts power back into the hands of everyday people — and builds a bridge between civic action and political accountability.
It’s not just a call to vote — it’s a call to rise. speak. act.

Because silence is complicity. And America needs more than politicians — it needs voices with values.

events.title: Voters of Tomorrow Raleigh: Politics AT the Dinner Table; Removing Taboo of Political Discourse

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description: "No politics at the dinner table!” In an environment with so much division, politics are often a subject that is not spoken about– especially in environments with differences of opinion. With holidays approaching and large gatherings around the table, many Americans across the country worry about these conversations coming up, and when politics do come up, they try to end the conversation as quickly as possible. According to the APA, 72% of adults hope to avoid political conversations with family members over the holidays, and 38% of American adults don’t want to see people they disagree with politically altogether.  Although it is important to remember that political discourse with people you agree with doesn’t have to be something that is avoided. A study done by the Pew Research Center shows that discussing politics helps reduce polarization and strengthens empathy and critical thinking, overall helping our democracy grow stronger. So, how do you handle conversations with people you don’t agree with, and what do you do when people step out of line? Come learn tips and tricks with VOT Raleigh and then practice these very skills in some political conversations. And since this is all to prepare for holiday meals, we will be enjoying a meal ourselves, Friendsgiving style! Join us for a night of dialogue, community, and good food; bring not only a dish but also your opinions and an open mind!

location.venue: Belle Isle Library - Metropolitan Library System

events.description:
*NOTE NEW LOCATION*

Join us for our Indivisible OKC monthly meeting on Saturday December 13th, 1:00 PM at the BELLE ISLE Library.

Meet this month's guest speaker: Erika Wright

Wright is the Oklahoma Education Justice Organizer for Advance Oklahoma’s Kids, a project of the Oklahoma Appleseed Center for Law & Justice. In this role, she works with state and national partners to shape strong public education policy and mobilize communities in support of Oklahoma’s schools. She is also the founder and director of the Oklahoma Rural Schools Coalition, a grassroots advocacy network of 18,000 members across all 77 counties.

Erika will introduce a preview of Better Outcomes for Oklahoma’s Kids (B.O.O.K.)—a bold five-year education agenda developed through a year-long research process to shift the narrative around public schools in our state. Inspired by the landmark bipartisan House Bill 1017 of 1990, B.O.O.K. outlines 16 policy recommendations across four themes: strengthening the teaching profession, ensuring adequate resources, improving student performance, and creating safe, supportive schools. With more than 700,000 Oklahoma students depending on public education, B.O.O.K. 2030 charts a clear path to stronger schools and better outcomes for every child.

events.description:
**Volunteers like you are essential to our vision of an Oklahoma where no one goes hungry.**

Through this on-site volunteer experience, volunteers like you sort, pack and prepare food for a variety of Regional Food Bank Programs. Activities may include:

- Assembling sacks of nutritious food for the Food for Kids Backpack Program
- Packing Commodity Supplemental Food Program boxes full of food for seniors living on fixed incomes
- Sorting and packing bread, produce, package meals and/or cans
- Tagging bags
- Cleaning
- Prepare and package fresh meals in Hope’s Kitchen, where the temperature is 55 degrees, so please dress accordingly.  

Because the Regional Food Bank's inventory changes daily, the Regional Food Bank cannot guarantee volunteers who sign up to work in the Volunteer Center will pack and prepare food for a specific program.

**The minimum age requirement is 8 years.** Volunteers under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an adult.

As a reminder, volunteers will enter through the Volunteer Center entrance, not the main entrance. Please look for the double doors toward the north end of the building with the Volunteer Center sign on the building.

events.title: Join us on zoom, let's flood representatives with calls. Most Mondays @12PM PST
events.description:
Are you upset about the dismantling of our democracy, the theft of millions of Americans’ private information, the acquiescence of many of our elected officials, the market manipulation, attacks on our healthcare and social security, the Republican intent to take away a woman’s right to vote, and more? You can take action.

One easy thing you can do that truly does matter, is make calls to your elected representatives, and let them know how you feel and how you expect them to act. Maybe you want to call your Congress Member or Senator but just haven’t done it yet. Or, do you feel hesitant about doing it? You know what you want, but you aren’t sure what to say. Maybe you want to make the calls, but procrastination keeps winning the day.

We’ve got a solution, and we plan to make it easy and rewarding by doing it together. Join us on zoom on Mondays, beginning on November 17, at noon Pacific time, and we’ll provide you with everything you need to make those calls. Phone numbers, scripts, everything you need except your telephone.

We will show you how it works, and then we’ll all make some calls. We’ll then spend a few minutes talking about the calls we made, feel good because we did it, and make plans for another day when we can make calls together, flood our representatives and fill up their voice mail boxes, and even send emails if we can’t leave messages.

Join us for an easy and effective action you can take. One half hour is all you’ll need. You can make a difference. We are in this together. Let’s make sure our elected officials know how we feel, what we expect, and that there are millions of us across America who demand Democracy and the protections of our constitution.

Come help to write post cards and letters to support democracy. The goal will be to write 6 letters and 10-15 postcards. The letters go to Tillis, Budd, Harrigan, Trump, the Supreme Court, and DHS (ICE). The postcards will go to voters.

For the letters, we’re writing very short LETTERS to our reps and the White House demanding that they fund healthcare, release the Epstein files, stop treating progressive Americans as enemies, etc. Plenty of topics to pick from. To the Supreme Court, we’re asking that they uphold the constitution and stop enabling Trump’s power grab. And to ICE, we’re demanding that they Unmask ICE agents and reminding them that secret police are unAmerican.

The letters will be SHORT – I have sample text you can copy. None are longer than two sentences. The idea is to send letters because they require more work to open and sort out so it makes more of an impact when they’re piled up in Congress, the White House mail room, and the Supreme Court.

With our extra time, we’ll be sending postcards to voters to encourage turnout for elections all up and down the ballot. MAGA reps don’t appear from nowhere. They come out of school boards, city councils, sheriff offices, etc. We need to fill those lower offices with people who support our values and are willing to defend democracy.

We will provide some supplies but feel free to bring along postcards, stationery, envelopes, notecards (even Birthday and Christmas cards work), etc. if you have them. If you have postcards stamps lying around, or really older stamps of ANY denomination, feel free to bring those too. If you don’t have any of those things, please come anyway! events.description:
Making Democracy work today needs more than using your one vote in the voting booth or donating to help a candidate. The neighborhood caucus is where American grassroots Democracy starts. Minnesota will hold local caucuses in every district all over the state on Tuesday, February 3rd, 2026. But the work to empower Democracy starts now. Any political party that does not arrange to have caucuses statewide will not be on the ballot.

Come discover how candidates become legally entitled to run on the ballot as DFL candidates, and whether attending your local caucus is "important" to keep Democracy functioning? Trump and MAGA aren’t invincible. Together, we can stop their assault on our democracy, our neighbors, and our future. events.title: Momentum: Books in Motion - Life After Cars
events.description:
Momentum: Books in Motion brings riders, readers, and neighbors together to explore ideas that shape safer, more connected communities. Each gathering begins with conversation over coffee, a cocktail, or a pint, followed by a short, social ride (3–5 miles) to keep ideas — and wheels — turning.

You don’t need to finish the whole book or be a “book-club person.” Come curious, come as you are, and join the discussion.

Format: Discussion → Short Ride → Good Company


📘 Book 1: Life After Cars By Sarah Goodyear, Doug Gordon & Aaron Naparstek

Venue: The Wild Detectives, Bishop Arts

Dates: Nov 15 • Dec 6 • Jan 17 • Jan 31 • Feb 21

Time: 11:00 AM – 1:00 PM (ride to follow)


What happens when we imagine cities designed for people instead of traffic? In Life After Cars, the hosts of The War on Cars podcast explore how communities can thrive when we reclaim our streets, slow down, and reconnect.

Each session dives into a few chapters at a time — no pressure to keep pace, just great conversation and ideas you can take back to your own neighborhood.


Schedule at a Glance:

11/15 Kickoff Discussion: What does “life after cars” mean to you?

12/6 How We Built for Traffic: Re-imagining our streets in DFW

1/17 Guest Speaker Session            

1/31 Designing for People: Human-scale design and joy in the street

2/21 Reflection Ride + Wrap-Up: What will your life after cars look like?


What to Expect:

Meet new people interested in better streets and community life.

Enjoy casual conversation — not a lecture or classroom.

Take a relaxed 3–5 mile social ride after each session.

All bikes and experience levels welcome.

events.title: Be a Conscious Consumer This Holiday Season!
events.description:
Conscious Consumption means understanding the goods and services you buy have an impact on the world beyond your personal use; it also considers the environmental, social, and political impact of your spending.  

Conscious Consumption for the holidays addresses everything from what you buy, to where you buy it, to how you wrap it.  Since many companies make most of their profits around the holidays, your spending this time of year has extra impact!   

Sign up on Mobilize to pledge you will be a Conscious Consumer this Holiday season.  Full details are at the link; read on below for key points: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1YvVkTCp5mkJT8yNgKDxSrjcwUMApo6PJtR-dTtMkVSs/edit?usp=sharing.  

What to buy - buying less stuff, buying secondhand, giving practical gifts, gifts from non-profits and charities are ways to have more environmental and social impact with your holiday spending.  

Where to buy - supporting local stores and online small businesses helps redistribute wealth away from the large corporations and oligarchs.  If you shop large chain stores, know that Costco, Burlington and REI (among others) support liberal values and democracy better than does Amazon or Home Depot (among others).  Please consider this when deciding where to shop. 

How to wrap - think reusable and recycled for your wrappings, which is better for the environment and your wallet. 

This a local Indivisible event!   Some recommendations are customized for Northern Virginia.  But the ideas apply throughout the U.S.

events.title: Allegheny Go Enroll-a-thon
events.description:
**Join Pittsburghers for Public Transit (PPT) for our Allegheny Go Enroll-a-thon in the Hilltop!**

Allegheny Go is a reduced fare program for Allegheny County transit riders receiving Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits. This program was made possible by years of advocacy and the raised voices of transit riders, neighbors, and community groups saying that the price of fares should not determine who can access essential resources and services. As the expenses of everyday living go up, our communities are in even more need of programs that lift the burden of transportation costs and promote wellbeing.

If you or someone in your household is a SNAP recipient, you could receive 50% off  your Pittsburgh Regional Transit (PRT) rides! To qualify for this discounted fare program you must: 

- Be a resident of Allegheny County 
- Be between the ages of 12-64 
- NOT already have a PRT discounted fare pass 
- Be currently enrolled in SNAP

The numbers are in, and we know that there are thousands of eligible families who have yet to register for this incredible cost saving program. Registration only takes minutes and PPT wants to help you make it happen! **Drop in anytime within our two hour window for registration support, snacks, and other relevant information.** 

For more information or to register for Allegheny Go independently, visit: https://discountedfares.alleghenycounty.us/

To read more about PPTs Fair Fares Campaign, visit: https://www.fairfaresnow.com/

CLP is not the host or organizer of this event. CLP does not support, sponsor, or represent this group or event.

events.title: Mutual Aid Sunday at Kruger Pines — Building the Kruger Pines Grocery Buddy Program
events.description:
Mutual Aid Sunday at Kruger Pines — Building the Kruger Pines Grocery Buddy Program

Host: Randy Chase — Seniors for Peace / No Kings Alliance
Location: Kruger Pines Senior Housing Clubhouse, 47 N Knoll Rd, Mill Valley
When: Every Sunday, 4:00 PM – 5:30 PM

We’re launching something real at Kruger Pines — a weekly Mutual Aid program dedicated to supporting the 56 households in this senior apartment community. With the continued government shutdown and ongoing gaps in senior services, many residents here are living with quiet struggles: food insecurity, mobility challenges, technology barriers, and isolation.

As a new resident of Kruger Pines, I’m developing the Kruger Pines Grocery Buddy Program — a neighbor-powered support network that pairs volunteers with residents to make sure everyone has food access, regular check-ins, and the human connection we all deserve.

This early phase is all about assessment.
We’re meeting neighbors, listening, and learning what each household needs so we can build a reliable, volunteer-driven safety net.

This Sunday event kicks off an every-Sunday series at the Kruger Pines Clubhouse. If you can only swing by for a few minutes, that’s perfect. If you can stay longer, even better. Come when you can — the work continues each week, and your presence strengthens the community we are building.

This is how we build community power: person to person, neighbor to neighbor, week by week.

No Kings / Seniors for Peace Code of Conduct:
We practice nonviolence, compassion, and respect — no exceptions.

events.title: Ohio Solar Supporters Webinar: Deep Canvassing & Rural Organizing
events.description:
Join Ohio Citizen Action for a conversation on deep canvassing, rural organizing, and community engagement in Ohio.

On December 1st at 6 PM, OCA Director of Programs, Bella Bogin and Rural Projects Coordinator, Jo Baldwin will share how they use deep canvassing and intentional, relationship-focused outreach to build trust across rural communities.

Drawing from their on-the-ground experience, they’ll discuss: What deep canvassing is and why it works, how rural organizing differs from traditional outreach, insights from conversations with voters, residents, and community leaders, and lessons from the field in places where clean energy development is both promising and challenging

This webinar will also highlight Morrow County, where residents are preparing for the December 10 public hearing on the proposed Crossroads Solar Grazing Center. Bella and Jo will walk through the dynamics on the ground, why the project matters, and how OCA is supporting community members ahead of the hearing.

Whether you're a seasoned organizer, a clean-energy advocate, or simply curious about how meaningful conversations can shift perspectives, this session will offer practical tools and firsthand stories from the field.

President Trump and Members of Congress have just passed a budget bill that represents one of the largest transfers of wealth from the working class to the obscenely rich in American history. As a result of the legislation, 16+ million Americans will lose their health care and it will result in 51,000 preventable deaths; more than a million children will go hungry; and working-class Americans will not be able to afford college.

This isn’t about party politics.

events.title: Weekly Taylor St Bridge Bannering Over I-8 | Monday Afternoons
events.description:
Park in front of The Remy (north side) or at the Taylor Street Park and Ride (south side).

We provide large physical messaging in the real world to connect with and activate voters to demonstrate that resistance is possible. Bring a sign for cars on the bridge or just wave to the cars passing below. You can also bring a flag, chair, bubbles, music, or anything else you want in order to have a good time!

Rules and Protocols

1. We avoid doing anything that could either harm ourselves or anyone else. This includes stepping into traffic, holding a sign where it could fall onto cars below, climbing fencing, etc.

2. We must not block pedestrian and bike traffic, so please keep the middle of the overpass and/or sidewalk clear to allow them to pass.

3. We supply the messages, you supply the waves. However, you are welcome to also display your own poster boards. Just avoid any messaging that would be rated above a PG-13.

4. We don’t litter. If we find litter, we pick it up and throw it away.

5. We don’t use stickers or anything that leaves a permanent mark on the overpass. However, chalk is okay and even encouraged.

6. If someone from the ‘opposition’ comes up to talk with us, do not engage with them. Best to just ignore them. One member will be designated to handle them and video record any aggressive interaction so that you can go right on waving.

7. We take lots of pictures and videos during our action for circulation on social media. If you prefer not to be included, please let us know and/or consider wearing a mask.

8. Should law enforcement pay us a visit, only the designated point person from the group should address them.

9. Ignore the middle fingers and negativity coming from some of the cars below. For every one of those confused folks, you are providing hope to another 100 people!

10. The Visibility Brigade is a non-violent, informal volunteer group in which we all participate with an understanding that our own actions are our personal responsibility and we accept our own personal liability. You participate with this understanding.

Feel free to reach out to VisibilityBrigadeSanDiego@gmail.com with any questions.

events.title: 🍓⭐️ Strawberry Coffeehouse Collective (Work
events.description:
My name is Randy Chase, I’m 62, and I’ve spent my whole life organizing for communities just like ours.
My parents met at a state Democratic convention, so political organizing wasn’t just a thing we did — it was the family sport. I grew up at a dinner table where campaigns were strategy sessions and community care was a shared obligation.

I’m here because the seniors, workers, and families of Marin deserve real support, not corporate platitudes. Starbucks workers in Strawberry show up for us every day — and until the corporation steps up, we’re going to step in together.

Seniors for Peace is launching this daily meet-up to build a community-backed safety net for our baristas: real benefits, real support, and real neighbor-to-neighbor solidarity. It doesn’t have to be complicated — it just has to be done.

I’m grateful you’re here. Let’s build something strong enough that other neighborhoods can copy it.

Cumberland County saw historic gains in the November 5 election — and Mechanicsburg and Upper Allen Township were part of that success, with six Democrats winning their races. events.title: Workshop: 'Do the Work: An Antiracist Activity Book'
events.description:
This isn’t your average book club. **Do The Work! is a workbook packed with hands-on exercises, quizzes, coloring pages, Q&A prompts, and real talk about white supremacy and how we dismantle it — together.** Whether you’re new to the work or deep in it, this 5-session series offers a welcoming, challenging, and creative space to reflect, engage, and grow.

We’ll laugh, listen, learn, and lean into discomfort. You’ll bring your workbook, your voice, and maybe some crayons. We’ll bring community, courage, and a commitment to change.

Ready to be the change you want to see? Let’s do the work.
We’ll laugh, listen, learn, and lean into discomfort. You’ll bring your workbook, your voice, and maybe some crayons. We’ll bring community, courage, and a commitment to change.

Ready to be the change you want to see? Let’s do the work. space is for learning, sharing, and growing together. Bring your workbook, your questions, and your courage. 

Join us for a 5-session workshop where we’ll share what we learned from doing the exercises in *Do The Work! An Anti-Racist Activity Book* by W. Kamau Bell & Kate Schatz.

## Who is this for?
As the authors say:
“This book is for white people... This book is not just for white people. White supremacy messes with all of us.”
If any of these sound like you, this space is for you:

* You know the system’s broken and want to help fix it
* You were (or weren’t) shocked by Trump’s election — and want to prevent it from happening again
* You’ve marched and asked, “What’s next?”
* You want to understand white privilege and help dismantle it
* You already know a lot — and want to share your perspective
* You believe white supremacy is a cancer on our culture and democracy

Are you ready to be the change you want to see?

BUY THE BOOK: This is a workbook — you’ll write in it, color it, tear out pages, and make it yours. Library copies won’t work.

Find it on Amazon or other booksellers (shipping may take longer). 
Price: ~$18–$20.


[Bookshop.org](https://bookshop.org/p/books/do-the-work-an-antiracist-activity-book-kate-schatz/6eb15192319301fd)

[BetterWorldBooks](https://www.betterworldbooks.com/product/detail/do-the-work-an-antiracist-activity-book-9781523514281)


[Thriftbooks](https://www.thriftbooks.com/w/do-the-work-an-antiracist-activity-book-for-all_kate-schatz_w-kamau-bell/27415287/#edition=58578730&idiq=47848417)


Need help covering the cost? Message noelle@indivisibleakron.org privately.

Optional: Bring crayons, markers, or colored pencils! This is an interactive workshop! Color while you listen.

You do NOT have to have attended every session. You don’t have to complete all the work in each chapter. We do ask, however, that if you don’t Do The Work, you come with a listening intent, and give priority to those who are Doing The Work.

events.title: 📣 Planning for Progress: Help Shape the Future of Pinellas County Schools-Dunedin High School
events.description:
📣 Planning for Progress: Help Shape the Future of Pinellas County Schools
Pinellas County Schools is hosting a series of Planning for Progress community meetings — and your voice is essential. As the number of school-age children in Pinellas County shifts, the district is gathering public input to guide decisions about enrollment, facilities, and the long-term future of our schools.
These conversations are especially important this year as Florida’s “Schools of Hope” rules create new pressures on districts — including forced co-locations and facility takeovers that can impact school utilization decisions. Your feedback helps ensure that community needs, not state-level mandates, drive the planning process.
💬 What to Expect
District leaders will present current information and gather community feedback on key topics, including:
📉 Population trends & enrollment projections
🏫 School building utilization & long-term facility planning — an area directly affected by “Schools of Hope” requirements
💡 New school programming & innovative learning opportunities
🔄 Potential grade configuration changes, consolidations, or closures, including how outside pressures may shape district decisions
This is an opportunity to understand what’s happening, ask questions, and make sure your community’s voice guides the future.
📅 Community Meeting Schedule
All meetings are 5:30–7:00 PM.
Monday, Nov. 17 – Largo High School
Tuesday, Dec. 2 – Dunedin High School
Thursday, Dec. 4 – Hollins High School
Tuesday, Dec. 9 – Lakewood High School
Attend the meeting closest to you — and bring a friend, neighbor, or fellow parent.
🤝 Why Your Voice Matters
Across Florida, “Schools of Hope” rules allow state-approved operators to move into or take over public school buildings — often without local consent. These policies can influence district planning decisions, especially around building capacity and “under-utilization.”
Community turnout ensures that:
✔ Local needs and lived realities guide decisions
✔ District leaders hear directly from families and educators
✔ Public schools remain strong, supported, and rooted in their neighborhoods
📢 Get Involved
The future of public education in Pinellas County is being shaped now. By showing up, asking questions, and sharing your insight, you help ensure students and communities have the strong, stable schools they deserve — not decisions driven by Tallahassee.

While we decorate gingerbread houses, we’ll talk about why housing has become so hard to afford, how today’s policies and incentives shape who gets to live where, and how Anna’s Fair Deal Housing Plan aims to make stable, attainable housing a reality for normal people again.

This event is welcoming for all ages! 
Kids are challenged to design the most exciting houses for our gingerbread citizen while we encourage adults to take on the challenge of housing as many of our gingerbread people affordably as they can!


Where: Morristown, NJ
When: December 20th, 2025
What to bring: Gingerbread kits provided! Suggested donation of $25 to cover materials

events.title: Canvassing with Empathy - Zoom Training
events.description:
CANVASSING WITH EMPATHY (A.K.A. Deep Canvassing) is a method of voter outreach that involves having authentic, empathic conversations with individuals about how they want government to serve them. Unlike traditional canvassing (which uses a script designed to persuade constituents to support a candidate or cause), CANVASSING WITH EMPATHY fosters a more in-depth and genuine way of connecting with voters to discuss the importance of electing leaders who represent one’s values and interests.

The purpose is to build sincere relationships with voters by actively listening to their beliefs and experiences and by sharing personal stories to foster common ground, empathy, and mutual respect.

SWING LEFT and INDIVISIBLE groups are partnering to conduct multiple trainings and canvassing efforts in key swing districts across the U.S., including Oregon’s critical 5th congressional district. The goal is to repair what’s broken in Democratic organizing by rebuilding trust and restoring faith in our electoral process. We want to hear from voters about their top concerns, and we want to make sure that candidates running for election address those concerns directly!

This is a 2-hour ZOOM event that includes role playing and examples of how to canvass.  A zoom link will be sent ONE WEEK before the training to everyone who signed up.

## CD6 CANDIDATE DEBATE: Amberson vs. Chapin

Join us for a crucial debate between the candidates seeking the DFL endorsement for U.S. Congress! **The CD6 DFL Endorsing Convention is scheduled for Saturday, April 25, 2026.**

This is a vital opportunity to hear directly from both **Anson Amberson** and **Doug Chapin** as they debate the issues that matter most to our district and the nation. The outcome of this debate will help inform delegates and voters ahead of the Convention.

---

### 🗓️ Event Details

* **Date:** Saturday, January 10, 2026
* **Time:** 11:00 AM - 1:00 PM
* **Location:** Great River Regional Library
    * **Address:** 1300 W. St. Germain St., St. Cloud, MN 56301

### 🎙️ Debate Format

This event will feature a traditional debate structure designed to provide in-depth candidate contrast:

* **Opening Statements:** Candidates will present their vision for CD6 and the country.
* **Moderated Questions:** Focused questions on key issues facing the district and state.
* **Rebuttals:** Time allotted for direct responses and contrasts between the candidates.
* **Closing Arguments:** Final appeals to the audience and prospective delegates.

---

### **IMPORTANT: Delegate Information & Caucuses**

If you are interested in becoming a delegate to the **CD6 Endorsing Convention on April 25, 2026**, your journey begins with the precinct caucuses:

* **Attend Your Caucus:** Precinct Caucuses will be held on **Tuesday, February 3, 2026**.
* **Learn the Process:** To understand how to become a delegate and secure your spot at the endorsing convention, please review the official DFL guide:
    [**DFL Caucus & Convention Process**](https://dfl.org/caucuses-conventions/process/)

We look forward to a civil, spirited, and informative discussion!
