events.title: Gathering/Potluck
events.description:
## Join Us for Our Monthly Gathering & Potluck — Help Shape MSUP’s Future

Our next Monthly Gathering & Potluck is coming up, and this one is an important milestone for Mat-Su United for Progress. We're asking everyone who can make it to join us at **6:30 p.m.** for a short business meeting before we roll into a fun, themed potluck.

This month we’ll take two big steps forward:

### 1. Voting to Adopt Our Bylaws

After months of collaborative work, edits, and discussion, our bylaws are ready for final approval. These bylaws lay the foundation for how MSUP will operate — how we make decisions, how our Board functions, and how we stay accountable to each other.  
[Here are the draft Bylaws for you perusal.](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1iLaXp7hGrWY7dIOb3GqZ35eS6PQA19PcHxsv6w_fNUY/edit?usp=sharing)

### 2. Electing Officers Under the New Bylaws

Once the bylaws pass, we’ll hold elections for the officer positions outlined in the document:

- Chair  
- Vice Chair  
- Secretary  
- Treasurer  
- Three (3) At-Large Board Seats  

Whether you’re new to MSUP or have been here since the beginning, **you are welcome to run**.  
Nominations are open now — including self-nominations. If you’d like to nominate yourself  included for review ahead of time.or someone else, please reach out so we can include them in the process.

---

## And Then… It’s Potluck Time!

After the short business meeting, we’ll move right into a themed potluck and a holiday cookie swap — because building community should also be joyful (and delicious).

### Potluck Challenge: Bring a Dish Starting With the First Letter of Your First Name

Have fun with it!

- Dave might bring *dumplings*.  
- Lynn might show up with *lasagna*.  
- Pete could appear with *potato salad*.  

Feel free to be creative, chaotic, or classic — it’s all welcome.

### Holiday Cookie Swap (Optional but Highly Encouraged!)

If you love having an assortment of cookies around the holidays, join in:

- Bring **three dozen** of one kind of cookie.  
- Leave with **three dozen** of all different kinds.

It’s a sweet way to share traditions — and go home with treats.

---

## Why This Night Matters

This past year, we’ve rallied, organized, showed up for local issues, and built a community that supports one another. Now we’re putting structure behind that energy so we can keep growing and be ready for the work ahead.

Approving our bylaws and electing officers strengthens MSUP.  
Sharing food strengthens our community.

I hope you’ll join us — to vote, to nominate, to run, to eat, or simply to be part of what we’re building together.

**See you at 6:30 p.m. — and don’t forget the dish that starts with your name!**

events.title: Fightback Phonebank: Campbell Coal Costs Are Too Damn High!
events.description:
Trump and MAGA Republicans are forcing us to pay more for a dirty, outdated power source - the J.H. Campbell Coal Plant in West Michigan! 

Help us fightback at this phonebank! 
We will be calling like-minded voters to make sure they understand what is at stake, and then we will connect them with their member of Congress to leave a message, so we can hold them accountable, which is the best way to make an impact We have a great training and calling system to make it super easy for anyone to participate, even if you have never done this before! Sign up with your friends for the biggest impact! 


Background:

Consumers Energy’s J.H. Campbell coal plant in West Michigan was supposed to close this year, saving ratepayers money, cutting dangerous air pollution, and accelerating Michigan’s shift to clean energy. But in a last-minute move, the Trump administration stepped in and ordered the plant to stay open through the summer, citing a made-up “energy emergency” and ignoring the utility’s closure plan and the decisions of state regulators.

Closing the coal plant was in the works for years, and its closure was expected to save Michigan ratepayers $600 million by 2040.

The Trump administration’s reckless decision is a disaster for our climate and our wallets. Campbell is one of the most expensive coal plants in the Midwest to run, and according to experts, the cost estimates of keeping it open could exceed $100 million. Meanwhile, Consumers Energy is asking state regulators for a $436 million rate hike, which would raise residential electric bills by more than 13%. Running Campbell longer only adds to the burden Michigan families are already facing.

Keeping the plant open means Consumers must rehire staff, purchase more coal, restart aging equipment, and pass those extra costs onto ratepayers. This isn’t about grid reliability, it’s about political interference overriding expert planning and forcing us to foot the bill.

Michigan deserves better. 


Take action! Join us for this phonebank to show Congress we won't stand for this!

Take this opportunity with Garden State Equality, to stand in support of a more accessible, affordable, safe, and welcoming New Jersey for all. Our collective advocacy effort will urge the Legislature to pass critical social justice legislation during this year’s lame duck session.

The People’s Agenda highlights legislative priorities that would meaningfully advance justice, equity, and opportunity across our state. Together, we’re calling on lawmakers to take action on the following:

🦆 S3672/A4987 – Immigrant Trust Act

🦆 S3009/A4083 – New Jersey Voter Empowerment Act

🦆 S3545/A4696 – Climate Superfund Act

🦆 S3491/A4656 – Protections for gender-affirming care and abortion providers and patients*

🦆 S3452/A4601 – Eliminates cost-sharing for insurance coverage of reproductive health care*

🦆 S2338/A4463 – Brings incarcerated elders home

🦆 S2348/A4175 – Codifies and strengthens protections against police use of force

[*indicates components of the Reproductive Freedom and Health Equity Bill Package!]

We’re also urging lawmakers to close corporate loopholes and ensure super-millionaires pay their fair share, helping to fund the essential programs and services our communities rely on.

events.title: Fighting for Environmental Justice in 2025 and Beyond
events.description:
Under the Biden Administration, the Justice40 initiative helped direct resources to communities that had long been ignored or underserved by federal programs. From installing clean air monitors to cleaning up toxic waste and replacing lead service lines, progress was being made to realize environmental justice. 

In just a year since President Trump took office, these efforts have been all but abandoned. This makes it even more difficult for communities to access the funding and data they need in the face of corporate polluters.

Join EDF Action and Asia Guest of the Frontline Resource Institute as we welcome Andrea Vidaurre from the People's Collective for Environmental Justice for a conversation on their efforts to fight for their communities in the face of a hostile administration. We'll also talk solutions and actions you can take to keep environmental justice moving forward.

events.title: Protecting Our Right To Vote: What We All Need to Know

location.venue: Missoula Public Library, Cooper Room B (South)

events.description:
Our votes hold power, otherwise they wouldn’t subvert them. We must raise our voices in the 2026 midterms and elect leaders who represent all of us, not just the billionaires. In preparation, we will be screening a powerful film and two PBS shorts. After the screening we will have a discussion and Q&A with a representative of the Missoula County Elections Office on Montana's elections procedures and regulations as well as challenges on the horizon. We will also hear an update on the Transparent Election Initiative that aims to end corporate dark money spending in Montana elections.

Brave New Films’ ‘SUPPRESSED AND SABOTAGED 2024: The Fight to Vote’ is a tool in the arsenal of every concerned American, sounding the alarm on voter suppression and election subversion ahead of November 2026. This 30-minute documentary film focuses on the swelling wave of efforts to disenfranchise voters across the U.S., with the 2018 Georgia gubernatorial race between Stacey Abrams and Brian Kemp providing a case study for understanding today’s restrictive measures. In 2023 alone, 150 bills were introduced to restrict voting access. SUPPRESSED AND SABOTAGED 2024 is a rallying call against the calculated, unconstitutional, and racist attacks intended to destroy democracy in the United States. 

PBS's "Civics Made Easy", hosted by Ben Sheehan, breaks down the complex world of American government and civic participation. Designed to empower and inform, the series makes understanding civics both accessible and engaging for all. We will be watching "How Elections Work" and "Who Has the Right to Vote in America". Each episode is roughly 11 minutes.

events.title: 2026 Sheriff Candidate Selection Committee
events.description:
🗳️ Aspen Seniors for Peace

2026 Sheriff Candidate Selection Committee

Pitkin County Edition — Launching in 60 Days

Seniors for Peace • Chase Housing Initiative • Aspen Organizing Project

📍 Aspen, Colorado — Community Location TBD
🗓️ First Organizing Meeting: [Insert date 60 days from now]
🕊️ Hosted by Aspen Seniors for Peace
💪 Supported by the Chase Housing Initiative Advocacy Program


---

Description

Aspen has a long tradition of challenging power — and occasionally turning politics completely on its head.
We all remember the moment when Hunter S. Thompson ran for Pitkin County Sheriff and nearly won, proving once and for all that a sheriff’s race in this valley can get a little weird, a little visionary, and a whole lot more democratic than anyone expects.

In that spirit, we’re launching the Pitkin County 2026 Sheriff Candidate Selection Committee — a serious, structured, community-driven process with a local flair that honors Aspen’s past while building its future.

We’re bringing together seniors, workers, artists, activists, faith leaders, and long-time residents to identify and support a sheriff who reflects the values this valley actually lives by:

transparency, fairness, compassion, and real mountain-town accountability.

This is Aspen stepping back into its legacy — not just to vote, but to shape the leadership that shapes our lives.


---

Our Goals

🔍 Identify candidates committed to humane policing, mental-health-first response, and transparent public safety
🗣️ Host public forums & listening circles in Aspen, Snowmass, Basalt, and the upper valley
🧭 Develop a shared community platform rooted in nonviolence, civil liberties, and senior safety
✍️ Coordinate with Pitkin County Democrats to secure a strong, values-forward endorsement
⚖️ Build a grassroots base prepared to organize, canvass, advocate, and win

> “Aspen doesn’t wait for change.
We build it — together.”




---

Why Aspen? Why Now?

The sheriff sets the tone for the entire county — from traffic stops to mental health calls to wildfire evacuations.
If we want a sheriff who actually reflects this community, we need to organize long before ballots drop.

Aspen has influence, imagination, and a rebellious streak.
This is the moment to use all three.


---

Join the Committee

Bring your ideas, your experiences, your concerns, and your voice.
This is how Aspen shapes the 2026 sheriff’s race — with intention, democracy, and a little bit of the spirit that once shook the valley awake.

🔗 RSVP & Join Aspen Seniors for Peace — 2026 Sheriff Selection Process

Join us in planning actions to make this happen.

Solidarity Warriors is an action-focused, Indivisible group formed after the November election. We were the lead organizers of No Kings 2 in Denver. events.title: One Million Families Rising: Brainstorm & Holiday Toy Drive
events.description:
We created the ICNW Parents group so we could empower families to take part in political activism in ways that are inclusive, welcoming, and accessible. In building a strong, connected community, we help families of all backgrounds find their voices and use them to make a difference.

**Indivisible Chicago Northwest is partnering with the Filament Theatre to host an in-person brainstorm session with parents and kids to hear what matters to you in 2026.** 

We'll discuss which issues resonate most with families of Northwest Chicago and think up ways we can further leverage this community. **This will support the sustained organizing we need to make a difference. This is a child-friendly event.** We will provide child care during the session and instructors from the Filament will lead kids aged 7-15 in their own brainstorming so we hear their voices, too! 

Our mutual aid partner for the event is [Share Our Spare](https://shareourspare.org/). Share Our Spare (SOS) ensures every Chicago area child, ages 0-5, has the essential items they need to support their health and development and equip them for a strong start. We will be accepting new and like-new toys for SOS to distribute to those in need during this holiday season. Before donating any like-new toys, please see the quality standards below: 

1. Like-new toys must:
  ● Have all the pieces.
  ● Be clean and in like new condition - no rips, stains, tears, smells, etc.
  ● Safe and appropriate for children ages Newborn to 5.
  ● No small trinket toys, single items that belong in a set, or anything with personalization.
2. Any toy that has multiple pieces should be self contained in a bag or plastic wrap and bundled with rubber bands/tape to ensure that pieces stay together.
3. Large toys like balance bikes, small indoor climbers, cozy coupe cars, push cars, wagons, etc. are acceptable if clean & in like new condition.
4. Make sure electronic toys work before donating.
5. *If you would not be excited to give the toys to a child in your life, please refrain from donating.*

***Doors open at 10 am and the event will begin at 10:15 am. Please note, parking on Milwaukee is limited, so please plan accordingly. See you there!***

Get ready to make history! We are thrilled to invite you to the official launch of the "Make America Affordable Now" PAC, a critical pillar of the One Fair Wage Living Wage for All campaign!

For too long, the economic deck has been stacked against working people, forcing millions to struggle on subminimum wages. 

While we've fought hard and won in many places, it's time to take our movement to the next level so that every single worker earns a living wage.

This PAC will power the organizing, advocacy, and electoral work needed to achieve our vision: raising the minimum wage to a true living wage in target localities and building the momentum necessary to finally raise the federal minimum wage!


Why This Launch Matters:
• No One Left Behind: Our core strategy ensures that, unlike in the past, tipped workers will be included in these vital wage increases. Living Wage for All means everyone gets a fair, sustainable income.

• Affordability is Possible: We're launching "Make America Affordable Now" because we believe a thriving economy is one where people can actually afford to live, work, and raise a family. This PAC is the vehicle to make that a reality.

• Build the Movement: Connect with workers, dedicated allies, and leaders from High Road restaurants who are already demonstrating that high wages are good for business and great for people.

This event is more just than a launch; it's the beginning of a worker-led movement! Your presence sends a powerful message that the movement for economic justice is strong, united, and ready to win a living wage for all.

events.title: Duluth Indivisible December Meeting: Organizing for the Long Haul
events.description:
“Any decent society has to be built on trust and love and the intelligent use of information and feelings. Education involves being able to practice those things as you struggle to build a decent society that can be nonviolent.”
— Myles Horton

We’ve shown repeatedly that Duluth Indivisible can really mobilize for rallies and protests. We'll probably always have to do that while the forces of fascism are on the move and intensifying. But what do we need to do to move beyond protests? Beyond reaction to action? From single issue to any issue? To lay the foundation for a powerful, non-violent, sustainable, long-term, resilient and nurturing community? To be nimbler? To enlarge our sphere of influence? To push back more forcefully and act more boldly? To unite the forces of good? 

Come be with us on December 4th at the Radisson (6:00 - 7:30) as we build on the concepts of power analysis we touched on in November and take the next step in building our organizing muscles. 

What structures do we need for mass resistance and what can we win in 2026?

events.title: Phonebank Moderation 101
events.description:
🌟Lead a Democratic Phone Bank🌟A Free Class for Chat Moderators

Are you passionate about saving democracy, and would like to amp-up your volunteer work and actually help run the phone banks working to save our democracy? We’re here to help with our FREE class designed specifically for those looking to support democracy in 2025 and beyond through leadership 🎉. 

📞 Why This Class?

Expert Guidance: Benefit from the wisdom of an instructor, Dr. Christopher Kavanau, with decades of experience in phone bank campaigning and volunteer mobilization. His insights will not only prepare you for the task at hand at helping save democracy, but will inspire you too!

Fun-Filled Learning: Discover how phone banking can be more than just making calls; it's about connecting, engaging, and making friends while you contribute to the cause of saving democracy that you believe in.

Make a Real Impact: This is your chance to play a crucial role in saving our democracy. With each call you're making a difference!

🎉 Who Should Join?

This class is perfect for anyone eager to support democratic efforts, regardless of your experience level.

What you need is a comfy place in your home and access to Zoom.

events.description:
## 🛫Avelo Airlines: Cancel your contract with ICE. 

### These flights are illegal, inhumane, & unconstitutional.

* Avelo Airlines is the first commercial airline to sign a deportation charter contract with ICE. Every day this $150 million contract stands, Avelo cashes in on tearing families apart — and every day it runs, deportation profiteering becomes more normalized. If they get away with it, other airlines will follow. Our leverage? Working with groups across the country to hit them on every front — at their airports, in the states and cities bankrolling them, and on the campuses that partner with them — until doing ICE’s dirty work costs too much to continue.

* These flights are secretive and unmarked, with no guarantee of legal counsel or due process for the people being removed. Every day the contract continues, Avelo is profiting from tearing families apart — and gambling its business on mass deportations.

* To keep the pressure on Avelo, Mesa Valley Indivisible continues to protest against Avelo Airlines operating ICE deportations on Sunday, November 30th!

### Important

* Call attention to Avelo Airlines separating families
* Complicity of Mesa/Gateway airport
* Illegal deportations without due process
* Human trafficking

###  Protest Information

🅿️ Parking is available around the intersection

⭐ Please share with friends, family, neighbors, EVERYONE!

events.title: >>>>>WE AIN’T BUYING IT>>>>> Nov 27, 2025 - Dec 01, 2025
events.description:
This Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, we’re coming together to send a clear message to corporate America and this administration: WE AIN'T BUYING IT!!!

For eleven months, our communities have faced relentless attacks — mass firings of federal workers, corporate pressure to dismantle DEI, and ICE raids targeting our neighbors. As the government shutdown left 42 million people without needed food, corporations like Target, Home Depot, and Amazon continued to profit from policies that harmed working families, immigrants, and communities of color.

ENOUGH IS ENOUGH!!!

This action is taking direct aim at Target, for caving to this administration's biased attacks on DEI; Home Depot, for allowing and colluding with ICE to kidnap our neighbours on their properties; and Amazon, for funding this administration to secure their own corporate tax cuts. We’ll send a clear message: until they cease collaborating with this administration’s harmful policies, our dollars will go elsewhere.

We Ain’t Buying It is a coordinated weekend of economic noncooperation (Nov 27–Dec 1), led by a coalition of organizations, including Indivisible, workers, and everyday people who believe our values are not for sale.

Together, we will:
Highlight the corporations colluding with authoritarian power;
Withhold spending from major corporate retailers;
Redirect our resources to mutual aid, small businesses, and Black- and immigrant-owned enterprises; and
Show the economic and social power of collective restraint.

Millions of families are feeling the impact of reduced SNAP benefits, while the same corporations driving up food prices are launching billion-dollar Black Friday sales.
We Ain’t Buying It is our collective refusal to keep feeding a system that profits off hunger.
This week, we’re asking partners and communities to pause spending with major retailers and redirect support to those most affected by food insecurity.

Instead of adding to a cart, we can:
Donate skipped spending to local food banks or mutual aid funds for delivery drivers and families who lost SNAP support.
Buy local or minority-owned, keeping money circulating where it’s needed most.

Suggested Day to Day Specific Actions:
Thursday - Don’t Spend a Dime, Spend Family Time 
Friday - Blackout Friday: Blackout Black Friday 
Saturday - Shop Small Saturday: Shop local, shop Black, shop Immigrant, shop POC 
Sunday - Circulate the Dollar: Mutual Aid, support one another
Monday - Cyber Shutdown: digital blackout

Every skipped sale is a statement: access to food should not depend on profit margins.

Let’s build a week of action rooted in care, not consumption.
Join us!!!

#WeAintBuyingIt #FeedEachOther #SNAPBack #EconomicRepair #CommunityOverCorporations

events.title: WFPeaches Service Saturday: Foods and Funds
events.description:
As reactionaries threaten the needs of our neighbors, we must unite as a community to support each other. In Georgia, more than 1.3 million residents rely on SNAP benefits to make ends meet. This includes 74,705 Fulton County households, 54,598 DeKalb households, and  29,857 Clayton County households. Federal cuts to SNAP have increased the strain on our community food banks and the food insecure Georgians they serve. In the wealthiest nation in the world, no person should go hungry.

**Here's how we're helping:** We're dedicating a Service Saturday to gather pantry items and donations to support the [Atlanta Community Food Bank](https://www.acfb.org/about-us/) (ACFB). ACFB works with nearly 700 community-based nonprofit partners across metro Atlanta and north Georgia, distributing more than 9 million meals per month. They have a time-tested system of collection and distribution logistics, multiple online payment options, and an employer matching gift search tool. ***On this Service Saturday, we will host a food drive for shelf-stable donations, as well as a fundraising phone bank to contact our community supporters. Together, we can help our neighbors in need\!***

### FAQs

***What will ACFB do with monetary donations?***  
ACFB uses monetary donations for many purposes, including:

* Purchasing in bulk at wholesale prices  
* Purchasing goods needed for a more balanced selection  
* Better meeting specific dietary needs and preferences  
* Covering operating costs, such as transportation and storage

***What if I only want to donate pantry items?***  
Great! We’d love to have them. Stop by anytime during our event to make your shelf-stable donation. There is no obligation to participate in the fundraising phone bank.

***I’ve never phone banked before. Will there be training?***  
Of course! We’ll show you how to make calls and help you feel comfortable and confident. We have a script you can use to help guide your conversations and designated volunteers to answer your questions.

***What should I bring for phone banking?***  
If you’d like to participate in our fundraising phone bank, please bring a fully charged cellular phone and laptop or tablet. You can alternatively use just your cell phone if needed, but a laptop or tablet will help you work more efficiently and comfortably.

events.title: No Partisan Maps - House Redistricting Committee
events.description:
Florida voters have already spoken loud and clear: we do not want mid-decade redistricting, and we refuse to accept partisan gerrymandering that rigs our districts for political gain. Now, the Legislature is moving toward drawing new voting maps before the next election—a move that violates Florida’s Constitution and threatens our democracy. Because drawing maps to benefit any party is illegal in Florida. 

Join advocates from across the state in Tallahassee to make sure lawmakers hear us: No mid-decade power grabs. No partisan maps. Honor the Fair Districts Amendments.

What We’ll Do

We’ll gather at the Florida Capitol, connect with organizers and community members, and attempt to speak directly with legislators, urging them to protect voters—not politicians. We will also make our voices heard during the committee hearing, where decisions about redistricting may be on the table.

Why It Matters

Floridians passed the Fair Districts Amendments to stop politicians from manipulating district lines for partisan advantage.

Drawing new maps now—mid-decade—is a direct response to national calls for gerrymandering and is illegal under Florida’s Constitution.

Partisan mid-decade map-drawing would disproportionately silence Black, Brown, and working-class communities across the state.

Redistricting determines who represents us. This process must serve the people, not political interests.

Our Message

No rigged maps. No partisan games.

Protect fair representation for all Floridians.

Say NO to any mid-decade redistricting scheme.

Florida’s democracy works best when every voice is heard—and yours is essential. Join us in Tallahassee to stand up for fair maps and a fair future.

The hearing will be in the Capitol building at Reed Hall (102 HOB)

More details will be shared as we get closer to the event.

events.title: Weekly (Fri) Mass Pike Overpass Standout in Westfield - Southampton Rd (Routes 10/202)
events.description:
Please wear highly visible clothing if possible. 

Wow! What a great location for a standout! There's lots and lots of traffic passing by. Southampton Road (Routes 10/202) is heavily traveled northbound and southbound, and the Mass Pike eastbound and westbound is below. Lots of honks and thumbs up and waves...and a few folks flying middle fingers. We smile and wave at them all!

We've discovered that the magic happens when we smile and wave to people!

Come when you can, and leave when you must. You needn't be present for the entire event.

## How to Get There

The address "130 Southampton Road, Westfield" will get you just north of the overpass.

## Parking
We can't park in the Southampton Rd breakdown lane. There are vacant business properties north of the bridge, and we've been warned NOT to park there.

Please park on the north side (the westbound shoulder) of Sgt. Thomas Dion Way, off of Southampton Rd. just north of the Mass Pike.

## Etiquette!
We don't give the finger to people who give the finger to us, or who say unpleasant things. We smile and wave to them, too.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

## Other Stuff
Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel.

## A Few Requests
We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

And, if you have an extra 3' x 5' American flag you're not using, we'd love it if you'd pass it on to us!

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Trump and MAGA Republicans are forcing us to pay more for a dirty, outdated power source - the J.H. Campbell Coal Plant in West Michigan! 

Help us fightback at this letter writing party! 
Join us for a fun evening with like-minded people. We will have a brief presentation about the issues we are facing, and then will take time to write our elected officials to hold them accountable! We will have time to socialize and learn about other upcoming opportunities. Sign up with your friends for the biggest impact! 

Sign up, and we will share the location over email. 


Background:

Consumers Energy’s J.H. Campbell coal plant in West Michigan was supposed to close this year, saving ratepayers money, cutting dangerous air pollution, and accelerating Michigan’s shift to clean energy. But in a last-minute move, the Trump administration stepped in and ordered the plant to stay open through the summer, citing a made-up “energy emergency” and ignoring the utility’s closure plan and the decisions of state regulators.

Closing the coal plant was in the works for years, and its closure was expected to save Michigan ratepayers $600 million by 2040.

The Trump administration’s reckless decision is a disaster for our climate and our wallets. Campbell is one of the most expensive coal plants in the Midwest to run, and according to experts, the cost estimates of keeping it open could exceed $100 million. Meanwhile, Consumers Energy is asking state regulators for a $436 million rate hike, which would raise residential electric bills by more than 13%. Running Campbell longer only adds to the burden Michigan families are already facing.

Keeping the plant open means Consumers must rehire staff, purchase more coal, restart aging equipment, and pass those extra costs onto ratepayers. This isn’t about grid reliability, it’s about political interference overriding expert planning and forcing us to foot the bill.

Michigan deserves better. 

Your voice matters! 
Join our letter writing party to have yours heard by the right people at an important time.

events.title: Perilous Fuel Tanks: Oregon's Ticking Time Bomb
events.description:
The Critical Energy Infrastructure (CEI) Hub holds 90% of Oregon’s liquid fuel supply and is located along the banks of the Willamette River in Northwest Portland, across the street from Forest Park and close to where the Willamette meets the Columbia River. Many of these fuel tanks were built over 70 years ago, before seismic standards were in place, and are located on liquefiable infill soil. This location is considered a quadruple hazard zone because it is vulnerable to earthquakes, wildfires, landslides, floods, and has great potential for a massive oil spill. With the growing risk of urban forest fires and the growing likelihood of a Cascadia Subduction Zone earthquake, these tanks are in a perilous position, and without significant changes, one event could lead to a complete collapse of our state’s fuel system and cause a multi-billion-dollar public health and environmental disaster. A disaster at the CEI Hub will have far-reaching impacts and will affect the entire state.
 
This event is a panel discussion about the long-reaching environmental effects of a collapse of the CEI Hub; the statewide consequences for our fuel supply; and past, current, and future state actions. The panelists will answer questions that attendees submit beforehand when they register for the event. And we'll leave you with some actions you can take to help reduce the risks the CEI Hub poses to all of us. 

Meet our panel of experts:

Moderator – Michael Dembrow, retired Oregon State Senator

Thuy Tran, State Representative for NE Portland District 45

Luke Hanst, Partnerships Manager for the Civil & Environmental Engineering Department at Portland State University. 

Kate Murphy, Senior Community Organizer at Columbia Riverkeeper.

events.title: Shake the Field Book Club: February 2026
events.description:
The Shake the Field Book Club is a space where 18–45 year olds can dig deep into social movement strategy and history. Whether you’ve been organizing for decades or just attended your first protest, come learn from the words of movement experts and from the life experiences of your peers.

This month we're reading *Liberation Stories: Building Narrative Power for 21st-Century Social Movements.* This book allows us to learn from activist communicators on to tell stories that change the world and gives us insight into the comms strategy from several modern social movements. 

A limited number of book scholarships are available each month to support 18–45 year olds with financial need who otherwise might not be able to participate in the bookclub. Scholarships will be distributed on a first come, first served basis. Book scholarship applications are due one month prior to the book club meeting. Applying for a book scholarship comes with a commitment to attending the book club gathering for that month. 

Learn more about us at shakethefield.org, and follow us on instagram @shakethefieldal.

events.title: The Blueprint for Affordable Energy Launch Event
events.description:
No matter where we come from, what we look like, or how much money we make, we all deserve clean air and clean water, to stay cool in the summer and warm in the winter, to be able to pay our utility bills without sacrificing other necessities, and to protect the places we love and call home for future generations.

Unfortunately, Wall Street utility companies are raising our rates to pay for energy and infrastructure that makes our air dirtier, our kids sicker, and our weather more extreme–ignoring more affordable, cleaner and more reliable solutions to our energy needs.

This Blueprint for Affordable Energy, from People's Action Institute, is a call to action for governors, state legislators, federal officials, community organizers and frustrated ratepayers ready to unite to lay down the path for clean, affordable and reliable energy for all.

events.title: Voting Rights Lobby Day and Rally in Frankfort - 2026

location.venue: Kentucky State Capitol and Capitol Annex

events.description:
Together, Kentuckians can build a healthy democracy where everyone’s voice counts – no exceptions.   Right now, about 200,000 Kentuckians with felonies in their past still can’t vote and that’s just not right.

Join us in Frankfort at the capitol on February 19th to restore voting rights to Kentuckians with felonies in their past. We'll meet at 8:30am in the Capitol Annex to train and break into small teams and have conversations with legislators throughout the day, then we'll gather at 2:00pm in the capitol annex for a rally led by people directly impacted by this issue, telling their stories.

Join us for just the rally, or hopefully for the whole day.

Bring a photo ID to get into the building and try to arrive early.  We encourage people to consider wearing masks.  We’ll have extra masks available. 

If you have one, please consider wearing a shirt lifting up whatever organization you want to be supporting that day.  Wear comfortable shoes too, but otherwise travel light (they're likely to take umbrellas at security, etc.).

Don't worry if you've never done anything like this before. We'll start with a training and lobby teams will be made up of a mix of people who are brand new to this and others who have been doing it for years!

Schedule for the day

Arrive early with ID to get through security (might take 30 minutes to get through)

8:30-9:30 Lobby training in Capitol Annex (room TBA).  We’ll break into lobby teams and train.

9:30-11:30 Overflow lobby training in Capitol Annex (room TBA).

9:30-2:00 lobbying, lunch, etc.   

2:00 Rally in the capitol annex

Group picture


Parking and directions.  We'll start the day at the Capitol Annex, 702 Capital Ave, Frankfort, KY 40601

The Capitol parking structure is at 861 Old Lawrenceburg Rd, Frankfort, KY 40601 and that might be the best place to park.  You can also access the parking lot from the top next to the annex.  Levels 5 and 6 or the surface are open to anyone. There's also street parking in the vicinity.

Meal tickets for lunch will be available for those who need it. Reach out to Heather Mahoney at heather@kftc.org or find her in the annex cafeteria between 10:30 and 1 on February 19 to receive your ticket (she’ll be wearing a name tag).

Event is sponsored by Kentucky Voting Rights Coalition.

events.title: Schools of Nope 101: What They Are and How to Organize Locally
events.description:
Schools of Nope 101: What They Are and How to Organize Locally
Join Families for Strong Public Schools for a powerful virtual training on Florida’s rapidly expanding Schools of Hope co-location and takeover scheme—and what communities can do to fight back.
Across the state, districts are receiving waves of “letters of intent” from private charter operators seeking to move into public school buildings under the Schools of Hope law. This session will break down what’s happening, why it matters, and how local advocates can organize quickly and effectively to defend their neighborhood schools.
Whether you’re a parent, educator, community leader, or simply concerned about protecting public education, this training will give you the tools, messaging, and next steps you need to take action in your county.
What we’ll cover:
What Schools of Hope really are and how the new rule expands them
How co-location and takeovers impact students, funding, and local control
What letters of intent mean and what to watch for in your district
Organizing strategies to activate your community fast
How to use the Schools of Nope toolkit to educate, organize, and mobilize
Ways to plug into statewide efforts and connect with local advocates
Come ready to learn, ask questions, and build power together.
Your community needs you—let’s get organized.

events.title: We Draw the Lines: No Partisan Maps: FL House Redistricting Committee Hearing # 1
events.description:
Florida lawmakers are attempting a mid-decade redistricting process designed to tip the scales of power for partisan gain and weaken the voices of everyday Floridians. On December 4, the Florida House Select Committee on Congressional Redistricting will hold its first meeting, and we are mobilizing to be present in the room and speak on the record. This hearing is a critical moment for lawmakers to hear directly from the communities who will be impacted.

Join us at the State Capitol as we gather to ensure our voices are heard and to demand transparency, accountability, and fair representation. We will attend the committee hearing together and, if public comment is allowed, deliver our message: Hands Off Our Maps.

For those who cannot be physically present, we will also host a coordinated digital action so supporters across the state can contact lawmakers by email, phone, and social media to speak out and amplify the call for fair maps.

Florida must stand up and fight back. Sign up to join us and make your voice heard.

events.title: #GivingTuesday Phone Bank for California Ranked Choice Voting
events.description:
Giving Tuesday is coming up, and we’ve got a huge opportunity to move the needle for ranked choice voting — with your help.

Our national partner Rank the Vote is hosting a Giving Tuesday Phone Bank on Tuesday, 12/2, and we’re inviting Cal RCV volunteers to join supporters from all over the country. As a Cal RCV volunteer, you'll be making warm calls to Californians who've already said they support ranked choice voting.

Pick one or more shifts any time between 3–8pm PT and help reconnect with people who already believe in RCV — and simply need someone like you to give them a nudge to chip in.


Why this matters:
Cal RCV is powered by individual donations. Our coalition is making progress on RCV in Los Angeles, Santa Clara County, Sacramento, San Diego, and planting more statewide seeds. We need to keep and build on that momentum, and that takes money. Whether or not you yourself donate, you can have a meaningful impact and help fund outreach, education, and the rest of the work needed to bring RCV to cities, counties, and the entire state of California.

Even if you’ve never phone banked before, you’ll fit right in. Rank the Vote's team will train you, walk you through the script, and the calls don’t come from your own number. It’s simple, energizing, and honestly a lot of fun to talk with people who already support RCV.

This is one of the most impactful ways you can help expand RCV — just a bit of your time powers a lot of progress.

events.title: Beacon Shine the Light Thursdays
events.description:
This a local Indivisible event.

Join The Beacon for Thursday Shine the Light, as we bring our voices to the street every Thursday from 12:30-1:00 PM.

Each week, we make our voices heard wherever we are. As beacons, we shine light by making a sign and bringing it outside—in front of our houses, apartment buildings, to our street corners, subway stops, etc.

Our signs proudly share whatever we’re feeling in our souls in the face of this regime’s actions. Our signs might read, “I Stand With Our Immigrant Neighbors,” or “Honk if You Love Ukraine,” or “Trans Rights Are Human Rights,” or “Read Banned Books.”  We encourage a POSITIVE message on all signs, and request that you do not use profanity.

Together, we are building visible resistance and organized compassion, meeting our neighbors, and joining together in acts of solidarity.

There are Beacon groups all over the USA.  Our local Great Neck group meets every Thursday from 12:30-1:00 pm throughout the cold weather months. 

For more information on the Beacon, visit beaconfordemocracy.org

Link to event information: https://www.tinyurl.com/thursdaylight

events.title: Rally Against Slumlords: Lynd & Trigild are a public health crisis.
events.description:
Everyone deserves safe, livable, decent housing conditions, but Lynd Living are subjecting tenants to unsafe conditions & unjust fees. 

Join us at Granville Parklet at 11AM on Thursday, December 11th to march on the nearby Lynd property management office to demand the urgent repairs needed from slumlords Lynd & Trigild as we head into yet another winter where tenants cannot count on slumlords to provide livable conditions.

Cosponsored by Hill District Consensus Group

As the property manager for most of the former AHRCO properties sold to NB Affordable now going through foreclosure cases, Lynd has claimed to tenants they are not at fault for the lack of repairs and don't have the money for repairs, all while working to millions to buy as much of the NB Affordable properties as they can. They profit more the less repairs they make, and they think they can get away with it.

Especially as we head into yet another winter where tenants of NB Affordable properties cannot count on timely repairs and are at risk of utility shutoffs, red tags, leaks, and more, it's time to step up the pressure on Lynd and Trigild.

Rally with us to demand Lynd Living & Trigild: Meet with with tenants organizing for safe & livable homes, Make needed repairs from licensed professionals, Distribute the utility subsidy checks many tenants are entitled to that Lynd & TriGild have not delivered, Erase all debt claims against tenants, rather than charging tenants for the landlord’s systematic failure to facilitate affordable housing subsidy recertifications & lease renewals, and stop retaliating against tenants for organizing.

events.description:
St. Mary's by the Sea Episcopal Church is partnering with Indivisible Monterey's WhistleSTOP Campaign to host Whistlemania in Pacific Grove on Tuesday, December 2, from 5pm to 6:30pm. 

The event, which is free and open to all, gathers volunteers to assemble whistle kits for local community members to alert their neighbors when ICE is nearby. Join us! All ages welcome.

The WhistleSTOP Campaign is inspired by the collective action of thousands of community members in Chicago, Los Angeles, Charlotte and elsewhere who have been using whistles to alert their friends and neighbors when ICE is near or abducting someone.

By literally blowing the whistle on ICE we encourage others to gather and protect community members. Be loud and gather a crowd!

The WhistleSTOP Campaign has a goal of providing 100,000 whistles to local residents to help them alert others when ICE is near. Join us Tuesday, December 2nd — together, we can protect our local community.

You can also contribute to these efforts by making a financial gift that will help us buy more whistles. Donate online here: https://onrealm.org/StMarysbytheSea/-/form/give/now

Be part of the grassroots movement that's changing how we connect with voters in St. Johns County! This comprehensive training will equip you with everything you need to become an effective Street Captain and build lasting relationships with your neighbors.

## What You'll Learn:

- **Get to Know Your Neighbor Program Overview** - Learn the proven Peterson Method: Mail, Text, Meet
- **Canvassing Best Practices** - Watch demonstration videos and participate in hands-on training exercises
- **Vote-by-Mail Expertise** - Master VBM myths & facts, learn to use QR codes for ballot requests, and help neighbors register
- **MiniVan Mobile App** - Get hands-on training with our voter contact database system
- **Community Building** - Discover creative ways to organize neighborhood meet-ups, coffee conversations, and social gatherings
- **Issues Surveys** - Learn how to gather valuable voter feedback on the issues that matter most

##No Experience Necessary!
Whether you're new to canvassing or a seasoned volunteer, this training will give you the confidence and skills to make meaningful connections with your neighbors.

Come ready to learn, share ideas, and become part of a dedicated team making a real difference in our community. Together, we're building a stronger, more connected Democratic movement right here in St. Johns County.

Available both in-person at DEC Headquarters and via Zoom

events.title: ICE OFF OUR STREETS - Roseburg, OR
events.description:
# ICE OFF OUR STREETS. 
## STOP TERRORIZING OUR NEIGHBORS.

**ICE has spent the entire year terrorizing our immigrant neighbors — and we’re done staying quiet about it.**

**On Saturday, December 13th, from 12:00 p.m. to 1:30 p.m.**, we’re rallying at the Stewart Parkway overpass above I-5 to send a message that cannot be ignored - **Abolish ICE!**



This is a peaceful, nonviolent, high-visibility rally demanding an end to ICE’s cruelty, fear tactics, and harassment of immigrant families.

We will gather on the sidewalk along the Stewart Parkway overpass above I-5 and hold signs and banners that drivers can clearly see from the highway. Our goal is visibility, solidarity, and truth-telling.

**Bring BIG, BOLD signs — short, loud, and unmistakable.**

## Suggested Sign Ideas:

- ABOLISH I.C.E.

- UNMASK I.C.E.

- I.C.E. IS THE NEW GESTAPO

- HONK IF YOUR MORAL COMPASS ISN’T BANKRUPT

- THEY BLAME IMMIGRANTS SO YOU WON’T BLAME BILLIONAIRES

- END THE I.C.E. AGE

- I.C.E. = STATE-SPONSORED TERRORISM

- DEPORT ICE

- I.C.E. OFF OUR STREETS

- STOP TERRORIZING OUR NEIGHBORS

- IMMIGRANTS ARE WELCOMED HERE

- IMMIGRANTS MAKE AMERICA GREAT

- IMMIGRANTS BUILT THIS COUNTRY

- NO ONE IS ILLEGAL ON STOLEN LAND

- HUMANS ARE NOT ILLEGAL

Keep your lettering huge and high-contrast. People must be able to read your sign at 60+ mph from I-5. **Big, bold, simple = effective.**

**What to Expect**

- Peaceful, nonviolent overpass rally

- Big, high-visibility signage

**Our giant banners will be present, including:**

- Deport ICE

- ICE = State Terror

- Justice For All

**Things to Remember:**

- Do not block traffic

- If counter-protesters or provocateurs show up, do not engage

- Remember to keep it peaceful. Everyone is responsible for de-escalation.


**Why We’re Doing This**

I.C.E.’s cruelty is not abstract — it’s real, local, and devastating. Families live in fear. Workers disappear. Communities are harassed. Children grow up terrified their parents won’t come home.

- We refuse to normalize this.

- We refuse to be silent.

- We refuse to let ICE terrorize our immigrant neighbors in our name.


**Stand with us. Stand with our immigrant neighbors.**

Join us on the overpass and help deliver a message loud enough for the whole city — and the whole freeway — to hear.

events.title: 🚨COMMUNITY MOBILIZATION: DEFEND OUR IMMIGRANT COMMUNITIES

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
On Tuesday, December 9th at 6:00 PM, we will gather at the Newton City Council Meeting to stand with our communities of color, our immigrant families, and every resident who deserves safety, dignity, and freedom from fear.

A formal resolution has been submitted to the City of Newton calling for the Blocking of the Use of City Property for Civil Immigration Enforcement Activities.
We need a powerful public turnout to ensure our leaders hear us loud and clear: Newton must protect its own.

Why We’re Showing Up

Across Western NC, ICE has escalated enforcement actions — including in Charlotte, Gaston County, and now targeting residents in Hickory. These raids overwhelmingly detain people with no criminal record and have left families shattered, businesses closed, and entire neighborhoods living in fear.

This crisis has intensified locally:
Brookford Police recently entered a 287(g) Task Force agreement with ICE, allowing local officers to act as federal immigration agents. This opens the door to profiling, unconstitutional searches, and the erosion of basic civil rights.

Newton does not need to follow that path.
Newton can choose to be a community where families stay together, businesses remain open, and everyone — regardless of background or status — feels safe in public spaces.

What the Resolution Calls For

The resolution affirms that Newton’s public resources should serve our people — not federal operations that destabilize our city. It emphasizes:

• Protecting immigrant families living in Newton
• Ensuring City property, facilities, equipment, and staff are not used for civil ICE operations
• Upholding Constitutional rights — including due process and protections against unreasonable search and seizure
• Preventing economic harm caused when ICE detains business owners, workers, and essential community members
• Strengthening community trust in local institutions and law enforcement

This resolution reflects Newton’s values: fairness, safety, family unity, and a commitment to a just and free society.

Why Your Presence Matters

Federal enforcement actions harm our neighbors, destabilize small businesses, and make our entire community less safe.
Cities across the country have taken proactive steps to block municipal participation in civil immigration enforcement — but this only happens when people show up.

We need a packed room on December 9th to show the city that Newton stands with immigrants, not with raids or police-state tactics.

📍 WHERE & WHEN

Newton City Council Chambers
Tuesday, Dec. 9
Protest begins at 5:00 PM, meeting begins at 6:00 PM

Bring your voice. Bring your signs. Bring your love for a city where all families deserve to live without fear.

Another world is possible — and Newton can lead the way.

❤️ COMMUNITY SOLIDARITY DRIVE

As part of our protest, we’ll be collecting canned food and essentials for anyone across Catawba County struggling with the cost of living crisis in our nation.

📦 Donations Accepted: Canned goods, nonperishables, baby formula, diapers, and hygiene products.
🤝 All items will be distributed locally to families in need — no questions asked.

Even in crisis, we take care of each other.
This is what real community looks like.

🔥 Our Message

No fear.
No police state.
No hungry neighbors.
Just solidarity, dignity, and justice for all.

events.title: December Event(s) of the Month: Documentary Screenings!!!
events.description:
As we look toward the new year, we’re inviting our community to reflect together on the realities of energy — where it comes from, who bears the costs, and how we can envision a cleaner future. This three-week documentary series offers a focused moment to learn, discuss, and imagine a greener path forward — turning new awareness into action.
Over three consecutive Saturdays in December (the 6th, 13th, and 20th), from 7:00–9:00 PM ET, we’ll host a virtual (or in-person) watch party. Each week features a different documentary that explores energy from a different angle: social justice, infrastructure failure, and demand-driven sustainability. After each screening, we’ll discuss what we watched, share perspectives, and ask: What now?
December 6th: Powerlands (2022), directed by Ivey Camille Manybeads Tso.
In this deeply personal and political journey, Navajo filmmaker Ivey Camille returns to her homeland to examine how chemical companies have exploited Indigenous lands — not just in her Navajo Nation, but also in Colombia, Mexico, the Philippines, and at Standing Rock. She meets Indigenous women leading resistance movements, exploring how resource extraction displaces communities, damages environments, and threatens cultural survival. 
December 13th: Ten Steps to Disaster: Texas Blackouts (2021)
This 44-minute episode investigates the 2021 winter storm in Texas that caused a massive blackout, leaving more than four million homes without power. The documentary breaks down ten critical failures — frozen power plants, an isolated grid, lack of backup plans, and missed warnings from earlier storms in 2011. 
It’s a powerful case study in systemic fragility: how energy infrastructure, policy choices, and regulation (or lack thereof) intersected to create a disaster. It pushes us to question what resilience means in an era of increasing climate extremes.
December 20th: The Real Cost of our Energy Demand (2025)
This shorter documentary examines the tension between rising global energy demand and the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. It explores how meeting that demand requires innovative, large-scale solutions — from energy storage to green infrastructure — and how those paths may shape our future. 
Join us on all three nights, or just come to the one you want! Watch with your hub, by yourself, or with some like-minded friends. Bring a snack or drink, and come ready to engage with energy: the past we want to step away from, and a hopeful future Sunrise strives towards.

South PBC Indivisible in Palm Beach County, FL is launching our first weekly discussion group called "Politics, Not As Usual"! *

Our first meeting starts Tuesday, December 2 at 7pm. 

Join us on Zoom every Tuesday Evening from 7-8pm ET except holidays. 

Zoom Link will be provided to those who rsvp to this post. Look for it in your emails.

At these lively evenings, we welome you to share your thoughts; perhaps learn a few new things; and explore ways to take actions related to promoting our democracy and standing up against authoritarianism and executive actions that are hurting our families and our nation.

The hour-long weekly discussions will not be recorded, so all can feel at ease to speak freely, and rules for civil discourse will be strictly followed. 

People who wish to speak will have up to three minutes to share on a relevant topic. Others will have the opportunity to respond.

Resources and relevant event announcements will be exchanged.

Discussions will be initiated and moderated by South PBC Indivisible member Bruce Harris, Esq. Bruce recently retired as attorney for the Palm Beach County School District and is a former civil litigator. 

Bruce will not be providing legal advice but will start off every discussion with a short statement of his views on a relevant topic and participants are welcome to respond, in turn.

Our desire is for these sessions to be friendly, build a sense of community and solidarity. We encourage all to spread the word and invite your friends to join us!

Make sure to check every week that you can make it and look for us in your inbox!

* Disclaimer: The views and the opinions expressed during the discussions are those of each and every speaker and do not necessarily reflect the views or positions of Indivisible National nor of South PBC Indivisible.

**A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.**

events.title: Shelby KFTC LGBTQ Book Club - Beyond Magenta
events.description:
In the aftermath of thefts from our local library targeting LGBTQ books, our group decided to start a reading group to read some of the very books that were stolen and read them together.  Our next book is Beyond Magenta.  We hope you decide to read it and join us for a discussion.

Beyond Magenta - A groundbreaking work of LGBT literature takes an honest look at the life, love, and struggles of transgender teens.  Author and photographer Susan Kuklin met and interviewed six transgender or gender-neutral young adults and used her considerable skills to represent them thoughtfully and respectfully before, during, and after their personal acknowledgment of gender preference. Portraits, family photographs, and candid images grace the pages, augmenting the emotional and physical journey each youth has taken. Each honest discussion and disclosure, whether joyful or heartbreaking, is completely different from the other because of family dynamics, living situations, gender, and the transition these teens make in recognition of their true selves. 

Link to buy through Half Price Books - https://www.hpb.com/beyond-magenta-transgender-teens-speak-out/P-4437370-USED.html?utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=HPB_SHOPPING_ALL_PRODUCTS&gad_source=4&gad_campaignid=21467474395&gclid=CjwKCAiAuIDJBhBoEiwAxhgyFhg74FORqFfgKmQ3FDDScXSw8e9GHsp-IV8AqskB1IDUFce6aQxxehoCgdIQAvD_BwE

The Fort Dix Resistance Brigade is still on active duty! We are a grass roots coalition in opposition to the plan to place a detainee deportation camp on base. We love our service members, our military families and our constitution. We strongly oppose ICE, it's presence on base, and it's disregard for constitutional due process.

This is a roadside visibility event with no real pedestrian traffic. Please bring signs with large fonts and simple messages which can be easily read from passing vehicles.

This will be our group's sixth event at the base, so we are confident in relaying that base security and local police have no intent to interfere with our first amendment right to free speech. These are friendly, peaceful, and fun events. You are more than welcome to bring children with you and help them learn about grass roots citizenship.

Please drive to our location and unload any passengers and gear. You will then be directed to our remote parking area and shuttle drivers will bring you back to the protest.

A core principle behind our events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

events.description:
Given major issues at the federal level, we need our state and city governments to step up, meet the moment, and implement transformative renewable energy policy.

So we'll be out in the Lower East Side to petition and flyer for the Bucks for Boilers Act, a bill to fund the replacement of outdated, dirty gas with clean energy!

If passed, Bucks for Boilers will mandate that all gas boilers in need of replacement are replaced with heat pumps through a state-funded program. 

Ultimately, a home that is properly insulated and using the latest electric heat pump technology will result in lower bills over time. The Bucks for Boilers Act is an investment in our future.

We'll be collecting petition signatures urging local State Senator Kavanaugh to join on as a co-sponsor!

These programs are the backbone of our communities, helping seniors retire with dignity, ensuring children have healthcare and food, supporting people with disabilities, and providing coverage for families whose jobs don’t offer affordable insurance.

We’re rallying to make one thing clear: cutting healthcare and food assistance is cutting into the heart of our communities. Rockford deserves leaders who fight for us, not against our wellbeing.

events.title: Protect America's Workforce Act - Nebraska Phone Bank
events.description:
It’s time to get it done for America’s workers.

Thanks to the hard work of working families, union members and our allies, our bipartisan bill to reverse President Trump’s union-busting executive order is getting a vote in Congress.

That’s right: We’ve got the 218 signatures we need—Democrats AND Republicans—to force Congress to vote on the Protect America’s Workforce Act in the next few weeks.

This is an all-hands-on-deck moment to help restore collective bargaining rights to the more than 1 million federal workers. 

Trump’s executive order to gut federal workers’ collective bargaining rights was the worst act of union-busting in American history. Since then, his administration has expanded the order to cover even more workers and canceled the union contracts of nearly half a million federal workers at agencies like the departments of Agriculture, Veterans Affairs, and Health and Human Services.

The American people didn’t sign up for this. Approximately 70% of Americans—people with different political positions—support the right to join a union. That’s why we have the support we need to get the Protect America’s Workforce Act across the finish line.

We need every representative—Republican or Democrat—who says they support America’s unions to vote for the Protect America’s Workforce Act and restore federal workers’ union rights.

Michigan United Action is part of Michiganders for Money Out of Politics (MMOP). We are going to fight back against corporate control of our government.

Our goal: Pass a citizen-led ballot initiative that bans political contributions from regulated monopoly utilities (like DTE and Consumers Energy) and corporations that seek or hold large state and local government contracts (over $250,000)

Why? Simple: We want to stop corporations from buying off our democracy.

Is this a campaign you support? Just ask yourself: Do we want a government that serves us — or a government bought and paid for by corporations?

events.title: No Partisan Maps - House Redistricting Committee Dec 10th
events.description:
In an attempt to rush the unconstitutional partisan midterm redistricting through, the house has scheduled another committee hearing on Dec 10th The hearing will be in the Capitol building at Reed Hall (102 HOB). 

Florida voters have already spoken loud and clear: we do not want mid-decade redistricting, and we refuse to accept partisan gerrymandering that rigs our districts for political gain. Now, the Legislature is moving toward drawing new voting maps before the next election—a move that violates Florida’s Constitution and threatens our democracy. Because drawing maps to benefit any party is illegal in Florida. 

Join advocates from across the state in Tallahassee to make sure lawmakers hear us: No mid-decade power grabs. No partisan maps. Honor the Fair Districts Amendments.

What We’ll Do

We’ll gather at the Florida Capitol, connect with organizers and community members, and attempt to speak directly with legislators, urging them to protect voters—not politicians. We will also make our voices heard during the committee hearing, where decisions about redistricting may be on the table.

Why It Matters

Floridians passed the Fair Districts Amendments to stop politicians from manipulating district lines for partisan advantage.

Drawing new maps now—mid-decade—is a direct response to national calls for gerrymandering and is illegal under Florida’s Constitution.

Partisan mid-decade map-drawing would disproportionately silence Black, Brown, and working-class communities across the state.

Redistricting determines who represents us. This process must serve the people, not political interests.

Our Message

No rigged maps. No partisan games.

Protect fair representation for all Floridians.

Say NO to any mid-decade redistricting scheme.

Florida’s democracy works best when every voice is heard—and yours is essential. Join us in Tallahassee to stand up for fair maps and a fair future.

More details will be shared as we get closer to the event.

**Vanessa Aronson will join us on Tuesday, December 2, at 11:00am ET.**
Many of us supported Vanessa Aronson in her recent campaign for NYC Council for which she came a few hundred votes short. Now she is running for NYS Assembly for District 73.
Vanessa Aronson is a tireless, tested and trusted champion for the east side of Manhattan. Vanessa served as president of the Lexington Democratic Club, is a Judicial Delegate and a member of the County Democratic Committee, serving on the Ethics Committee. Vanessa held leadership roles on the local Community Board and at Park Avenue Synagogue, where she supported her community's most vulnerable neighbors. She taught in NYC public schools and, as an advisor to the president of Hunter College, strengthened our education system. As a Foreign Service Officer, she tackled food insecurity around the world. Throughout her career, Vanessa has fearlessly lived her values and promoted democracy, safety and security.

We strive to build community, educate voters, and use our Sharpies to write to save democracy together. Write postcards with us or just join the conversation. If you need help getting started with postcarding, please visit our [FAQ](https://markersfordemocracy.org/postcarding/postcarding-faq).

Election Board Meetings permit Public Comments (3 minutes per person). Arrive early and sign up to speak. You must sign up before the meeting starts. Do not expect a response from the Election Board for questions or comments. Follow the rules laid out by the Election Board. We want to have a large presence at the meeting, armed with appropriate talking points and questions. 

Access to voting is not a for-profit business. It is our constitutional right!

Recommendation: Express your opinions as a nonpartisan member of the community.  This change, if approved, would affect ALL voters in Spalding County, including Republican, Independent, and Democratic. Invite your friends and neighbors to attend this Election Board meeting.

events.title: Stop Partisan Redistricting - Tallahassee Indivisible
events.description:
##  **STOP PARTISAN MID-DECADE REDISTRICTING**
### Mass Protest -- Committee Hearing -- Legislative Office Visits

## The Issue
**Redistricting** is the process of drawing the boundaries that determine who lives in each voting district and who represents them. Under Florida’s Constitution, it is _illegal_ to draw maps that favor any political party. Floridians made this clear when we passed the **Fair Districts Amendments** in 2010.

Any effort to redraw voting maps before the next election—especially in response to the President’s call for nationwide partisan gerrymandering—is unlawful in Florida. It also goes against the will of the people: majorities across party lines oppose both mid-decade redistricting and partisan gerrymandering.



## How We Fight Back

**WE NEED EVERY ONE OF YOU** on **December 4th** to make our voices impossible to ignore and send an unmistakable message to our state legislators: Floridians will not tolerate illegal partisan gerrymandering.

[Indivisible Tallahassee](indivisibletallahassee.com) is joining partners from across the state for  several days of action at the Florida Capitol. **The most important one is on December 4th.**
	

## THURSDAY, DEC. 4th starting at 12pm.


Choose one of the following opportunities. But MOST NEEDED is to show up for ALL THREE. We **must** deliver an unmistakable message to the Governor, the Legislature, and to Florida and the entire country: **This is wrong. This is illegal. This is a blatant, undeniable power grab.**

 - **Mass Protest at the Capitol** from 12:00-2:00 PM @ Florida Historic Capitol, 400 S. Monroe St.
 - **Visit Your Legislators' offices** anytime before or after the Protest or the Committee Hearing. 
 - **[Hearing of the Select Committee on Congressional Redistricting](https://www.flhouse.gov/Sections/Committees/committeesdetail.aspx?CommitteeId=3364)**  **PLEASE ATTEND** from **1:30-3:00PM,** 102 House Office Bldg, Reed Hall - 402 S. Monroe St, Tallahassee, FL 32399-1300. 

## What to Expect

After signing up: 

 - We'll send you talking points to share with your legislators. 
 - We'll share messaging to use in commenting during the hearing.
 - Need to find your legislators' offices? 
	 - Click here for your [Florida House Representative](https://www.flhouse.gov/FindYourRepresentative)
	 - Click here for your [State Senator](https://www.flsenate.gov/senators) 

## Why It Matters

events.title: Capitalism, Socialism, and the Battle of Ideas

location.venue: Elkridge Branch - Howard County Library System

events.description:
## Hosted by HoCo for Human Dignity • Led by Dr. Jared Ball

**When**: Wednesday, December 17, 5:30–7:00 pm

**Where**: Hockley Room

**Hosted by**: Howard County for Human Dignity (HoCo for Human Dignity)

**Discussion Leader**: Dr. Jared Ball

**Featuring**: Claudia De La Cruz, Activist and former Party for Socialism and Liberation presidential candidate

In the wake of Mamdani’s victory and a growing openness to alternatives to the status quo, many people are asking: What is socialism actually? How is it different from capitalism? And why are we taught to fear it so intensely?

Join HoCo for Human Dignity for a community discussion led by Dr. Jared Ball on the real differences between capitalism and socialism. We’ll look at how advertising, PR, and psychological warfare shape what we believe is “common sense,” who benefits from that, and what a different kind of society could look like.

We’ll explore questions like:
- What are the core values and assumptions of capitalism vs. socialism?
- How do these systems shape our daily lives — work, housing, healthcare, education?
- What role does marketing, media, and psychological warfare play in keeping people skeptical of socialism?
- How can we build power for working people and communities instead of corporations and billionaires?

We’ll also encourage attendees to read Socialist Reconstruction from the Party for Socialism and Liberation (PSL) as a way to go deeper, and talk about bringing PSL and other organizers/experts into future sessions.

All are welcome — whether you already identify as a socialist, are curious and skeptical, or just want a space to ask honest questions and think together about a different future.

Join us to support public education, teachers, and students on December 2nd!

Did you know that:

Charter and private schools weakly or partially comply with State requirements to have certified professional teachers or have a full offering of extracurricular activities?

Private schools are not required to comply with State requirements to accept
students with special needs or to have students assessed through state tests for academic achievement?

Charter and private schools are also not required to comply with State requirements for the following:

   Certified professional administrators
   Governed by an elected school board
   Neighborhood school locations
   Buildings that meet safety and hurricane standards
   All students are accepted regardless of gender identity
   Discipline policies are published for public review


Please keep the message of your signs on supporting public education, students, and teachers.


Park at Lowe Orthodontics on Clyde Morris or at Walmart on Dunlawton.

events.title: Door Knock on Dec 6 for Dr. Satani and Help Flip District 98!
events.description:
🚪✨ Charleston Dems: Let’s Flip House District 98! ✨🚪

January 6, 2026 is a BIG day — there’s a special election in one of the most competitive districts anywhere near Charleston. Competitive races in SC don’t come around often, and this is our chance to make a real impact.

Dr. Sonja Satani, our Democratic candidate for SC House District 98 (Charleston + Dorchester Counties), can actually win this seat — but only if we help her get out the vote.

👟 The Peninsula Dems Are Hitting the Pavement 

We’re hosting two door-knocking days for Dr. Satani:

• Saturday, December 6 
• Saturday, December 13

Don’t worry — this is NOT about persuading MAGA voters.

We’re knocking on the doors of friendly Democrats to make sure they know there’s a special election, know where to vote, and turn out. That’s it.

You’ll be:

• Going out in small groups (no one solos!)
• Getting clear training + guidance
• Walking suburban, super-walkable neighborhoods

📍 Event Details

Date: December 6, 2025 
Meet Time: 1030AM 
Location: Panera Bread, 9480 Dorchester Rd
When you arrive, we will assign you to a door-knocking group. 
Questions: Email Richie at charlestonpeninsulademocrats@gmail.com 

What you need:
• Download the MiniVAN app
• Dr. Satani’s campaign will share a code to unlock our walk list on the app 
• The app maps out addresses for you — easy and beginner-friendly
• Plan for 3–4 hours of door knocking with your group

⸻

🧭 Connect with the Campaign

Dr. Satani’s campaign manager, Nick Outen, is happy to answer any questions. If you’re in North Charleston or Dorchester County, Nick can plug you into even more volunteer opportunities. Email Nick at nicholaus.outen@gmail.com.

events.title: Blow the Whistle on ICE Party
events.description:
🔊 YOU'RE INVITED TO A BLOW THE WHISTLE ON ICE PARTY! 🔊
Build Power Together. Protect Our Neighbors.
Sunday, December 7 3:30 - 5:30 p.m.
Downtown Greeley Armory

Why This Matters
Our community deserves to know its rights and feel safe. Together, we're creating "Know Your Rights" whistle packets that empower people to look out for each other and stand up to illegal ICE activity. When we organize together, we build the kind of people power that can't be ignored.

Three Ways YOU Can Make an Impact:
💰 DONATE SUPPLIES
Bring any of these items to help us reach more people:

Whistles (lots of them!)
String or cord
Sandwich/ziplock bags
"Know Your Rights" cards or info (we'll have some available)

✋ ASSEMBLE PACKETS
Join us at the event to:

Put together whistle packets that will go directly into community members' hands.
Learn about your own rights and how whistle brigades work
Meet neighbors who share your commitment to justice.

📦 GRAB & DISTRIBUTE
If you don't have supplies to donate or can't stick around to help us make the bags, you can still take finished packets to:

Pass out in your neighborhood
Share with local businesses
Give to community organizations
Hand to anyone who wants to help protect immigrant rights


The Bigger Picture
These simple packets are tools for resistance. When neighbors have whistles and know their rights, communities can:

Alert each other to ICE activity
Document what's happening
Respond together rather than in isolation
Create accountability through collective witnessing

Whistle brigades work because they turn individual fear into collective courage.

Commitment to Safety
In line with our organizing principles:

This is a nonviolent, legal community action
We prioritize de-escalation and respect
All activities are lawful and focus on education and empowerment
Data privacy and personal security are our top priorities


Can't Make It But Want to Help?
Donate supplies: Drop off whistles, string, or bags at [contact info/location]
Spread the word: Share this with friends, neighbors, coworkers, and community groups
Stay connected: [Contact info for updates and future actions]

"An attack on one is an attack on all of us. When we organize together, we become powerful."
See you December 7th! Bring friends. Bring hope. Bring whistles.

events.title: Love as Action - Philadelphia

location.venue: Love Park - Corner of 16th Street and JFK Blvd

events.description:
Quaker witness for public action has stood in silent opposition to cruel and authoritarian actions in our country before. It is time for us to show this love in action again.

Please join the American Friends Service Committee, Friends Meetings and Quaker organizations throughout the Greater Philadelphia region, to bear witness to the destruction and dehumanization that federal immigration actions are inflicting in our communities.

On Saturday Dec. 6 at Noon, we will gather at Love Park (16th Street and JFK Blvd in Center City, Philadelphia) for one hour of silent public worship and community fellowship, while holding signs and banners (homemade and printed) that express our unwavering support for immigrants in our communities.

Our hope is that our presence will give heart to all who see us – including through media and online communications – and remind everyone of our moral obligations to one another.

This is the first of what we hope will become a series of actions in future months all across our country, showing love in action as a public witness of our Quaker values in a time of rising fascism.

events.title: Listen to Win: Empathetic Conversations Training with Swing Left

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
**Note:** This is an in-person event in Mountain View, CA.

Politics is about persuasion—reaching out, person to person, and bringing others along. But persuasion doesn’t mean you’re rattling off statistics, arguing about policy, or convincing someone to do a 180º on the spot. In fact, persuasion starts with listening.

In a fractured political environment, it is both more challenging and more important to engage with those who might not vote like us (or not vote at all!). We know talking with voters works, but more often than not, Democratic campaigns start too late and target too narrowly. They underinvest in persuasion conversations, and ignore 1 in 4 potential voters because they’re unlisted or mislisted in the data Democrats rely on. Swing Left's new Ground Truth canvassing program will change that. By starting early and having empathetic listening conversations with every voter, we’re uncovering concerns that campaigns need to address, earning trust in communities that might feel overlooked, and making sure Democrats are speaking to what people actually want. That’s how we help Democrats flip the House in the 2026 midterm elections.

This new approach to voter contact means we’ll be talking with all kinds of people, and we know that can be intimidating. Whether you’re knocking on doors in a swing district, simply talking with a friend, or anything in between, honing your empathetic listening skills will help us engage in productive conversations—and ultimately change the hearts and minds we need to win. 

Come learn more about how empathetic listening conversations work, and how you can get involved now to win in 2026.

*Hosted by It's Blue Turn*
