Every Saturday at 1:00 PM | Coolidge Corner

Join members of three Brookline pro-democracy groups — indivisible Activist Evenings, Brookline Pax, and Speak Out, Seniors! — for our weekly rally at Coolidge Corner.

We gather to raise our voices and our signs in defense of democracy, justice, and decency — and to stand united against the abuses of the Trump administration and the forces that threaten our rights and freedoms.

We stand for:

• Immigrant rights, human rights, and racial justice

• Free speech, the Constitution, and the rule of law

• Access to health and healthcare for all

• Protection of our planet and the future we leave to the next generation

We choose empathy over cruelty, peace over violence, and hope over fear.

Our rallies are peaceful, spirited, and uplifting — a chance to connect, recharge, and stand up for what matters. Bring your friends, your voice, and your sign (or borrow one of ours!).

All are welcome!  The rally is multi-generational and family-friendly; those using walkers or other mobility devices may use them to sit to participate.

events.title: Gathering/ Potluck, Palmer Alaska, Mat-Su United for Progress
events.description:
## Join Us for Our Monthly Gathering & Potluck — Help Shape MSUP’s Future

Our next Monthly Gathering & Potluck is coming up, and this one is an important milestone for Mat-Su United for Progress. We're asking everyone who can make it to join us at **6:30 p.m.** for a short business meeting before we roll into a fun, themed potluck.

This month we’ll take two big steps forward:

### 1. Voting to Adopt Our Bylaws

After months of collaborative work, edits, and discussion, our bylaws are ready for final approval. These bylaws lay the foundation for how MSUP will operate — how we make decisions, how our Board functions, and how we stay accountable to each other.  
[Here are the draft Bylaws for you perusal.](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1iLaXp7hGrWY7dIOb3GqZ35eS6PQA19PcHxsv6w_fNUY/edit?usp=sharing)

### 2. Electing Officers Under the New Bylaws

Once the bylaws pass, we’ll hold elections for the officer positions outlined in the document:

- Chair  
- Vice Chair  
- Secretary  
- Treasurer  
- Three (3) At-Large Board Seats  

Whether you’re new to MSUP or have been here since the beginning, **you are welcome to run**.  
Nominations are open now — including self-nominations. If you’d like to nominate yourself  included for review ahead of time.or someone else, please reach out so we can include them in the process.

---

## And Then… It’s Potluck Time!

After the short business meeting, we’ll move right into a themed potluck and a holiday cookie swap — because building community should also be joyful (and delicious).

### Potluck Challenge: Bring a Dish Starting With the First Letter of Your First Name

Have fun with it!

- Dave might bring *dumplings*.  
- Lynn might show up with *lasagna*.  
- Pete could appear with *potato salad*.  

Feel free to be creative, chaotic, or classic — it’s all welcome.

### Holiday Cookie Swap (Optional but Highly Encouraged!)

If you love having an assortment of cookies around the holidays, join in:

- Bring **three dozen** of one kind of cookie.  
- Leave with **three dozen** of all different kinds.

It’s a sweet way to share traditions — and go home with treats.

---

## Why This Night Matters

This past year, we’ve rallied, organized, showed up for local issues, and built a community that supports one another. Now we’re putting structure behind that energy so we can keep growing and be ready for the work ahead.

Approving our bylaws and electing officers strengthens MSUP.  
Sharing food strengthens our community.

I hope you’ll join us — to vote, to nominate, to run, to eat, or simply to be part of what we’re building together.

**See you at 6:30 p.m. — and don’t forget the dish that starts with your name!**
*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

Confused about the courts and their role in our democracy? You are NOT alone! 

Come and learn about the critical functions of our NC courts and how without fair courts, we have lost our last line of defense against gerrymandering. Fair judges lead to fair maps and fair elections. Find out what YOU can do to ensure our elections are fair to all NC citizens! 

There are 4 critical judicial races in our 2026 elections, including a State Supreme Court seat.  We MUST work to ensure the election of fair judges. 

We have numerous opportunities for getting involved, including work at home (writing, phoning, helping with social media messaging); spreading the word neighbor-to-neighbor; door knocking; dropping literature on porches; and many others! 

Join us on at the High Point Public Library to learn details and begin the work of making sure North Carolina has fair elections. 

Space is limited! Be sure to register to ensure your seat!

events.title: Newburyport "Tea & Toy Party" Protest and March
events.description:
In place of our regular weekly protest, the Newburyport Democratic City Committee will host a Tea & Toy Party Protest in honor of the Newburyport Tea Party (yes, that happened here too!).  It will be held on Saturday, December 13th from 11 AM to 12:30 PM. (Please note that this event is longer than our weekly protest.)

In December 1773, Newburyport residents burned shipments of tea in Market Square to protest the tea tariffs imposed by King George III and the British Parliament. 

Now we're protesting the Trump tariffs - but instead of burning tea we will march from the Bartlet Mall to Market Square. Come out in your colonial best and we'll make our own protest history!

Weather permitting, we will meet at the Bartlet Mall and march down Green Street to the Christmas tree and Menorah in Market Square.
We will have a brief introduction at the Mall and then a speech or two in Market Square about the Newburyport Tea Party and how it parallels what we are going through today. 

TOY PARTY DONATION GUIDELINES

We welcome you to bring a new, unwrapped holiday gift or gift card to donate to the Boys and Girls Club of Salisbury. They asked us to provide the following guidelines:

* Please bring an unwrapped toy or gift card only. No clothing. 
* Gifts should be geared for 1st - 12th graders.  
* For middle and high school, they recommend gift cards for food places like Duncan Donuts, McDonalds, pizza places (chains). Please purchase these in $10.00 increments.
* All gifts must be unwrapped. 

Thank you in advance to all who choose to bring a gift to our "Tea & Toy Party" protest. The Boys and Girls Club is so appreciative  -- and we love the idea of expanding our outreach to include helping youth in our community.

events.title: Interfaith vigil for international Migrants'Day with Miramar Circle of Protection

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
On Wednesday, December 17, Florida will host an Interfaith Vigil outside the Miramar ICE facility to mark International Migrants Day. People of faith, community leaders, families, and immigrants will gather to pray, bear witness, and highlight ongoing abuses—including prolonged detentions, intimidation during check-ins, and the growing involvement of local agencies in immigration enforcement through 287(g).

The vigil will honor the dignity of all migrants and lift up our shared commitment to justice, compassion, and human rights.

This gathering is part of a broader national moment. From Dec. 10 to Dec. 18, communities across the U.S. are observing Human Rights Day and International Migrants Day by denouncing immigration raids, detention, and deportation—and by calling attention to harmful 287(g) agreements that fuel fear, racial profiling, and family separation.

Together, we stand in solidarity with immigrants and people on the move, working toward a world where everyone is free to live, belong, and thrive.

events.title: Press Conference & Petition Delivery: Enforceable Heat Standards Now

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

events.description:
Join the Arizona Heat Standards Coalition at the Arizona State Capitol as we call for strong, enforceable heat protections for workers ahead of next summer.

As extreme heat continues to threaten the lives of construction workers, farmworkers, delivery drivers, and countless others, our coalition is bringing forward worker testimonies, community voices, and policy solutions. Arizona can’t wait any longer.  We need water, shade, and rest guaranteed in every workplace. 

As part of this event, we will also be delivering more than 1,500 petitions from Arizonans urging Governor Hobbs and the Arizona Division of Occupational Safety and Health (ADOSH) to adopt enforceable heat protections. These signatures represent families, workers, and community members across the state demanding action. 

Led by a steering committee of AFSCME, Agave Community Threads, AZ AANHPI, Arizona Jobs with Justice, EDF Action, Mi Familia en Acción, National COSH, SEIU, and UNITE HERE.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Únete a la Coalición de Estándares de Calor de Arizona en el Capitolio del Estado de Arizona mientras exigimos protecciones contra el calor fuertes y exigibles para las y los trabajadores antes del próximo verano.

A medida que el calor extremo sigue amenazando la vida de trabajadores de la construcción, jornaleros agrícolas, repartidores y muchas otras personas, nuestra coalición presentará testimonios de trabajadores, voces comunitarias y soluciones de política pública. Arizona no puede esperar más. Necesitamos garantizar agua, sombra y descanso en todos los lugares de trabajo.

Como parte de este evento, también entregaremos más de 1,500 peticiones que instan a la Gobernadora Hobbs y a la División de Seguridad y Salud Ocupacional de Arizona (ADOSH) a adoptar protecciones contra el calor que sean verdaderamente exigibles. Estas firmas representan a familias, trabajadores y miembros de la comunidad en todo el estado que demandan acción.

Este esfuerzo está liderado por un comité directivo compuesto por AFSCME, Agave Community Threads, AZ AANHPI, Arizona Jobs with Justice, EDF Action, Mi Familia en Acción, National COSH, SEIU y UNITE HERE.

events.title: New Circle Host Orientation Call
events.description:
## Learn how to start a SURJ Circle!

This call is for SURJ members who want to learn more about starting a SURJ Circle—or are ready to take the first step to launch one!

A SURJ Circle is a small, in-person organizing group (usually 3–15 people) that meets at least monthly to move SURJ’s national campaigns forward through local action.

**Why Circles?**

The only way we can slow down and prevent the worst of Trump’s authoritarian attacks is by doing this work together in our communities. Circles grow the movement—creating spaces to build relationships and skills, take bold local action in coordination with national strategy, and welcome new people into the work.

SURJ designs campaigns—like elections, immigration defense, and noncooperation—to be done in teams. Campaigns are more effective and more motivating when we do them together!

**Register now—we’ll send follow-up materials even if you can’t make it live.**

events.description:
Please join Democracy Support Group on Hillandale and Engaged Durhamites for Democracy every Friday 3-4:00pm (unless it is raining) at Samuels Drive and Hillandale near Croasdaile in Durham.

Come through the welcome entrance at Croasdaile, 2600 Croasdaile Farm Parkway, ask for directions to Samuels Drive and north parking lot and follow signs for EVENT PARKING.

Park anywhere in the north parking lot. We walk out the gate on Samuels Drive.

Signs are available. Emphasis on policies and not personalities.

This will be a POSITIVE and nonviolent protest. We are here to protect our democracy. We are standing up for what we believe in. We want to inspire people to join us and grow our movement!

Please bring positive signs only. Some examples: Instead of "Stop defunding science" Say "Protect Research" "Immigrants make us stronger" "Housing for all" "Healthcare for all" "Save the planet"

Make signs about what you're standing up for -- whether that is the libraries, DEI, healthcare, women’s rights

Please no mocking signs, no swastikas

We are excited to see you there and stand together for our country!

See you every Friday engaging drivers in Durham.

Please join our Substack: https://substack.com/profile/115484101-engaged-durhamites-4-democracy

For more ED4D Mobilize Events: https://www.mobilize.us/engageddurhamitesfordemocracy/

events.title: Indivisible NEO General Meeting with Licensed Counselor Kathryn Raven
events.description:
Join us at our general meeting where we welcome Kathryn Raven. She is a Licensed Professional Clinical Counselor with over 25 years of clinical experience. She is currently facilitating adult individual psychotherapy in an UHCMC outpatient clinic. Raven’s areas of expertise include: psychological trauma, stress, anxiety, and anger management, coping skills development, processing grief/loss, relationship concerns, and personal growth in self-esteem, value, worth, and self-respect. She also has 10 years of hospice experience. Having been around diverse populations most of her life, Kathryn has taken an interest in human disconnection & connection.

Othering is an innate urge creating caution around the differences in another to keep ourselves safe. Simultaneously, there exists a deep mammalian urge for human connection. These drives are veiled in equality vs inequality, exclusion vs inclusion, openness vs closed, conservative vs liberal, and threatening vs safe. How do we choose our friends, families, neighborhoods, and communities? Do we make our choices knowingly or unknowingly? What/ who influences our decisions/ choices around places to live/ work/ socialize in and around how we feel about different people? Can we overcome our natural urge to be fearful of differences and shut people out of our lives? Yet, in our desire to connect, we may open our doors too wide…some people are really not safe to be around. We need to develop our discernment to better sense who is actually threatening vs someone who is simply different. In order to survive we need both the desire to be safe and the desire to connect.

events.title: Family Meeting: Child Care & the Washington State Budget Emergency
events.description:
**--------------Español abajo —--------------**
 
Organizing for a brighter future for Washington families in 2026 starts now! It’s time to huddle up and make a 2026 game plan for protecting child care during the Washington state budget crisis. 

Join SEIU 925, Children's Campaign Fund Action, and MomsRising for a virtual **Family Meeting: Child Care & the State Budget Emergency.**

Our state is in a budget crisis, and we know most of our families are too. We’re calling a family meeting to learn about what’s at stake and to co-create the budget solutions that will lift all families.

Together, we'll get up to speed about the state of the 2026 state budget and how budget choices will impact moms, families, caregivers, and workers in our state. We'll hear from leaders from across Washington state, including Senator Claire Wilson, Senator Emily Alvarado, Representative Mary Fosse, and leaders from SEIU 925 and MomsRising.

¡La tarea de organizar un futuro mejor para las familias de Washington para el 2026 comienza ahora! Es hora de reunirnos y elaborar un plan de acción para el 2026 con el fin de proteger el cuidado infantil durante la crisis presupuestaria que enfrenta el estado de Washington.

Juntos nos pondremos al corriente sobre la situación actual del presupuesto estatal para el 2026 y cómo las decisiones presupuestarias afectarán a mamás, familias, a los que proveen cuidado infantil y a trabajadores de nuestro estado. events.title: Holiday Food Distribution Volunteering - SF Democrats & Booker T Washington CSC
events.description:
Food insecurity in San Francisco is at a critical point. Even in one of the wealthiest cities in the country, many families, seniors, and working people struggle to afford groceries as costs rise and displacement increases. For too many neighbors, the weekly choice is between paying rent or buying food.

That’s why volunteer-powered food distribution matters. When we pack bags and support local food programs, we’re doing more than moving boxes. We’re giving families dignity and relief. Every hour volunteered expands the number of people we can serve and strengthens our community safety net.

We’re proud to assist Booker T. Washington Community Service Center, a century-old Black-led institution that has supported San Franciscans for generations. Booker T. provides everything from hot meals to childcare to senior services, creating a welcoming space for all. By volunteering here, you’re supporting a pillar of the community working every day to build a more inclusive and thriving San Francisco.

https://btwcsc.org/

We ask that our Food Justice volunteers: 

 • Be physically able to comfortably stand, lift, bend, pack, and carry items 

 • Please wear layers (we may be working outside) 

 • Wear comfortable clothing and closed-toed, supportive shoes 

 • Commit to one whole shift 

 • We may ask that folks wear a face mask and gloves (we will provide) 

 • Be kind and patient with our staff and clients 

 • We will have access to bathrooms and water 

 • We do not offer parking; rideshares and public transportation is highly recommended. 

 • Please do not take photos of the Center, children or our clients without our explicit permission. 


Co-sponsored by:

Join Chispa and Crece for a special PONCHE & CAÑA workshop, part of Crece’s Community Saturdays ( a weekly gathering where each Saturday centers a different food theme.) This Saturday's focus is “Food Is Life,” and we’re excited to dig into the roots, culture, and community behind the ingredients that nourish us.

At this workshop, we’ll be learning how to make traditional ponche using caña (sugar cane) grown by a local farmer. Along the way, we’ll explore the rich and complicated history of the sugar cane crop: its journey through trade systems, how it migrated across regions, and the role it has played in shaping food, culture, and community survival.

We’ll also learn the basics of planting and growing caña, so you can take that knowledge back to your home, garden, or community space.

And of course, we’ll be sharing a warm meal together, building connection, joy, and community care as we learn, and celebrate.


You don’t want to miss this beautiful night of culture, food, and community!

events.title: Northern Illinois December Meeting
events.description:
We are starting a new PDA Chapter Organizing Committee in Northern Illinois. Please join activists from the greater Rockford area for this first meeting. Let's be a model for other regional chapters as we move Progressive issues and legislators forward! We have an agenda (below) and a great guest speaker, David Kraft from the Nuclear Energy Information Service.
 
Agenda:
1. Introductions
2. History of PDA and why a Northern IL PDA Chapter is being formed.
3. David Kraft's presentation.
4. Q & A
5. Forming the PDA Northern thern ILL. What do we need to do? What are the possibilities?
 
Please share this invitation with friends interested in building a Progressive Movement, including getting Progressive decision-makers elected!
 
Special Guest Speaker, Dave Kraft from the Nuclear Energy Information Service, speaking on "The Role of Nuclear Power in Ending Global Warming". Dave is a safe-energy advocate and co-founder of NEIS. He has served as its director since its inception in 1981. Kraft’s interest in the environment moved him to found NEIS with seven other people to provide the public with credible information about the hazards and effects of nuclear power and waste, and the viable means to replace them. 
 
Kraft is an accomplished public speaker and writer on nuclear topics.  He has been called upon to testify in hearings related to nuclear power at the state and federal levels. He was responsible for creating the “Know Nukes!” series of videos on nuclear topics in cooperation with CAN-TV Chicago, and is a co-founder of the Radiation Monitoring Project, designed to provide training and field monitors to communities contaminated by radioactive substances. He has received recognition and awards for his work, most recently, in May 2016, the Judith Johnsrud “Unsung Hero of the Year” award for his lifelong activism.
 
Ask to join our Google Group to share information and stay in touch - NIPDA@googlegroups.com, 
Register for our chapter launch meeting here:
 
Bob Babcock - PDA Rockford - 630.417.0042 - weloverockvalley@hotmail.com
Dan O'Neal - PDA National Organizing Team - 489-650-0746 - dan@pdamerica.org

events.title: Stand Up for Government Transparency: Join Us in Trenton on 12/1!
events.description:
**Good government is under attack in New Jersey in a way it never has been before! We need to act! Join us in Trenton on 12/1 to defend the Office of the State Comptroller!** 

Our state has struggled for a long time with ethics and transparency. Now our state reps want to erode the limited existing protections we residents have by stripping the Office of the State Comptroller of its power to identify potential waste, conflicts of interest, and corruption. The time is now for us to push back and demand government oversight. **Without government watchdogs, nepotism and corruption will spread, leading to a more expensive state and one less centered around the needs of residents.**

**On Monday, December 1, 10 AM, a State Senate Committee chaired by LD6 Senator and Camden County Democratic Committee Chairman Jim Beach will be voting on a bill that would disempower our State Comptroller.** The timing here is not coincidental. The State Comptroller recently published a report that noted numerous concerns with the State Health Insurance Fund (HIF) and many of them were centered around the firms collecting massive profits that all have clear ties to George Norcross. **Once again, what's at stake is whether our government serves the people or the party boss.**

**We need you to join us in Trenton on Monday Dec 1 to show up in defense of the Office of State Comptroller and the need for transparency and oversight in our government.** There will be opportunities to testify for anyone interested. If you don't want to testify but want to make your opinion known, you can join us there and fill out a slip that will be read stating opposition to the bill. 

For those interested in carpooling up from South Jersey to the Statehouse together, we will be meeting at Kate Delany's house in Collingswood at 8:15 AM. We will share some talking points with anyone interested in speaking and will have South Jersey Progressive Democrats stickers for anyone who needs one. 

**Let's stand up for good government together on 12/1 in Trenton!**

[S4924]: (https://pub.njleg.state.nj.us/Bills/2024/S5000/4924_I1.PDF)
[State Comptroller's report on the HIF]: (https://www.nj.gov/comptroller/reports/2025/20250909.shtml)

events.title: MULTIPLE FUTURES and other PARANOID FANTASIES
events.description:
MULTIPLE FUTURES — The Films That Warned Us

If you’re part of NO KINGS, these films are required viewing.
Not optional. Not casual.
Required.

Alyce Wittenstein’s Multiple Future trilogy didn’t just imagine authoritarianism, corporate domination, and the collapse of democratic norms — it predicted them with eerie accuracy.
These films feel less like fiction and more like field notes for the resistance.

🎥 BETAVILLE

A mind-bending vision inspired by Godard’s Alphaville, Betaville imagines a city-state ruled entirely by the dictates of style.
Fashion isn’t just culture — it’s law.
Aesthetics function as the surveillance system, the weapon, and the regime. Citizens are kept compliant through the meticulously enforced rules of appearance, expression, and trend. Deviate from the prescribed “look,” and you’re marked as a threat.

It’s glamorous. It’s absurd.
It’s authoritarianism dressed in couture — and its parallels to our influencer-driven, algorithm-engineered world hit harder every year.

🎥 NO SUCH THING AS GRAVITY

A fierce, visionary work powered by an extraordinary trio of underground icons:
Nick Zedd of the Cinema of Transgression,
Taylor Mead, the legendary Andy Warhol superstar,
and Emmanuelle Chaulet, known for her luminous collaborations with Éric Rohmer.
Their collective presence gives the film its rebellious pulse, its humor, its bite, and its enduring resonance.

In this future, corporations don’t just dominate the world — they govern it outright.
Identity, livelihood, belonging, and even truth are controlled by a single mega-corporation whose authority is absolute. Opting out of consumer culture is treated as sedition, and anyone who resists is deported off-planet — erased from the system completely.

The film’s world is sleek, seductive, and terrifying — where convenience replaces freedom, and where the illusion of choice masks total control. With its iconic cast and razor-sharp political instinct, No Such Thing As Gravity feels less like a movie and more like a broadcast from the future we’re being pushed toward.

🎥 THE DEFLOWERING

Set in a dystopian future that looks like Victorian London re-wired through steampunk bio-tech, The Deflowering imagines a world where bodily contact is taboo, every child is conceived artificially, and flowers are treated as poisonous contraband. HUXLEY BIO-TECH and its army of white-gloved technicians are on a crusade to “sanitize” and “beautify” the planet—scrubbing away pollen, touch, and anything messy, unpredictable, or alive.

Within this heavily regulated, gear-and-goggles world of corsets, brass machinery, inhalers, and elaborate breathing devices, one couple decides to do the unthinkable: have a baby the old-fashioned way. Their act of intimacy becomes an act of rebellion, setting off moral panic, bureaucratic hysteria, and a witch-hunt against anything natural.

The film’s steampunk-meets-Victorian design—lace and leather fused with tubes, valves, masks, and medical fetish gear—creates a rich, immersive atmosphere where every object feels engineered for control. Underneath that aesthetic, The Deflowering is a sharp, surreal attack on purity culture, bio-control, and the obsession with “perfecting” human life by erasing everything real, alive, and human.

Why NO KINGS Protesters Should Show Up

Because these films show the world we’re fighting against.
Because they clarify the stakes.
Because they remind us how fast things can slide — and how resistance must evolve just as quickly.
And because movements need nights where art sharpens vision, and vision fuels action.

**December 6. Spectacle Theater. One night only.

Let’s fill the theater with NO KINGS energy — and sell this out.**

Come be part of a night that reminds us: our stories matter, our youth matter, and our community is still here: vibrant, proud, and unbanned.

events.description:
Join the Democratic Progressive Caucus of Florida for our 2026 conference in Orlando, FL!

On February 21st, we’ll be hosting a slate of panel discussions and trainings to concentrate on building progressive power and to showcase the path forward. 

To have access to these panels and trainings, you must purchase a ticket or request for a stipend here: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/dpcfconference2026

Our communications panel hosts a roster of amazing content creators, communications directors, and other professionals to discuss the future of progressive digital organizing. Our panelists are the following: 

Kat Dusterhaus (she/they): An award-winning activist and nationally recognized feminist leader within the 50501 Movement, Kat is a certified badass. Their advocacy has helped pass four historic survivor justice laws and push President Biden to declare the ERA the law of the land. Their leadership has earned them the Marsha P. Johnson Award and the Giraffe Award for their activism and courage. Now, their platform @_comrade_kat_ has reached over fifty million people in the last six months alone.

Sebastian Martinez (he/him): As a dedicated public education advocate, the Communications Director for the Florida Young Democrats, and the statewide organizing coordinator for SEE Alliance, Sebastian is a fighter for all. His organizing efforts have included building record breaking field programs and developing campaigns that have reached and educated millions of Florida voters. He is now working to build the “Midterms on our Terms” movement to take back school boards and help shape the 2026 elections.

Lee Perry (she/her): A lifelong environmental educator, climate advocate, and political strategist dedicated to strengthening communities across Central Florida, Lee has it all. She has led urban agriculture initiatives as the Urban Agriculture Program Director for Fleet Farming and as Chief Operations Officer of IDEAS for Us, environmental policy advocacy as a leader within Save Split Oak Forest, and then as a Senior Aide to Orange County Commissioner Nicole Wilson and as a Campaign Manager for Carlos Guillermo Smith. Most recently, she served as Regional Director for Florida Rising, but now leads her own firm, Organizing to Victory, supporting grassroots candidates, nonprofits, and issue-based campaigns.

Natasha Sutherland (she/her): Natasha serves as the Executive Director of Florida Watch, a non-profit hub for messaging development, digital communications, and research. She recently served as an official spokesperson for Yes on 4, Florida’s 2024 abortion rights citizen-led ballot initiative, and recently served as a Commissioner on the Tallahassee-Leon Commission on the Status of Women and Girls. A first-generation American, former educator, and military spouse, Natasha serves as an effective communicator and advocate, helping lift up initiatives that seek to improve the lives of every-day Floridians.

events.title: ⭐ After We March, We Organize: Stand With Starbucks Workers in Strawberry
events.description:
After We March, We Organize: Starbucks Strawberry Solidarity Action

(Mayday Strong / Mobilize)

Workers across the country are organizing for safety, fair schedules, and respect — and Starbucks baristas are at the center of that fight. The Strawberry Village Starbucks crew deserves to know their community sees them, supports them, and stands beside them.

This action is pro-worker, pro-community, and fully nonviolent. We show up with calm energy, strong values, and a commitment to supporting workers without disrupting the store or confronting customers. Think of this as a presence: a visible wave of solidarity that makes workers safer and makes organizing possible.

We’ll gather outside Starbucks in Strawberry Village on public property only. Flyers, talking points, and guidance will be provided on arrival — no experience necessary.

Together, we’ll:

Offer gentle, informative flyers

Keep the tone friendly, steady, and supportive

Let customers approach us (no chasing, no blocking pathways)

Stand in clear, calm solidarity with the workers

Model de-escalation and community care


This action is part of a broader tradition of mutual aid and worker support. Before joining us, please take a moment to review our mutual aid guide so you know exactly how we keep each other and the public safe:

👉 Mutual Aid Guide:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1IYohpjDgaqlLZ0YHhnBecE-s3LkJ6VJr3_bea_ReG3c/edit?usp=sharing

Whether you're brand-new to organizing or a longtime movement builder, this is a simple, effective, meaningful way to stand with workers and strengthen our community
events.accessibility_notes:
✨ STORY OF SELF, US, AND NOW — STRAWBERRY STARBUCKS WORKER SOLIDARITY ACTION

Story of Self — Why I Show Up

I’m Randy, and I didn’t get into organizing because it was easy. I got into it because at every stage of my life — from being unhoused, to serving on the board of the Colorado Coalition for the Homeless, to finally landing in Kruger Pines — I’ve seen how dignity, safety, and stability can turn a person’s whole world around.

Workers gave me food when I had none.
Neighbors gave me a place to sit when I had nowhere to go.
People who didn’t owe me anything showed up anyway.

So now I show up for others.
Especially workers who are trying to organize inside massive corporations where the deck is stacked against them. When Starbucks baristas fight for respect, schedules that don’t wreck their lives, or a voice on the job — that hits home for me. They’re doing the brave thing.

And the least I can do is stand with them.


---

Story of Us — What We Believe Together

All of us coming to this action share something: we know community doesn’t build itself. It’s built moment by moment, hand to hand, when people choose to stand up for one another instead of looking away.

We’re not a mob.
We’re not here to “take down Starbucks.”
We’re neighbors showing up for neighbors — the people who make the coffee, open the store at dawn, smile through the holiday madness, and deserve the same respect anyone else does.

Our shared values shape how we act:

We stay peaceful because fear and chaos don’t build movements — people do.

We stay on public property because the law is a tool, not a trap.

We de-escalate because our goal is to create safety, not conflict.

We never bring weapons because presence is power, not force.

We uplift workers — and we never shame customers or employees.


We’re the ones who build community by showing what solidarity looks like.


---

Story of Now — The Moment We’re Stepping Into

Right now in Strawberry, and across the country, Starbucks workers are organizing. They’re pushing through corporate resistance, legal hurdles, and intimidation tactics big and small. And here’s the truth: those fights go better — and safer — when communities show up with a steady, visible presence.

That’s where we come in.

This action isn’t about confrontation. It’s about protection, connection, and public witness. It’s about letting the workers know that Marin has their back. It’s about modeling the kind of calm, steady solidarity that makes organizing possible.

And to make that happen, we have a process — a safe, confident, welcoming way of showing up:

1. We stand only on public property.

No exceptions. It's where the law protects us, and where we do our best work.

2. We engage people with warmth, not pressure.

A simple “We’re supporting Starbucks workers organizing for fair treatment” goes further than any argument ever could.

3. We de-escalate like it’s a superpower.

Lower voices, open body language, step back, don’t argue.
Disagreement is not danger — escalation is.

4. We watch out for each other.

No one is alone. We stay in eyesight of one another, check in, rotate roles, and keep breaks flowing.

5. We bring heart, not hardware.

No weapons of any kind, even if legal.
This is a space for safety and dignity.

6. We show workers they are seen, valued, and supported.

Even a simple nod or “We’re rooting for you” can change someone’s week.


---

The Invitation

If you’ve never done this before — perfect.
This is exactly the kind of action you learn by doing, with a group that’s got you.

If you have done this before — bring your calm presence, your wisdom, your good energy. Others will follow your lead.

We’re building something — a culture of solidarity that outlasts any single action. This is how worker power spreads. This is how communities stay human.

And it starts with us showing up — together, peacefully, and with purpose.


---

Required Nonviolence & Safety Disclaimer

This event follows a strict commitment to nonviolent action. All participants must avoid verbal or physical confrontation, remain on public property, and actively seek to de-escalate any potential conflict. Weapons of any kind — including those legally permitted — are prohibited. By attending, you agree to uphold these principles and represent our community with safety, dignity, and respect.

events.title: Feet on the Streets - with a twist - tell Home Depot to get I C E out
events.description:
*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

Hi Everyone:

I'm trying to think out of the box for ways to utilized Indivisible to organize a lot of Good Trouble ... 

This is my first try at this, so let's just see how it goes!

You might have all heard about the badass warriors who made a point of all going to Home Depot to purchase an *ice scraper* for super cheap (under a buck) ... with a CREDIT CARD if you can ... and then standing back in line 5 minutes later to return it ... (google it - people are so creative) .

Well, how about we all just do that at our own leisure? 

I tried it last week - it was a success, and it made me feel better LOL ...

Here is what you can do ... as often as you can manage it ... work it into your routines if you have to!   I plan on doing it after all of my protests - on the way home !  

Go to Home Depot ... walk around and "shop" for as long as you want -- I like to go and just PAY ATTENTION -- my eyes are suspect to anyone white and maga-looking (sorry, not sorry for lumping all my counterparts in........) ... keep an eye on them - I hear they like to cosplay as construction workers to fit in!  (they still stick out like a sore thumb in my book).  Have a WHISTLE ready to warn people if you see anything sus .......

Buy California's version of an "ice scraper "   I bought a small putty knife for 98 cents ... 

PAY by your CREDIT CARD if you can - for extra bonus points (they get charged a fee no matter what is purchased with a credit card -- win win) ...

Then, immediately walk right back in the store and go to the Customer Service line to RETURN it !

I told the nice lady (remember it is NOT the employees fault their employers are not-c's ...kindness matters), that I was returning this "ice scraper" in solidarity with my friends in the community - to send a message that we do not welcome thugs into our neighborhoods to terrorize our friends!    All with a smile on my face ... she almost cried when she said, I totally understand !!   and happily returned my buck back to my credit card ...

ANYONE can make this happen -- if you are looking for a way to RESIST with us, but being on a street corner is intimidating (no judgment, we all do what we feel comfy with), well THIS little Good Trouble Causing mission is for you!!!

Bonus points if you then post about it on your social media platforms to encourage others to do this simple act!

They shut down a Home Depot (I feel it was in upper Cali) when they had 100's of people doing this AT THE SAME TIME ...

So, for now, let's just do it on our own ... whenever you can!

Let's also stick together ... if you are on Facebook (I know...but, I'm old like that), friend me!!!!   or inbox me and let me know you are from Indivisible ... then tag me in your post to amplify this idea ... maybe it will take off ...  https://www.facebook.com/janine.manchel


Meantime, I'm going to be sending out a few extra emails in the next few weeks as my brain and imagination work to figure out other ways to resist that aren't necessary getting your Feet on the Streets, yet are still KEY to our Resistance, so I apologize in advance for repeats !   

Also, I'm *always* open to hearing about any locations, or ideas you have to help others to RESIST ... the more we are seen and heard from in the community the better!

So, for today, enjoy your family and meals ... tomorrow, we continue to RESIST !

*Next up:  an actual protest in front of that same Home Depot - maybe we can coordinate it to do the ice scraper thing first, and then protest them afterward ... either on the main road, or right in front of their store ...........*

Beeeeeeep
Beeeeeeeeep
Janine
858-229-9738

This gathering is a space to honor impacted immigrant families and communities and to affirm together that every person deserves dignity, safety, and a stable home.

This vigil’s honoree is **Donna Hughes Brown**, a pillar of Refuge Church in Missouri. 
Donna was detained at Chicago O’Hare Airport after visiting family in Ireland, despite a life here marked by deep roots, faith, caregiving, and quiet service to others. Like so many people in IÇE detention, she deserves the chance to remain in the only home she has known since childhood.

As people of conscience, we come together to stand with Donna, her loved ones, and all families living with the trauma of detention and deportation. We will hold space for prayer, reflection, and testimony, lifting up stories of resilience and calling for immigration policies that keep families together and respect human rights.

**A core principle behind all our events is a shared commitment to nonviolent action. All are welcome to stand with us in hope, grief, and solidarity as we call for compassion and justice for Donna and for all who are detained. events.title: Gather Nomination Signatures for Judge Chris Taylor (DEC 1-15)

events.title: Stand Up! Speak Out!
events.description:
People that are fed up with Nebraska Senators not doing what the majority of people elected them to do.  Bring your grievance on a sign and meet with like minded folks at the intersection of 13th Street and "O" Street in Lincoln, NE from 4-5PM on Fridays. Check the web site for future events:
https://standuplincoln.net/
You can enter the UBT building to visit each Senator's offices, but most likely will find the office door door locked a sign saying you need to schedule your meeting.

events.title: Oregon City Commission Public Comment: ICE Destroys Communities
events.description:
Join us at the Wednesday, Dec. 3rd Oregon City Commission Public Comment portion of meeting.

Support your Interfaith Neighbors, as they deliver a Statement of Opposition to Ice to their elected officials.

Arrive around 6:30 so you can write down your thoughts about Ice terrorizing and destroying communities. Tell our city government that we stand with our immigrant neighbors. The more we visibly dissent, the more we inspire others to join us!

Helpful tips from the City Staff:

1) Submit a written public comment to recorderteam@orcity.org by noon on the day of the meeting. The city staff will make sure everyone on the Commission sees the comment. The earlier you submit a written public comment the better, as it ensures the Commissioners have more time to read it.

2) Speak in person at the meeting. The regular meetings start at 7:00, and public comment is one of the first items on the agenda. When you come into the meeting room, there will be a table on your left with signup cards. Fill one of those out, and give the card to the City Recorder, who will be at a table to the right of the dais.

3) Speak virtually. You can register with the City Recorder to speak virtually through Zoom by emailing recorderteam@orcity.org before 3:00 on the day of the meeting.

events.title: Clackamas Board of County Commissioners: Public Comment

3) Join via Zoom or watch live on YouTube

events.title: No Kings Alliance Mutual Aid Drive in Ridgecrest
events.description:
**The No Kings Alliance is mobilizing urgent, nationwide action in response to the Republican government shutdown. Join us this weekend as we provide mutual aid and care to our neighbors hurt by the Republican government shutdown.**

Right now Republicans are refusing to protect critical healthcare and nutrition programs which will result in 42 million Americans losing the benefits that keep their families fed. When those in power hoard resources and use our government to punish people, we answer with collective care and resistance, feeding our bodies and fueling our movement.

Join us at 132 N China Lake Blvd from 9-11am to donate food, household, and personal care products to support families in need. Donations will be delivered to Salvation Army.

Salvation Army has requested the following goods: Rice-a-roni, Cup of noodles, pasta, canned protein (tuna, chicken, beef, beef stew), cereal & granola bars, cans of nuts, boxed cookies & crackers, dried fruits, beef jerky, dry milk, bottled water, mac & cheese, single serving cups of fruit & pudding, cereal, oatmeal packets, and jelly/jam (no peanut butter, they have enough.)

Donation drop off by the shopping center sign.

Find more out about our group at ridgecrest50501.com

_A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events._

events.title: No Kings Alliance Mutual Aid Drive in WHITTIER,CA!
events.description:
Join the Whittier Indivisible Chapter at Michigan Park in Whittier, CA on November 15th, from 11-12:30pm to gather together and DONATE non-perishable food to support families in need. 

Our Chapter will also host a fundraising campaign for the entire month of November to help those in need - ALL proceeds to the Chapter will be sent to a local food pantry. You can donate here: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/indivisiblewc1368840224

Let us support and love on our community! Thousands in our own cities will be affected by the ending of SNAP benefits, and we want to help them. Will you join us?

Additionally, if you cannot make this Mutual Aid Drive & Potluck event on November 15th, we will be hosting various “pop-up tables” throughout the La Habra/Fullerton/Whittier areas to gather donations throughout the month. Please view our Facebook and Instagram pages for information on locations of these tables. All donations will be delivered to the Santa Fe Springs Interfaith Food Center.

All attendees will be sent more details, including the specific list of necessary food items, upon registration! We hope to see you there.
**PLEASE NOTE: We will be hosting TWO FOOD DRIVES at Michigan Park: November 15th and November 22nd (which is why you will see 2 Mobilize events.)
Thanks for joining us!
